<a id="current-amplifier"></a>**Current amplifier** — An amplifier that senses an input current and delivers an output current, modeled by its short-circuit current gain A_is with R_i and R_o; ideally R_i → 0 and R_o → ∞. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md).

<a id="current-density"></a>**Current density** — Current per unit area as a vector field, J = nqv_d (A/m²); the current through a surface is the flux of J, and J = σE in an ohmic material. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="current-divider"></a>**Current divider** — Parallel resistors sharing a current in proportion to their conductances; for two, i1 = i R2/(R1 + R2), so the smaller resistor takes the larger current. *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="current-efficiency"></a>**Current efficiency** — The fraction of a regulator's input current that reaches the load, I_L/(I_L + I_Q); it multiplies V_out/V_in in an LDO's efficiency and dominates at light load. *First defined in* [20-04](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-04-ldo-regulators.md). *See also:* [Quiescent current](#quiescent-current), [Low-dropout regulator (LDO)](#low-dropout-regulator-ldo).

<a id="current-gain"></a>**Current gain** — The common-emitter ratio β_F = I_C/I_B of a bipolar transistor, about 100 in typical devices; the common-base gain α_F = I_C/I_E = β_F/(1 + β_F) is just below 1. *First defined in* [09-07](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-07-bipolar-junction-transistor.md).

<a id="current-mirror"></a>**Current mirror** — Two or more transistors sharing a gate (base) voltage with one diode-connected, so that the others copy its current in the ratio of their sizes, independent of the threshold to first order. *First defined in* [10-02](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-02-mosfet-dc-operation-and-biasing.md). *See also:* [Diode-connected transistor](#diode-connected-transistor).

<a id="current-mirror-load"></a>**Current-mirror load** — A current mirror used as the load of a differential pair, which copies one side's signal current to the other so that both halves' currents reach a single-ended output, doubling its transconductance to g_m. *First defined in* [12-02](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-02-active-loads-cascodes-multistage.md). *See also:* [Active load](#active-load), [Five-transistor OTA](#five-transistor-ota), [Differential pair](#differential-pair).

<a id="current-mode-logic-cml"></a>**Current-mode logic (CML)** — Logic or buffering built from differential pairs that steer a constant tail current fully to one side, giving small differential swings across resistor loads, high speed and nearly constant supply current; standard in high-speed serial links. *First defined in* [12-01](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-01-differential-pairs.md). *See also:* [Differential pair](#differential-pair), [Differential signaling](#differential-signaling).

<a id="current-sense-shunt"></a>**Current-sense shunt** — A low-value resistor (milliohms) whose voltage, i R_sh, measures current; its value trades signal against I²R loss, and four-terminal parts with Kelvin layout keep copper's 0.39%/°C out of the measurement. *First defined in* [06-11](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-11-practical-dc-circuits-and-measurement.md). *See also:* [Four-terminal (Kelvin) measurement](#four-terminal-kelvin-measurement), [Burden voltage](#burden-voltage).

<a id="current-steering-dac"></a>**Current-steering DAC** — A DAC built from unit current sources that are switched between two output nodes and summed in load resistors; the architecture of nearly all DACs above about 100 MS/s. *First defined in* [20-09](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-09-dacs.md). *See also:* [Segmentation (DAC)](#segmentation-dac), [Glitch impulse](#glitch-impulse).

<a id="cursor-pulse-response"></a>**Cursor (pulse response)** — A sample h_k of a link's overall pulse response at a symbol instant; h_0 is the main cursor, k > 0 are postcursors (left by earlier symbols) and k < 0 precursors. *First defined in* [17-04](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-04-baseband-digital-transmission.md). *See also:* [Intersymbol interference](#intersymbol-interference), [Peak distortion](#peak-distortion).

<a id="curvature-compensation"></a>**Curvature compensation** — Cancelling the residual T ln T curvature of a first-order bandgap, typically by adding a scaled difference of junction voltages biased with PTAT and constant currents; its benefit is limited by how accurately the temperature exponent η of the saturation current is known. *First defined in* [20-03](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-03-bandgap-references.md). *See also:* [Bandgap reference](#bandgap-reference), [Magic voltage](#magic-voltage).

<a id="custom-asic"></a>**Custom ASIC** — An application-specific integrated circuit designed for one customer's own products or workloads, often with a design partner; the customer pays the NRE and avoids a merchant's margin. *First defined in* [26-04](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-04-engineering-economics-2.md). *See also:* [Merchant silicon](#merchant-silicon), [Design partner (ASIC services)](#design-partner-asic-services).

<a id="custom-hbm"></a>**Custom HBM** — HBM whose logic-process base die includes functions specified by the accelerator customer, such as parts of the memory controller or near-memory compute. *First defined in* [23-05](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-05-hbm-in-depth.md). *See also:* [Base die](#base-die).

<a id="cutoff-frequency"></a>**Cutoff frequency** — The frequency f_T at which a transistor's short-circuit current gain falls to 1; for a bipolar transistor 1/(2π[τ_F + (C_jE + C_jC)V_T/I_C]), rising with current until the Kirk effect sets in. *First defined in* [09-07](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-07-bipolar-junction-transistor.md).

<a id="cutoff-voltage"></a>**Cutoff voltage** — The terminal voltage at which a device or protection circuit stops discharging a cell; reaching it under load strands charge, more so at high current or low temperature. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md).

<a id="cutoff-wavelength"></a>**Cutoff wavelength** — The longest wavelength a material absorbs, λc = hc/Eg (1239.84 nm·eV divided by the band gap): 1107 nm for silicon, about 1550 nm for germanium's direct transition. *First defined in* [24-08](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-08-silicon-photonics.md). *See also:* [Band gap](#band-gap).

<a id="cyber-resilience-act-cra"></a>**Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)** — Regulation (EU) 2024/2847, which sets cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements sold in the EU, including vulnerability reporting and security updates over a support period of at least five years in most cases. *First defined in* [27-08](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-08-edge-ai-and-iot.md). *See also:* [Secure boot](#secure-boot), [Over-the-air (OTA) update](#over-the-air-ota-update).

<a id="cycle-life"></a>**Cycle life** — The number of full equivalent charge–discharge cycles a cell delivers before its capacity falls to a stated fraction (often 80%) of rated, under stated conditions. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md). *See also:* [Calendar aging](#calendar-aging).

<a id="cyclic-prefix"></a>**Cyclic prefix** — A copy of the last G samples of each OFDM symbol placed in front of it, so that a channel with up to G + 1 taps convolves the symbol circularly; it removes inter-symbol and inter-carrier interference at an overhead of G/(N + G). *First defined in* [16-03](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-03-the-dft.md). *See also:* [OFDM](#ofdm), [Circular convolution](#circular-convolution).

<a id="cyclic-redundancy-check-crc"></a>**Cyclic redundancy check (CRC)** — An error-detecting check formed as the remainder of the message polynomial divided by a generator polynomial over GF(2); a degree-r CRC catches every burst of length r or less, and Ethernet frames end in a 32-bit one. *First defined in* [08-01](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-01-number-systems-and-codes.md). *See also:* [Hamming distance](#hamming-distance).

<a id="cyclomatic-complexity"></a>**Cyclomatic complexity** — McCabe's count of linearly independent paths through a function, M = E − N + 2 for its control-flow graph, equal to the number of decision points plus one; also the number of basis-path tests. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="cyclostationary-process"></a>**Cyclostationary process** — A random process whose mean and autocorrelation repeat periodically in time, such as a PAM signal with a fixed symbol clock; adding a random timing offset uniform over one period makes it wide-sense stationary, with the period-averaged autocorrelation. *First defined in* [17-01](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-01-random-processes-and-psd.md). *See also:* [Wide-sense stationary](#wide-sense-stationary), [Spectral line](#spectral-line).

<a id="cyclotron-frequency"></a>**Cyclotron frequency** — The orbital frequency of a charge in a uniform magnetic field, f_c = |q|B/(2πm), independent of speed; 28.0 GHz per tesla for an electron. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="c-v-characteristics"></a>**C–V characteristics** — The small-signal capacitance of a MOS structure against gate voltage, C_ox in accumulation, falling through depletion, and either returning to C_ox (quasi-static, or in a transistor) or staying at C_min (high frequency) in inversion; used to extract oxide thickness, doping and oxide charge. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md). *See also:* [C–V profiling](#c-v-profiling).

<a id="c-v-profiling"></a>**C–V profiling** — Extracting doping from capacitance–voltage data, using the slope of 1/C² against voltage (which gives the doping of the lightly doped side) and its intercept (which gives the built-in potential). *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="letter-d"></a>

## D

<a id="d-flip-flop"></a>**D flip-flop** — An edge-triggered storage element whose output takes the value D had at the active clock edge and holds it until the next edge; the basic register cell of synchronous design. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md). *See also:* [Master–slave flip-flop](#master-slave-flip-flop), [Setup time](#setup-time), [Hold time](#hold-time).

<a id="d-latch"></a>**D latch** — A level-sensitive storage element that is transparent (Q follows D) while its clock or enable is active and holds its value while it is inactive. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md). *See also:* [D flip-flop](#d-flip-flop).

<a id="dadda-tree"></a>**Dadda tree** — A multiplier reduction tree that brings the partial-product columns down to target heights 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 13, ... using as few adders as possible, needing n^2 - 4n + 3 full adders for an n by n multiplier. *First defined in* [08-09](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-09-arithmetic-circuits.md). *See also:* [Carry-save adder](#carry-save-adder), [Partial product](#partial-product).

<a id="damped-natural-frequency"></a>**Damped natural frequency** — ω_d = ω₀√(1 − ζ²), the frequency at which an underdamped system actually rings. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md). *See also:* [Natural frequency](#natural-frequency).

<a id="damping-ratio"></a>**Damping ratio** — ζ = α/ω₀, the single number that classifies a second-order system: underdamped (ζ < 1, rings), critically damped (ζ = 1) or overdamped (ζ > 1); overshoot depends only on ζ. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="dark-current"></a>**Dark current** — The current an image-sensor pixel or photodiode collects with no light, mainly thermal generation through traps in depleted regions and at interfaces; it scales roughly with n_i and so grows rapidly with temperature. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="dark-silicon"></a>**Dark silicon** — The part of a power-limited chip that cannot switch at full speed at the same time as the rest, because running all of it would exceed the power or thermal budget. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="darlington-pair"></a>**Darlington pair** — Two bipolar transistors with the first one's emitter driving the second one's base, giving a current gain of about the product of the two betas at the cost of two base-emitter drops and slower turn-off; the Sziklai pair uses a complementary driver to keep a single drop. *First defined in* [12-07](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-07-output-stages.md). *See also:* [Class-AB amplifier](#class-ab-amplifier).

<a id="data-bus-inversion-dbi"></a>**Data bus inversion (DBI)** — Sending a byte inverted, flagged on an extra pin, when that reduces the number of wires at the costly level; in DDR4 a byte with more than four 0s is inverted, cutting the expected low wires per byte from 4 to 3.27 for random data. *First defined in* [23-04](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-04-dram-interfaces.md). *See also:* [Pseudo-open-drain (POD) I/O](#pseudo-open-drain-pod-i-o).

<a id="data-hazard"></a>**Data hazard** — A pipeline hazard in which an instruction needs a result that an earlier instruction has not yet written back (a read-after-write dependence). *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md). *See also:* [Forwarding (bypassing)](#forwarding-bypassing), [Load-use hazard](#load-use-hazard).

<a id="data-parallelism"></a>**Data parallelism** — Splitting training data across replicas of a model, each computing gradients on its own batch, with the gradients averaged once per step by an all-reduce; its traffic is large but infrequent, so it can cross the scale-out network. *First defined in* [27-07](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-07-ai-datacenter-server-and-rack.md). *See also:* [All-reduce](#all-reduce), [Tensor parallelism](#tensor-parallelism).

<a id="data-processing-inequality"></a>**Data-processing inequality** — For a Markov chain X → Y → Z, I(X;Z) ≤ I(X;Y): no processing of an observation creates information about the input; the reason hard decisions lose capacity. *First defined in* [17-07](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-07-information-theory-and-shannon.md). *See also:* [Mutual information](#mutual-information).

<a id="data-retention-voltage"></a>**Data-retention voltage** — The lowest supply at which an idle SRAM cell's cross-coupled inverters still hold their state; far below the voltage needed to read and write, it sets how low a sleep mode can drop the array to cut leakage. *First defined in* [23-02](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-02-sram-technology.md).

<a id="data-weighted-averaging"></a>**Data-weighted averaging** — A dynamic element matching method that selects the next D elements in rotation for each code D, so every element is used equally often and element mismatch becomes first-order noise-shaped error. *First defined in* [20-09](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-09-dacs.md). *See also:* [Dynamic element matching](#dynamic-element-matching).

<a id="dataflow-accelerator"></a>**Dataflow (accelerator)** — The choice of which operand an accelerator array keeps in place while the others move (weights, outputs or inputs), which determines the data reuse the hardware exploits. *First defined in* [14-14](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-14-ai-accelerators.md). *See also:* [Weight-stationary](#weight-stationary), [Output-stationary](#output-stationary).

<a id="dataflow-limit"></a>**Dataflow limit** — The execution time with unlimited resources and perfect prediction, set by the longest latency-weighted chain of true dependences (the critical path); no machine can be faster. *First defined in* [14-08](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-08-out-of-order-and-superscalar.md). *See also:* [Instruction-level parallelism (ILP)](#instruction-level-parallelism-ilp), [True dependence](#true-dependence).

<a id="datapath"></a>**Datapath** — The part of a processor that holds and transforms data — program counter, memories, register file, ALU, adders and multiplexers — steered by the control unit. *First defined in* [14-05](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-05-single-cycle-datapath.md). *See also:* [Control unit](#control-unit).

<a id="datapath-and-controller-fsmd"></a>**Datapath and controller (FSMD)** — The split of a design into a small FSM that sequences operations and a datapath of registers, counters and arithmetic that performs them, linked by control and status signals. *First defined in* [08-08](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-08-finite-state-machines.md). *See also:* [Finite state machine (FSM)](#finite-state-machine-fsm).

<a id="days-per-mask-layer-dpml"></a>**Days per mask layer (DPML)** — A fab productivity metric: wafer cycle time divided by the number of mask layers, typically about 1–1.5 days; cycle time is roughly mask count times DPML. *First defined in* [25-01](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-01-process-flow-overview.md). *See also:* [Wafer cycle time](#wafer-cycle-time).

<a id="dbm"></a>**dBm** — Power expressed in decibels relative to 1 mW, 10·log10(P / 1 mW); 0 dBm = 1 mW and 30 dBm = 1 W. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md). *See also:* [Decibel](#decibel).

<a id="dc-blocker"></a>**DC blocker** — The filter (1 − z^−1)/(1 − a z^−1) with a just below 1, a zero at z = 1 and a pole just inside it, which removes DC and passes frequencies above about (1 − a) rad/sample; used to strip converter offsets. *First defined in* [16-02](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-02-dtft-and-z-transform-for-dsp.md).

<a id="dc-distribution-800-v"></a>**DC distribution (800 V)** — Datacenter power distribution at 800 V (or ±400 V) DC to racks, replacing AC and 48–54 V DC to cut current, copper and conversion stages for racks approaching a megawatt. *First defined in* [22-10](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-10-datacenter-power-delivery.md).

<a id="dc-gain"></a>**DC gain** — H(0), the steady-state output per unit of constant input for a stable system; it is also the final value of the unit-step response. *First defined in* [02-05](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-05-laplace-transform-for-odes.md). *See also:* [Transfer function](#transfer-function), [Final-value theorem](#final-value-theorem).

<a id="dc-level-shifting"></a>**DC level shifting** — Moving a signal's DC level between directly coupled stages, by alternating NMOS and PMOS stages, by a source or emitter follower (a shift of V_GS or V_BE), or by a fixed drop across diodes or resistors carrying a set current. *First defined in* [12-02](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-02-active-loads-cascodes-multistage.md). *See also:* [Multistage amplifier](#multistage-amplifier), [Level shifter](#level-shifter).

<a id="dc-transformer"></a>**DC transformer** — The ideal model of a lossless switching converter, which conserves average power so that V_out = M·V_in and I_in = M·I_out, like a transformer that also works at DC. *First defined in* [22-01](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-01-power-conversion-principles.md). *See also:* [Conversion ratio](#conversion-ratio), [Switching converter](#switching-converter).

<a id="dc-bias-derating"></a>**DC-bias derating** — The loss of capacitance of class II ceramic capacitors (X5R, X7R) under applied DC voltage, because their ferroelectric dielectric's permittivity falls with field; a part can deliver a fraction of its marked value at its working voltage. *First defined in* [07-01](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-01-capacitors-and-inductors.md). *See also:* [Multilayer ceramic capacitor (MLCC)](#multilayer-ceramic-capacitor-mlcc).

<a id="ddr5-subchannel"></a>**DDR5 subchannel** — One of the two independent 32-bit halves of a DDR5 module's data bus; with BL16 each moves a 64-byte payload, keeping cache-line granularity despite the doubled burst. *First defined in* [23-04](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-04-dram-interfaces.md). *See also:* [Access granularity](#access-granularity).

<a id="de-broglie-wavelength"></a>**De Broglie wavelength** — The wavelength λ = h/p associated with a particle of momentum p; about 0.12 nm for a 100 eV electron, comparable to atomic spacings, which is why electrons diffract from crystals. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="de-moivres-theorem"></a>**De Moivre's theorem** — (r∠θ)ⁿ = rⁿ∠nθ. Raising a complex number to a power raises its magnitude to that power and multiplies its angle. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="de-morgans-theorem"></a>**De Morgan's theorem** — The complement of an OR is the AND of the complements, and the complement of an AND is the OR of the complements; to complement an expression, swap AND and OR and complement every literal. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md). *See also:* [Bubble pushing](#bubble-pushing).

<a id="de-embedding"></a>**De-embedding** — Removing the effect of a characterized fixture (board traces, package, probe pads) from a measurement, usually by inverting its transfer or ABCD matrices, to obtain a device's S-parameters at its own terminals. *First defined in* [21-01](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-01-s-parameters.md).

<a id="de-emphasis"></a>**De-emphasis** — Transmitter equalization that lowers the level of slow (repeated-symbol) patterns relative to transitions, because a peak-swing-limited FFE cannot raise the transitions; quoted in dB as 1/Σc_j, the inverse of the FFE's DC gain. *First defined in* [24-03](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-03-serdes-architecture.md). *See also:* [Feed-forward equalizer (FFE)](#feed-forward-equalizer-ffe).

<a id="dead-time"></a>**Dead time** — The short interval in which both switches of a half bridge are held off between transitions, so that they never conduct together and short the supply; the inductor current flows through a body diode meanwhile. *First defined in* [22-02](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-02-buck-converter-steady-state.md). *See also:* [Synchronous rectification](#synchronous-rectification).

<a id="deadlock"></a>**Deadlock** — Tasks waiting forever for resources held by each other, for example A holding X and waiting for Y while B holds Y and waits for X; prevented by a global lock order or the priority ceiling protocol. *First defined in* [18-07](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-07-rtos-concepts.md). *See also:* [Mutex](#mutex).

<a id="deal-grove-model"></a>**Deal–Grove model** — The linear-parabolic law x² + Ax = B(t + τ) for thermal oxidation of silicon, derived from oxidant transport, diffusion through the oxide and reaction at the Si/SiO₂ interface; linear while the oxide is thin, parabolic once diffusion limits. *First defined in* [25-01](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-01-process-flow-overview.md).

<a id="debug-probe"></a>**Debug probe** — Hardware that connects a host to a microcontroller's debug port (SWD with two pins on Cortex-M, or JTAG), letting a debugger halt the core, read and write memory, set breakpoints and program flash. *First defined in* [18-02](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-02-bare-metal-c-and-toolchain.md). *See also:* [Semihosting](#semihosting).

<a id="debye-length"></a>**Debye length** — The screening length L_D = √(εkT/(q²N)) over which mobile carriers smooth out a charge disturbance; 41 nm at 10¹⁶ cm⁻³ in silicon, and the scale of the soft edges of a depletion region. *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="decibel"></a>**Decibel** — A logarithmic ratio, 10·log10 of a power ratio (or 20·log10 of an amplitude ratio for equal impedances); 3 dB ≈ 2× power, 10 dB = 10× power. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="decimation"></a>**Decimation** — Keeping every M-th sample of a sequence, y[n] = x[Mn]; it discards samples, so unlike continuous-time compression it can lose information, and its effect on energy depends on which samples are kept. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md). *See also:* [Zero-insertion interpolation](#zero-insertion-interpolation).

<a id="decimation-in-frequency"></a>**Decimation in frequency** — The FFT split into even- and odd-indexed output bins (input split into halves), giving natural input order, bit-reversed output order, and butterflies that multiply the difference by the twiddle. *First defined in* [16-04](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-04-the-fft.md). *See also:* [Decimation in time](#decimation-in-time).

<a id="decimation-in-time"></a>**Decimation in time** — The FFT split into even- and odd-indexed input samples, giving bit-reversed input order, natural output order, and butterflies that multiply by the twiddle before the add and subtract. *First defined in* [16-04](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-04-the-fft.md). *See also:* [Decimation in frequency](#decimation-in-frequency), [Bit-reversed order](#bit-reversed-order).

<a id="decision-region"></a>**Decision region** — The set of received points mapped to one symbol; for ML detection in AWGN, the Voronoi cell of the constellation point, bounded by perpendicular bisectors to its neighbours. *First defined in* [17-05](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-05-matched-filters-and-detection.md). *See also:* [Maximum-likelihood detection](#maximum-likelihood-detection).

<a id="decision-tree"></a>**Decision tree** — A diagram of decisions, chance events with probabilities, and outcomes, solved backward by taking expected values at chance nodes and the best branch at decision nodes. *First defined in* [26-04](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-04-engineering-economics-2.md).

<a id="decision-feedback-equalizer-dfe"></a>**Decision-feedback equalizer (DFE)** — A receiver equalizer that subtracts the interference of earlier symbols computed from its own past decisions; one wrong decision can then cause a burst of errors, which transmitter precoding limits to about two bit errors. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="decode-and-prefill"></a>**Decode and prefill** — The two phases of language-model inference: prefill processes the whole prompt at once and is compute-bound, while decode generates one token per step, reading all weights and the KV cache each time, and is memory-bound. *First defined in* [23-01](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-01-memory-hierarchy-and-memory-wall.md). *See also:* [KV cache](#kv-cache), [Arithmetic intensity](#arithmetic-intensity).

<a id="decoder"></a>**Decoder** — A block with n inputs and 2^n outputs, exactly one of which is 1 (the minterm of the inputs); with an enable input it is also a demultiplexer, and it selects rows in memories and decodes instructions. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md).

<a id="decoupling-capacitor"></a>**Decoupling capacitor** — A capacitor placed close to a load to supply its fast current changes until the regulator responds, limiting the droop to ΔI·Δt/C and the spike to L·di/dt; its effectiveness at high frequency is limited by inductance more than by capacitance. *First defined in* [07-01](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-01-capacitors-and-inductors.md). *See also:* [Equivalent series inductance (ESL)](#equivalent-series-inductance-esl).

<a id="deep-depletion"></a>**Deep depletion** — The non-equilibrium state of a MOS capacitor swept into inversion faster than thermal generation can supply minority carriers, so the depletion region grows beyond its equilibrium maximum; CCD pixels collect photo-electrons in this state. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="defect-density-d0"></a>**Defect density (D0)** — The average number of killer defects per unit area (usually per cm²) on a wafer; with die area A it sets the expected defects per die, A·D₀. *First defined in* [25-04](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-04-yield-and-die-cost.md). *See also:* [Poisson yield model](#poisson-yield-model), [Negative-binomial yield model](#negative-binomial-yield-model).

<a id="defect-level-dppm"></a>**Defect level (DPPM)** — The fraction of shipped (test-passing) parts that are defective, usually in defective parts per million; the Williams–Brown model gives DL = 1 − Y^(1−T). *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="defective-matrix"></a>**Defective matrix** — A square matrix with fewer independent eigenvectors than its size (a repeated eigenvalue short of eigenvectors); it cannot be diagonalized, and its powers and exponentials contain extra factors k or t. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="definite-integral"></a>**Definite integral** — The limit of Riemann sums ∫_a^b f(x) dx, equal to the signed area under f; its units are those of f times those of x. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="degenerate-semiconductor"></a>**Degenerate semiconductor** — A semiconductor so heavily doped that its Fermi level lies within a few kT of a band edge or inside a band, so that Boltzmann statistics fail and the Fermi–Dirac integral is needed; silicon becomes degenerate above roughly 10¹⁸–10¹⁹ cm⁻³. *First defined in* [09-02](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-02-carriers-doping-fermi-level.md). *See also:* [Fermi–Dirac integral](#fermi-dirac-integral), [Band-gap narrowing](#band-gap-narrowing).

<a id="delay-margin"></a>**Delay margin** — The largest extra time delay a stable loop tolerates before it oscillates, PM (in radians) divided by the gain crossover frequency; a delay adds phase lag ωT without changing the magnitude. *First defined in* [15-07](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-07-frequency-domain-design.md). *See also:* [Phase margin](#phase-margin).

<a id="delta-connection"></a>**Delta connection** — Three-phase sources or loads connected end to end in a loop, each element between two lines; no neutral. A balanced Δ of Z_Δ is equivalent to a Y of Z_Δ/3. *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md).

<a id="delta-update"></a>**Delta update** — An update that sends only the difference between the installed and the new image; the device rebuilds the new image locally, saving airtime and energy at the cost of working space and server-side patch management. *First defined in* [18-08](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-08-boot-and-firmware-update.md). *See also:* [Over-the-air (OTA) update](#over-the-air-ota-update).

<a id="delta-sigma-modulator"></a>**Delta-sigma modulator** — A feedback loop of integrators, a coarse quantizer and a DAC, run far above the Nyquist rate, whose output averages to its input while its quantization noise is shaped away from the signal band; followed by a decimation filter it forms a delta-sigma (sigma-delta) ADC. *First defined in* [20-08](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-08-sigma-delta-converters.md). *See also:* [Noise shaping](#noise-shaping), [Noise transfer function (NTF)](#noise-transfer-function-ntf), [Oversampling](#oversampling).

<a id="delta-wye-transformation"></a>**Delta–wye transformation** — Replacing three resistors in a triangle (delta) by three meeting at a node (wye), or the reverse, with equal behaviour at the three terminals; R_a = R_ab R_ca/(R_ab + R_bc + R_ca). *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="demand-paging"></a>**Demand paging** — Mapping a page only when it is first accessed, by servicing the resulting page fault, so that memory is allocated or loaded lazily. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Page fault](#page-fault), [Thrashing](#thrashing).

<a id="density-of-states"></a>**Density of states** — The number of electron states per unit energy (and per unit volume), g(E) ∝ √E for free electrons; multiplied by the occupation f(E) it gives how many electrons sit at each energy. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="density-of-states-effective-mass"></a>**Density-of-states effective mass** — The mass of a single spherical band that would hold as many states as the real, possibly anisotropic and multi-valley, band; for silicon electrons m_dn = 6^(2/3)(m_l m_t²)^(1/3), about 1.08 m0 at the band edge. It sets N_C and N_V. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md). *See also:* [Conductivity effective mass](#conductivity-effective-mass).

<a id="departure-angle"></a>**Departure angle** — The angle at which a root-locus branch leaves a complex open-loop pole, 180° minus the angles from the other poles plus the angles from the zeros; the analogous arrival angle applies at a complex zero. *First defined in* [15-06](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-06-root-locus.md). *See also:* [Root locus](#root-locus).

<a id="dependent-source"></a>**Dependent source** — An ideal voltage or current source whose value is a fixed multiple of a voltage or current elsewhere in the circuit (VCVS, VCCS, CCVS, CCCS); it models gain in transistors and amplifiers and stays in place when independent sources are turned off. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [VCVS](#vcvs), [VCCS](#vccs), [CCVS](#ccvs), [CCCS](#cccs), [Small-signal model](#small-signal-model).

<a id="depletion-approximation"></a>**Depletion approximation** — The model of a junction's space-charge region as completely empty of carriers between sharp edges and exactly neutral outside, which turns Poisson's equation into simple integrals; accurate to a few percent except near flat band. *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="depletion-region"></a>**Depletion region** — The layer around a pn junction stripped of mobile carriers, leaving fixed ionized dopants (−qN_A on the p side, +qN_D on the n side); Gauss's law gives its triangular field, peaking at the junction. *First defined in* [04-03](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-03-gauss-law.md).

<a id="depth-of-focus-dof"></a>**Depth of focus (DOF)** — The range of defocus over which an image prints acceptably; it scales as λ/NA², so it shrinks faster than resolution improves as NA rises. *First defined in* [25-02](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-02-lithography.md).

<a id="depthwise-separable-convolution"></a>**Depthwise-separable convolution** — A convolution factored into a per-channel k × k spatial filter and a 1 × 1 pointwise convolution that mixes channels, cutting MACs and weights to 1/C_out + 1/k² of a standard convolution. *First defined in* [27-08](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-08-edge-ai-and-iot.md). *See also:* [TinyML](#tinyml).

<a id="dereference"></a>**Dereference** — To access the object a pointer points to (\*p in C, or p->field for a struct); dereferencing an invalid or null pointer is undefined behavior. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="derivative"></a>**Derivative** — The instantaneous rate of change f'(a) = lim_{h→0} (f(a + h) − f(a))/h, the slope of the tangent line; its units are the output's units per input unit. *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md). *See also:* [Difference quotient](#difference-quotient), [Differentiable](#differentiable).

<a id="derivative-kick"></a>**Derivative kick** — The large, brief controller output produced when the derivative term acts on the error and the setpoint steps; it is avoided by taking the derivative of the measurement only and is bounded by the derivative filter at K_p(1 + N). *First defined in* [15-08](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-08-pid-control.md). *See also:* [Setpoint weighting](#setpoint-weighting).

<a id="describing-function"></a>**Describing function** — The effective gain of a memoryless nonlinearity for a sinusoidal input, the fundamental of its output divided by the input amplitude; an oscillator's amplitude settles where the describing-function loop gain equals one. *First defined in* [12-09](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-09-oscillators.md). *See also:* [Barkhausen criterion](#barkhausen-criterion).

<a id="desense"></a>**Desense** — Loss of a receiver's sensitivity caused by the same device's own transmitter, through transmit noise, harmonics or intermodulation landing in the receive channel; an interferer inside the receive filter's pass band can only be removed before it reaches the shared antenna path. *First defined in* [21-09](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-09-rf-front-end.md). *See also:* [Carrier aggregation](#carrier-aggregation), [Duplexer](#duplexer).

<a id="desensitivity-factor"></a>**Desensitivity factor** — The factor 1 + T by which negative feedback divides the fractional sensitivity of the closed-loop gain to the forward gain, dA_f/A_f = (dA/A)/(1 + T); the feedback network's own errors are not divided. *First defined in* [12-05](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-05-feedback-topologies.md). *See also:* [Loop gain](#loop-gain), [Negative feedback](#negative-feedback).

<a id="desensitization"></a>**Desensitization** — Loss of a receiver's ability to detect weak signals in the presence of a strong blocker, through gain compression of the wanted signal, reciprocal mixing or added noise; a blocker compresses a weak signal's gain by 1 dB at a power 3 dB below the amplifier's own 1 dB compression point. *First defined in* [21-03](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-03-noise-figure-and-linearity.md). *See also:* [Reciprocal mixing](#reciprocal-mixing), [P1dB (1 dB compression point)](#p1db-1-db-compression-point).

<a id="design-for-test-dft"></a>**Design for test (DFT)** — Design features (scan chains, built-in self-test, test access) that make manufactured chips testable for defects at low cost. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="design-margin"></a>**Design margin** — The part of a budget deliberately held back (as reserve or contingency) to absorb optimistic estimates and late discoveries; it is tracked and released by the budget's owner rather than spent silently. *First defined in* [26-01](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-01-requirements-and-specifications.md). *See also:* [Requirement flow-down](#requirement-flow-down).

<a id="design-partner-asic-services"></a>**Design partner (ASIC services)** — A company that turns a customer's specification or RTL into a manufactured chip, supplying interface IP, physical design, packaging, test and supply-chain management, and sells the chips at a margin. *First defined in* [26-04](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-04-engineering-economics-2.md).

<a id="design-rules"></a>**Design rules** — A foundry's geometric constraints on layout (minimum widths and spacings, enclosures and extensions, density and context-dependent rules) that ensure what is drawn can be manufactured reliably; textbooks use scalable rules in units of λ, real processes absolute rules. *First defined in* [19-09](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-09-layout-and-standard-cells.md). *See also:* [Design-rule check (DRC)](#design-rule-check-drc).

<a id="design-under-test-dut"></a>**Design under test (DUT)** — The design instantiated inside a testbench, whose outputs are driven, observed and checked against a reference model. *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md). *See also:* [Testbench](#testbench).

<a id="design-verification"></a>**Design verification** — The engineering function (and activity) of demonstrating, before tapeout, that a design's RTL implements its specification, using simulation, coverage, formal methods and emulation. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="design-rule-check-drc"></a>**Design-rule check (DRC)** — Automated verification that every polygon of a layout obeys the foundry's design rules; a required signoff step before masks are made. *First defined in* [19-09](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-09-layout-and-standard-cells.md). *See also:* [Design rules](#design-rules), [Layout versus schematic (LVS)](#layout-versus-schematic-lvs).

<a id="detector-error-ratio-der"></a>**Detector error ratio (DER)** — The error ratio of a receiver's symbol decisions before FEC, used by IEEE 802.3 instead of a bit error ratio because equalizer error propagation and precoding make errors bursty; 802.3dj budgets DER₀ = 2e-4 for 200 Gb/s-per-lane backplane and copper-cable links. *First defined in* [24-02](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-02-eye-diagrams-jitter-ber.md). *See also:* [Forward error correction (FEC)](#forward-error-correction-fec).

<a id="determinant"></a>**Determinant** — The number det A attached to a square matrix, fixed by three rules (det I = 1, a row exchange flips the sign, linearity in each row); it equals ± the product of the pivots, is zero exactly when A is singular, and |det A| is the volume scale factor of the map x → Ax. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md). *See also:* [Cofactor](#cofactor), [Inverse matrix](#inverse-matrix).

<a id="deterministic-jitter-dj"></a>**Deterministic jitter (DJ)** — The bounded part of jitter: data-dependent jitter from ISI and duty-cycle distortion, periodic jitter and bounded uncorrelated jitter from crosstalk; worst cases add linearly, and DJ(δδ) is its dual-Dirac fit, which can be smaller than its peak-to-peak value. *First defined in* [24-02](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-02-eye-diagrams-jitter-ber.md). *See also:* [Random jitter (RJ)](#random-jitter-rj), [Dual-Dirac model](#dual-dirac-model).

<a id="device-firmware-update-dfu"></a>**Device firmware update (DFU)** — Updating a device's firmware over a wired or local link (UART, USB, a ROM bootloader's protocol); also the name of the USB class for it. *First defined in* [18-08](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-08-boot-and-firmware-update.md). *See also:* [Over-the-air (OTA) update](#over-the-air-ota-update).

<a id="dft-bin"></a>**DFT bin** — One of the N frequencies 2πk/N (k f_s/N in hertz) at which the DFT samples the DTFT; bins above N/2 are negative frequencies, and the bin spacing f_s/N is the reciprocal of the record length. *First defined in* [16-03](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-03-the-dft.md). *See also:* [Discrete Fourier transform (DFT)](#discrete-fourier-transform-dft).

<a id="dft-spread-ofdm"></a>**DFT-spread OFDM** — OFDM in which each block of data symbols is DFT-precoded before subcarrier mapping, giving a nearly single-carrier waveform with several decibels lower PAPR; NR's uplink "transform precoding" (also called SC-FDMA). *First defined in* [17-10](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-10-ofdm.md). *See also:* [Peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR)](#peak-to-average-power-ratio-papr), [OFDM](#ofdm).

<a id="diagnostic-coverage"></a>**Diagnostic coverage** — The fraction of an element's dangerous failure rate that a safety mechanism detects in the field; the remainder is the residual-fault rate. It is not the same as manufacturing test coverage. *First defined in* [25-10](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-10-qualification-and-functional-safety.md). *See also:* [FMEDA](#fmeda).

<a id="diagonalization"></a>**Diagonalization** — Writing A = XΛX⁻¹ with eigenvectors in X and eigenvalues in Λ, possible when A has n independent eigenvectors; it gives powers as Aᵏ = XΛᵏX⁻¹. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="diagonally-dominant-matrix"></a>**Diagonally dominant matrix** — A matrix in which each diagonal entry is at least the sum of the magnitudes of the other entries in its row; a nodal conductance matrix is, with strict inequality at nodes that have conductance to ground. *First defined in* [06-04](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-04-nodal-analysis.md). *See also:* [Conductance matrix](#conductance-matrix), [Positive definite matrix](#positive-definite-matrix).

<a id="diamond-structure"></a>**Diamond structure** — The crystal structure of Si, Ge and diamond, a face-centered cubic lattice with a two-atom basis offset by (a/4)(1,1,1), giving 8 atoms per cubic cell and four tetrahedral bonds per atom. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md). *See also:* [Crystal lattice](#crystal-lattice), [Zinc blende](#zinc-blende).

<a id="die-to-die-interface"></a>**Die-to-die interface** — A link between dies in one package, run wide and slow over a short, nearly lossless channel with a forwarded clock and no equalization, judged by energy per bit (tenths of a picojoule or less) and bandwidth per millimetre of die edge. *First defined in* [24-06](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-06-d2d-memory-phys-scale-up.md). *See also:* [Chiplet](#chiplet), [UCIe](#ucie), [Bunch of Wires (BoW)](#bunch-of-wires-bow).

<a id="die-to-wafer-bonding"></a>**Die-to-wafer bonding** — Placing individual tested dies onto a target wafer and bonding them; it allows known-good-die selection and different die sizes but has coarser placement accuracy than wafer-to-wafer bonding. *First defined in* [25-07](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-07-advanced-packaging-and-chiplets.md). *See also:* [Wafer-to-wafer bonding](#wafer-to-wafer-bonding), [Known-good die (KGD)](#known-good-die-kgd).

<a id="dielectric"></a>**Dielectric** — An insulator that polarizes in an electric field, reducing the field of a given free charge by its relative permittivity ε_r and raising a capacitor's capacitance by the same factor. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md). *See also:* [Relative permittivity](#relative-permittivity).

<a id="dielectric-breakdown"></a>**Dielectric breakdown** — The sudden failure of an insulator when the field is strong enough to tear electrons loose and start an avalanche; about 3 MV/m in air and above 10 MV/cm in thermal SiO₂. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="dies-per-wafer"></a>**Dies per wafer** — The number of whole dies that fit on a round wafer, approximated by πd²/(4A) − πd/√(2A); the subtracted edge-loss term grows in relative size as dies get larger. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="difference-equation"></a>**Difference equation** — A recursion relating a sequence's present and past values, y[n] + a₁y[n − 1] + … + a_N y[n − N] = b₀x[n] + … + b_M x[n − M]; with constant coefficients and initial rest it defines a causal LTI system, the discrete-time counterpart of a linear ODE. *First defined in* [11-04](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-04-lti-systems-and-differential-equations.md). *See also:* [IIR filter](#iir-filter), [Characteristic equation](#characteristic-equation).

<a id="difference-quotient"></a>**Difference quotient** — The slope (f(a + h) − f(a))/h of the secant line through two nearby points; its limit as h → 0 is the derivative. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="differentiable"></a>**Differentiable** — Having a derivative at a point; differentiability implies continuity, but not conversely (|x| is continuous with a corner at 0). *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="differential-conductance-pair"></a>**Differential conductance pair** — Storing a signed weight as two conductances G⁺ and G⁻ in two columns and taking the current difference, so offsets common to both cancel. *First defined in* [23-09](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-09-compute-in-memory.md). *See also:* [Analog crossbar](#analog-crossbar).

<a id="differential-entropy"></a>**Differential entropy** — The continuous counterpart of entropy, h(X) = −∫ f log2 f dx; a Gaussian of variance σ² has ½ log2(2πeσ²), the most of any density with that variance. *First defined in* [17-07](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-07-information-theory-and-shannon.md). *See also:* [Entropy (information)](#entropy-information), [Shannon–Hartley theorem](#shannon-hartley-theorem).

<a id="differential-nonlinearity-dnl"></a>**Differential nonlinearity (DNL)** — For a data converter, the deviation of each code step from the ideal 1 LSB, in LSBs; it is largest where many bits switch at once, such as the major carry. *First defined in* [06-07](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-07-linearity-and-superposition.md). *See also:* [Superposition](#superposition).

<a id="differential-pair"></a>**Differential pair** — Two matched transistors whose emitters or sources share a tail current source, so that the tail fixes their total current and the input difference decides how it splits; the input stage of op-amps, comparators and CML buffers. *First defined in* [12-01](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-01-differential-pairs.md). *See also:* [Tail current source](#tail-current-source), [Half-circuit](#half-circuit), [Common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR)](#common-mode-rejection-ratio-cmrr).

<a id="differential-signaling"></a>**Differential signaling** — Sending a signal as equal and opposite voltages on two wires and receiving their difference, which doubles the signal and cancels interference common to both wires. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="differential-mode-gain"></a>**Differential-mode gain** — The gain from the difference of a differential stage's two inputs to its output, g_mR_D for a resistor-loaded pair with a differential output and half that for one output. *First defined in* [12-01](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-01-differential-pairs.md). *See also:* [Common-mode gain](#common-mode-gain), [Differential pair](#differential-pair).

<a id="differentiator-op-amp"></a>**Differentiator (op-amp)** — An op-amp circuit with a capacitor at the input and a resistor in the feedback path, giving v_out = −RC dv_in/dt; a resistor in series with the capacitor caps its gain for fast changes, turning a step's impulse into a finite exponential spike. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="diffraction"></a>**Diffraction** — The spreading of a wave through an aperture or around an edge by about λ/aperture radians; a slit's first zero is at sin θ = λ/a, a circular aperture's at 1.22λ/D. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="diffusion"></a>**Diffusion** — The net flow of carriers from regions of high to low concentration caused by random thermal motion alone, with flux −D dn/dx (Fick's law); the carrier spread grows as √(Dt). *First defined in* [09-03](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-03-drift-and-diffusion.md). *See also:* [Diffusion coefficient](#diffusion-coefficient), [Fick's law](#ficks-law).

<a id="diffusion-capacitance"></a>**Diffusion capacitance** — The small-signal capacitance from minority charge stored in a forward-biased diode, proportional to bias current; τ_p g_d/2 for a long diode and W²g_d/(3D) for a short one, usually far larger than the junction capacitance in forward bias. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md). *See also:* [Junction capacitance](#junction-capacitance).

<a id="diffusion-coefficient"></a>**Diffusion coefficient** — The constant D linking diffusion flux to concentration gradient (cm²/s); for silicon at 300 K about 35 cm²/s for electrons and 12 cm²/s for holes in lightly doped material, related to mobility by D = (kT/q)μ. *First defined in* [09-03](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-03-drift-and-diffusion.md). *See also:* [Einstein relation](#einstein-relation).

<a id="diffusion-length"></a>**Diffusion length** — The average distance a minority carrier diffuses before recombining, L = √(Dτ); regions much shorter than L transport carriers with little recombination, those much longer absorb them. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="digital-downconverter-ddc"></a>**Digital downconverter (DDC)** — A digital block that multiplies a sampled signal by a numerically controlled oscillator, low-pass filters and decimates, selecting one channel and gaining 10 log(f_s/2B) of processing gain. *First defined in* [21-08](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-08-transceiver-architectures.md). *See also:* [Processing gain](#processing-gain), [Direct RF sampling](#direct-rf-sampling).

<a id="digital-in-memory-computing"></a>**Digital in-memory computing** — Compute-in-memory that sums bitcell-gated partial products with digital adders next to SRAM arrays; exact and free of ADCs, but with less energy advantage than analog schemes. *First defined in* [23-09](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-09-compute-in-memory.md). *See also:* [Compute-in-memory (CIM)](#compute-in-memory-cim).

<a id="digital-ldo"></a>**Digital LDO** — A linear regulator whose error amplifier is replaced by a clocked comparator and controller that switches an array of unit pass transistors on or off; it works at supplies too low for analog amplifiers and scales with digital processes, at the cost of limit-cycle ripple, quantized response and weak high-frequency supply rejection. *First defined in* [20-04](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-04-ldo-regulators.md). *See also:* [Low-dropout regulator (LDO)](#low-dropout-regulator-ldo), [Capacitor-less LDO](#capacitor-less-ldo).

<a id="digital-multiphase-controller"></a>**Digital multiphase controller** — A controller IC that samples the output and phase currents digitally and computes the duty cycles of many interleaved phases, with programmable compensation, phase shedding and telemetry over PMBus or similar buses. *First defined in* [22-07](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-07-converter-dynamics-and-control.md).

<a id="digital-predistortion-dpd"></a>**Digital predistortion (DPD)** — Distorting the transmit signal in baseband with an approximate inverse of the power amplifier's nonlinearity, learned from an observation receiver, so the cascade is linear; it cannot extend the output beyond saturation. *First defined in* [21-07](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-07-power-amplifiers.md). *See also:* [Crest-factor reduction (CFR)](#crest-factor-reduction-cfr), [AM-PM conversion](#am-pm-conversion).

<a id="digital-resonator"></a>**Digital resonator** — A second-order recursive filter with poles at r e^{±jω0} near the unit circle (often with zeros at z = ±1), whose response peaks at ω0 with gain about 1/(1 − r), −3 dB width about 2(1 − r) rad/sample and Q about ω0/[2(1 − r)]; it rings for about 1/(1 − r) samples. *First defined in* [16-02](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-02-dtft-and-z-transform-for-dsp.md). *See also:* [Notch filter](#notch-filter), [Poles and zeros](#poles-and-zeros).

<a id="digital-signal"></a>**Digital signal** — A signal that is discrete in time and takes values from a finite set, such as ADC output codes; quantization makes it digital, sampling only makes it discrete-time, and it need not be binary. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md). *See also:* [Quantization noise](#quantization-noise), [PAM4](#pam4).

<a id="digitally-assisted-analog"></a>**Digitally assisted analog** — A design approach that builds deliberately imprecise analog circuits and removes their errors with digital estimation and correction, trading analog gain and matching for cheap logic. *First defined in* [20-12](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-12-why-analog-does-not-scale.md). *See also:* [Background calibration](#background-calibration), [Dynamic element matching](#dynamic-element-matching).

<a id="dijkstras-algorithm"></a>**Dijkstra's algorithm** — The shortest-path algorithm of link-state routing, finalizing nodes in order of distance from the source; it requires non-negative link costs. *First defined in* [17-13](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-13-computer-networks-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Bellman–Ford algorithm](#bellman-ford-algorithm).

<a id="dimension"></a>**Dimension** — The number of vectors in any basis of a subspace (all bases have the same number). *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="dimensional-analysis"></a>**Dimensional analysis** — Checking that every term of an equation has the same physical units (and that arguments of exp, log and trig functions are dimensionless) to catch errors and derive relationships. *First defined in* [00-03](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-03-how-to-study-this-curriculum.md).

<a id="diode-connected-transistor"></a>**Diode-connected transistor** — A transistor with its gate tied to its drain (or base to collector), which is always saturated (active) and behaves as a two-terminal device whose voltage sets itself to carry the current fed to it; the input half of a current mirror. *First defined in* [10-02](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-02-mosfet-dc-operation-and-biasing.md).

<a id="direct-band-gap"></a>**Direct band gap** — A band gap whose conduction-band minimum lies at the same crystal momentum as the valence-band maximum (GaAs, GaN), so electrons and holes recombine by emitting light efficiently; indirect gaps (Si, Ge, SiC) need a phonon. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="direct-charging"></a>**Direct charging** — Fast charging in which the adapter itself regulates the battery current (for example through USB PD PPS) and the phone uses a switched-capacitor divider instead of an inductive charger. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md). *See also:* [Programmable Power Supply (PPS)](#programmable-power-supply-pps).

<a id="direct-form-i-and-ii"></a>**Direct form I and II** — Block-diagram realizations of a difference equation; direct form I uses separate delay lines for input and output (2N delays for order N), direct form II runs the recursive part first so one line serves both (N delays, canonical); transposed direct form II rearranges it for better floating-point behavior. *First defined in* [11-04](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-04-lti-systems-and-differential-equations.md). *See also:* [Biquad](#biquad).

<a id="direct-memory-access-dma"></a>**Direct memory access (DMA)** — Data transfer between a device and memory performed by a DMA engine acting as a bus manager, following descriptors set up by software and interrupting on completion, so the CPU need not move the data itself. *First defined in* [14-11](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-11-io-buses-and-interconnect.md). *See also:* [Interrupt](#interrupt).

<a id="direct-rf-sampling"></a>**Direct RF sampling** — Digitizing the RF band directly with a gigasample ADC (or synthesizing it with an RF DAC) and doing frequency translation and channel filtering digitally; limited by converter jitter, noise figure, linearity and power. *First defined in* [21-08](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-08-transceiver-architectures.md). *See also:* [Nyquist zone](#nyquist-zone), [Aperture jitter](#aperture-jitter), [Digital downconverter (DDC)](#digital-downconverter-ddc).

<a id="direct-time-of-flight"></a>**Direct time-of-flight** — Ranging by timing the round trip of a light pulse to a target, d = ct/2 (dToF); timing jitter Δt sets the depth resolution cΔt/2. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="direct-conversion-zero-if-receiver"></a>**Direct-conversion (zero-IF) receiver** — A receiver whose quadrature mixers convert the channel straight to baseband; it needs no image filter, but I/Q mismatch, DC offsets, flicker noise and second-order distortion fall on the signal and must be calibrated. *First defined in* [21-08](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-08-transceiver-architectures.md). *See also:* [Low-IF receiver](#low-if-receiver), [Image-rejection ratio (IRR)](#image-rejection-ratio-irr).

<a id="direct-mapped-cache"></a>**Direct-mapped cache** — A cache in which each memory block can be placed in exactly one line, chosen by the index bits of its address; simple and fast but prone to conflict misses. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Set-associative cache](#set-associative-cache).

<a id="direction-field"></a>**Direction field** — A plot of short segments with slope f(t, y) at a grid of points for y' = f(t, y); solutions run tangent to the segments, so the field shows their behavior before any algebra. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="directional-derivative"></a>**Directional derivative** — The rate of change of f along a unit vector u, D_u f = ∇f · u. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="directivity"></a>**Directivity** — The ratio of an antenna's maximum radiation intensity to the average over all directions, D = 4πU_max/P_rad; 1.5 for a Hertzian dipole, 1.64 (2.15 dBi) for a half-wave dipole. *First defined in* [13-11](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-11-radiation-and-antennas.md). *See also:* [Antenna gain](#antenna-gain), [Radiation pattern](#radiation-pattern).

<a id="directory-protocol"></a>**Directory protocol** — Cache coherence in which a directory at each block's home node records which caches hold the block, so requests and invalidations go only to those caches; scales to many cores at the cost of directory storage and extra hops. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Snooping](#snooping).

<a id="dirichlet-kernel"></a>**Dirichlet kernel** — The DTFT of a length-N rectangular sequence, e^{−jω(N−1)/2} sin(Nω/2)/sin(ω/2): a main lobe of null-to-null width 4π/N with sidelobes about 13 dB down; it is what truncation convolves every spectrum with. *First defined in* [11-07](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-07-discrete-time-fourier-transform.md). *See also:* [Window function](#window-function).

<a id="discontinuous-conduction-mode-dcm"></a>**Discontinuous conduction mode (DCM)** — Operation in which the inductor current falls to zero and stays there for part of each cycle, because a diode or diode-emulating switch blocks reverse current; the conversion ratio then depends on the load, M = 2/(1 + √(1 + 4K/D²)) for a buck with K = 2L/(R·T_s). *First defined in* [22-02](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-02-buck-converter-steady-state.md). *See also:* [Continuous conduction mode (CCM)](#continuous-conduction-mode-ccm), [Pulse-frequency modulation (PFM)](#pulse-frequency-modulation-pfm).

<a id="discontinuous-reception-drx"></a>**Discontinuous reception (DRX)** — A cellular idle-mode scheme in which the device sleeps between scheduled paging occasions one DRX cycle apart; extended DRX (eDRX) stretches the cycle to tens of seconds or more, trading reachability for energy. *First defined in* [27-03](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-03-wearables-smartwatch.md). *See also:* [Duty cycling](#duty-cycling).

<a id="discount-factor"></a>**Discount factor** — D(t) = exp(−∫ r dt), the present value of one unit due at time t; it is exactly the integrating factor of the balance equation B' − r(t)B = deposits. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md). *See also:* [Integrating factor](#integrating-factor).

<a id="discounted-unit-stream"></a>**Discounted unit stream** — U = Σ V_t/(1 + i)^t, the number of year-0 units equivalent to a shipment plan; any per-unit charge r has present value rU. *First defined in* [26-04](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-04-engineering-economics-2.md).

<a id="discrete-fourier-transform-dft"></a>**Discrete Fourier transform (DFT)** — X[k] = Σ_{n=0}^{N−1} x[n] e^{−j2πkn/N}: N equally spaced samples of the DTFT of a length-N sequence, computed in N log N operations by the FFT. *First defined in* [11-07](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-07-discrete-time-fourier-transform.md). *See also:* [Discrete-time Fourier transform (DTFT)](#discrete-time-fourier-transform-dtft), [Zero-padding](#zero-padding).

<a id="discrete-time-fourier-transform-dtft"></a>**Discrete-time Fourier transform (DTFT)** — X(e^{jω}) = Σ x[n] e^{−jωn}, with inverse x[n] = (1/2π)∫ over one period of X(e^{jω}) e^{jωn} dω: the spectrum of a sequence, a continuous function of ω that is periodic with period 2π. *First defined in* [11-07](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-07-discrete-time-fourier-transform.md). *See also:* [Fourier transform](#fourier-transform), [Discrete-time frequency](#discrete-time-frequency).

<a id="discrete-time-frequency"></a>**Discrete-time frequency** — The frequency ω of a sequence e^{jωn} or cos(ωn), in rad/sample; it is defined only modulo 2π, so ω and ω + 2π give the same sequence and the fastest oscillation is at ω = π. Sampling a tone of f hertz at f_s gives ω = 2πf/f_s. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md).

<a id="discrete-time-signal"></a>**Discrete-time signal** — A sequence x[n] defined only at integer indices n, often the samples x(nT_s) of a continuous-time signal; it is undefined, not zero, between samples. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md). *See also:* [Continuous-time signal](#continuous-time-signal), [Sampling rate](#sampling-rate).

<a id="discrimination-filter-specification"></a>**Discrimination (filter specification)** — D = (10^(As/10) − 1)/(10^(Ap/10) − 1), the ratio by which a low-pass filter must separate its power gains at the passband and stopband edges; every classical order formula is a function of D and the edge ratio. *First defined in* [16-07](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-07-iir-filter-design.md). *See also:* [Passband ripple](#passband-ripple), [Stopband attenuation](#stopband-attenuation).

<a id="dishing-and-erosion"></a>**Dishing and erosion** — CMP defects that depend on pattern density: dishing recesses wide soft-metal lines below the dielectric, erosion thins the dielectric in dense line arrays. *First defined in* [25-03](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-03-deposition-etch-cmp-implant-metrology.md).

<a id="displacement-current"></a>**Displacement current** — The term ε₀ dΦ_E/dt that Maxwell added to Ampère's law; a changing electric field makes a magnetic field as a current does, so a charging capacitor's gap carries a displacement current equal to its lead current. *First defined in* [04-08](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-08-maxwell-preview.md).

<a id="dissipation-factor"></a>**Dissipation factor** — D = tan δ = R/|X| = 1/Q, the ratio of a component's loss to its reactance at a stated frequency; for a capacitor with series resistance, D = ωC·ESR. Capacitor datasheets quote it at a test frequency such as 120 Hz or 1 kHz. *First defined in* [07-05](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-05-sinusoidal-steady-state-and-impedance.md).

<a id="distance-from-neutral-point-dnp"></a>**Distance from neutral point (DNP)** — The distance of a solder joint from the point of zero relative thermal displacement, usually the die centre; joint shear strain grows in proportion to it, so the corner joints fail first. *First defined in* [25-06](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-06-packaging-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Coffin–Manson relation](#coffin-manson-relation).

<a id="distortionless-line"></a>**Distortionless line** — A transmission line satisfying Heaviside's condition R′/L′ = G′/C′, for which the attenuation and velocity are independent of frequency and Z₀ is real, so pulses arrive attenuated but undistorted. *First defined in* [13-08](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-08-transmission-lines-sinusoidal-steady-state.md). *See also:* [Propagation constant](#propagation-constant), [Telegrapher's equations](#telegraphers-equations).

<a id="distortionless-transmission"></a>**Distortionless transmission** — Passing a signal with only a gain and a delay, y = Kx(t − t₀), which requires a constant magnitude response and a phase that is linear in frequency (constant group delay). *First defined in* [11-06](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-06-continuous-time-fourier-transform.md). *See also:* [Group delay](#group-delay).

<a id="distributed-rc-line"></a>**Distributed RC line** — A wire whose resistance and capacitance are spread along its length; driven by a step, its far end reaches 50% at about 0.38 RC, so delay grows as length squared. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="disturbance-rejection"></a>**Disturbance rejection** — A feedback loop's ability to keep an unwanted input (a load, a supply change, an ambient change) from reaching the output; an output disturbance is multiplied by S = 1/(1 + L), so rejection is good only where the loop gain is large. *First defined in* [15-04](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-04-feedback-and-steady-state-error.md). *See also:* [Sensitivity function](#sensitivity-function).

<a id="dither"></a>**Dither** — A small random signal added before a quantizer so that the quantization error stops tracking the signal. Triangular-PDF dither two steps wide makes the mean and power of the total error independent of the input, at the cost of tripling the error power. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="divergence"></a>**Divergence** — ∇ · F, the net outflow of a vector field per unit volume at a point; a source density. Gauss's law states ∇ · E = ρ/ε₀. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md). *See also:* [Flux](#flux).

<a id="divergence-theorem"></a>**Divergence theorem** — The total outward flux of a field through a closed surface equals the integral of its divergence over the enclosed volume; it turns local source density into a global balance. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md). *See also:* [Divergence](#divergence), [Flux](#flux).

<a id="diversity-gain"></a>**Diversity gain** — The reduction in required SNR, at equal total received energy, from combining independently fading branches; distinct from array gain, which is the extra energy the branches collect. *First defined in* [17-09](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-09-wireless-channels.md). *See also:* [Array gain](#array-gain).

<a id="diversity-order"></a>**Diversity order** — The exponent L in an error or outage probability that falls as SNR^(−L); obtained from L independently fading copies of the signal across antennas, frequency or time. *First defined in* [17-09](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-09-wireless-channels.md). *See also:* [Maximal-ratio combining](#maximal-ratio-combining), [Rayleigh fading](#rayleigh-fading).

<a id="dma-overrun"></a>**DMA overrun** — Loss of data when a DMA overwrites a buffer, or a receiver's ring, before software has finished with its previous contents; detected by comparing indices or by status flags, and prevented by sizing blocks for the worst-case service latency. *First defined in* [18-04](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-04-dma-and-data-movement.md). *See also:* [Ping-pong buffering](#ping-pong-buffering).

<a id="doherty-amplifier"></a>**Doherty amplifier** — A main amplifier feeding the load through a quarter-wave impedance inverter, with an auxiliary amplifier that turns on at high drive and modulates the main's load, so the main reaches full swing, and peak efficiency, 6 dB below the combined peak (Doherty, 1936). *First defined in* [21-07](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-07-power-amplifiers.md). *See also:* [Load modulation](#load-modulation).

<a id="domain-and-range"></a>**Domain and range** — The domain is the set of allowed inputs of a function; the range is the set of outputs it can produce. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md).

<a id="domain-specific-accelerator"></a>**Domain-specific accelerator** — A processor specialized for one class of workloads, such as neural networks, trading generality for much higher throughput and efficiency through dedicated datapaths, local memories and narrow number formats. *First defined in* [14-14](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-14-ai-accelerators.md). *See also:* [Systolic array](#systolic-array).

<a id="dominant-mode"></a>**Dominant mode** — The mode with the lowest cutoff frequency in a waveguide, TE₁₀ in a rectangular guide (f_c = c/2a); operating between its cutoff and the next mode's keeps the guide single-mode. *First defined in* [13-10](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-10-waveguides-and-resonators.md). *See also:* [Waveguide mode](#waveguide-mode).

<a id="dominant-poles"></a>**Dominant poles** — The poles closest to the imaginary axis, whose slowly decaying modes shape most of a response; a pair dominates when the other poles are several times (commonly more than five times) farther to the left. *First defined in* [15-03](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-03-time-response.md). *See also:* [Dominant-pole approximation](#dominant-pole-approximation).

<a id="dominant-pole-approximation"></a>**Dominant-pole approximation** — For a transfer function whose denominator is 1 + b_1s + b_2s² + …, with one pole far below the others, the low pole is about 1/b_1 and the next about b_1/b_2; it errs low when the poles are less than about a decade apart. *First defined in* [12-03](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-03-frequency-response-miller-poles-zeros.md). *See also:* [Gain-bandwidth product](#gain-bandwidth-product), [Miller effect](#miller-effect).

<a id="dominant-pole-compensation"></a>**Dominant-pole compensation** — Stabilizing a multi-pole feedback amplifier by making one pole so low that the loop gain falls to one before the other poles add much phase lag; lowering an existing pole costs less bandwidth than adding a new one. *First defined in* [12-06](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-06-stability-and-compensation.md). *See also:* [Miller compensation](#miller-compensation), [Phase margin](#phase-margin).

<a id="domino-logic"></a>**Domino logic** — Dynamic gates each followed by a static inverter, so that every dynamic-gate input starts low and can only rise during evaluation; the stages evaluate in sequence like falling dominoes. Each stage is non-inverting, so inverted functions need dual-rail domino. *First defined in* [19-03](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-03-logic-families.md). *See also:* [Dynamic logic](#dynamic-logic).
