<a id="fermi-estimate"></a>**Fermi estimate** — An order-of-magnitude estimate built from rounded assumptions and simple multiplication, used to sanity-check calculations and claims. *First defined in* [00-03](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-03-how-to-study-this-curriculum.md).

<a id="fermi-level"></a>**Fermi level** — The energy E_F at which a state would be occupied with probability one half; in equilibrium it is constant throughout a system, and its position relative to the band edges sets the electron and hole concentrations. *First defined in* [09-02](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-02-carriers-doping-fermi-level.md). *See also:* [Fermi–Dirac distribution](#fermi-dirac-distribution), [Intrinsic Fermi level](#intrinsic-fermi-level).

<a id="fermi-level-pinning"></a>**Fermi-level pinning** — The weak dependence of Schottky barrier height on metal work function, caused by interface states that hold the Fermi level near a fixed energy in the gap; for silicon Hu fits φ_Bn ≈ 0.7 V + 0.2(ψ_M − 4.75 V). *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md).

<a id="fermi-dirac-distribution"></a>**Fermi–Dirac distribution** — The probability f(E) = 1/(1 + e^((E − E_F)/kT)) that an electron state of energy E is occupied in equilibrium; it falls from 0.9 to 0.1 over about 4.4 kT and reduces to the Boltzmann factor far above E_F. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="fermi-dirac-integral"></a>**Fermi–Dirac integral** — The function F_1/2(η) = (2/√π)∫₀^∞ √x dx/(1 + e^(x − η)) that gives the carrier density of a parabolic band with any Fermi level, n = N_C F_1/2((E_F − E_C)/kT); it reduces to e^η when η ≪ −1. *First defined in* [09-02](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-02-carriers-doping-fermi-level.md).

<a id="ferranti-effect"></a>**Ferranti effect** — The rise of voltage at the open or lightly loaded far end of a long line above the sending voltage, V_R = V_S/cos(βℓ), because the line's capacitive charging current flows through its inductance. *First defined in* [22-12](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-12-power-systems-fundamentals.md).

<a id="ferroelectric-fet-fefet"></a>**Ferroelectric FET (FeFET)** — A transistor with a ferroelectric in its gate stack, whose polarization shifts the threshold voltage; the memory window is roughly 2E_c t_FE and the read is nondestructive. *First defined in* [23-08](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-08-emerging-memories.md). *See also:* [Ferroelectric RAM (FeRAM)](#ferroelectric-ram-feram).

<a id="ferroelectric-ram-feram"></a>**Ferroelectric RAM (FeRAM)** — A 1T1C memory whose capacitor dielectric is ferroelectric; reading reverses the polarization and senses the released charge 2P_rA, so the read is destructive but the data needs no refresh. *First defined in* [23-08](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-08-emerging-memories.md). *See also:* [Remanent polarization](#remanent-polarization), [Ferroelectric FET (FeFET)](#ferroelectric-fet-fefet).

<a id="ferromagnetism"></a>**Ferromagnetism** — Strong, spontaneous alignment of atomic magnetic moments in domains (iron, nickel, cobalt, ferrites), giving high permeability, saturation and hysteresis. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="ficks-law"></a>**Fick's law** — The statement that a diffusion flux is proportional to, and directed down, the concentration gradient, F = −D dn/dx; it follows from a random walk. *First defined in* [09-03](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-03-drift-and-diffusion.md).

<a id="field-stitching"></a>**Field stitching** — Printing a die larger than one exposure field as two or more abutting exposures; it costs throughput and needs alignment across the stitch. *First defined in* [25-02](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-02-lithography.md).

<a id="field-weakening"></a>**Field weakening** — Reducing a machine's effective field above base speed (field current in a DC or wound-rotor machine, a demagnetizing stator current in a PMSM) so the back EMF stays within the supply voltage, trading torque for speed at roughly constant power. *First defined in* [22-11](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-11-electric-machines.md).

<a id="field-oriented-control"></a>**Field-oriented control** — Vector control that transforms measured stator currents into a frame rotating with the rotor flux and regulates the flux-producing (d) and torque-producing (q) components separately, making an AC machine as controllable as a DC one. *First defined in* [22-11](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-11-electric-machines.md).

<a id="field-programmable-gate-array-fpga"></a>**Field-programmable gate array (FPGA)** — A chip of lookup tables, flip-flops, block RAMs, DSP blocks and I/O joined by programmable routing, configured after manufacture by loading a bitstream. *First defined in* [08-11](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-11-memories-and-programmable-logic.md). *See also:* [Lookup table (LUT)](#lookup-table-lut), [Block RAM](#block-ram), [Bitstream](#bitstream).

<a id="figure-of-merit-modulation"></a>**Figure of merit (modulation)** — The ratio of a scheme's output SNR to the baseband reference γ = S_R/(N0·W) at the same received power; 1 for DSB-SC and SSB, about 1/3 for full-modulation tone AM, 1.5β² for tone FM above threshold. *First defined in* [17-03](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-03-analog-modulation.md). *See also:* [Frequency modulation](#frequency-modulation), [Single-sideband modulation](#single-sideband-modulation).

<a id="fill-factor"></a>**Fill factor** — The ratio of a solar cell's maximum output power to the product V_oc I_sc, measuring how square its I–V curve is; about 0.75 is typical, and higher for an ideal cell. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="fin-efficiency"></a>**Fin efficiency** — The heat a fin removes divided by what it would remove if it were entirely at its base temperature; tanh(mL)/mL for a straight fin with an insulated tip, with m = sqrt(2h/(k t)). *First defined in* [25-08](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-08-thermal-engineering.md). *See also:* [Heat transfer coefficient](#heat-transfer-coefficient).

<a id="fin-quantization"></a>**Fin quantization** — In a FinFET, a transistor's width comes in whole fins, so device strength ratios inside a cell can only be ratios of integers; nanosheet transistors remove the restriction by letting the ribbon width vary. *First defined in* [23-02](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-02-sram-technology.md). *See also:* [Nanosheet](#nanosheet).

<a id="final-test"></a>**Final test** — Testing packaged parts, often at temperature and at speed, to catch assembly damage, test what wafer sort could not and assign speed or voltage bins. *First defined in* [25-11](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-11-test-ate-sort-burn-in.md).

<a id="final-value-theorem"></a>**Final-value theorem** — f(∞) = lim sF(s) as s → 0, valid only if f actually settles, that is, every pole of sF(s) lies in the open left half-plane; applied to an unstable or oscillating signal it gives a wrong answer. *First defined in* [02-05](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-05-laplace-transform-for-odes.md). *See also:* [Initial-value theorem](#initial-value-theorem), [DC gain](#dc-gain).

<a id="finfet"></a>**FinFET** — A multigate MOSFET whose channel is a thin vertical silicon fin with the gate draped over its sidewalls and top; its width is 2H_fin + W_fin per fin and comes in whole fins. *First defined in* [09-12](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-12-finfet-gaa-cfet-backside-power.md).

<a id="finite-state-machine-fsm"></a>**Finite state machine (FSM)** — A sequential circuit described by a finite set of states, a next-state function of the present state and inputs, an output function and a reset state; implemented as a state register with next-state and output logic. *First defined in* [08-08](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-08-finite-state-machines.md). *See also:* [Moore machine](#moore-machine), [Mealy machine](#mealy-machine), [State diagram](#state-diagram).

<a id="finite-difference-method"></a>**Finite-difference method** — Approximating derivatives by differences on a grid; for Laplace's equation each grid potential equals the average of its four neighbours to second order in the spacing, giving linear equations that a computer, or a grid of equal resistors, solves. *First defined in* [13-02](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-02-electrostatics-boundary-value-problems.md). *See also:* [Laplace's equation](#laplaces-equation).

<a id="finite-time-blow-up"></a>**Finite-time blow-up** — A solution of a nonlinear ODE reaching infinity at a finite time although the equation is smooth, as for y' = y² with y = 1/(1 − t); it signals superlinear positive feedback. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="fir-filter"></a>**FIR filter** — A finite impulse response filter, y[n] = Σ h[k] x[n − k] over finitely many taps; always BIBO-stable, it costs one multiply-accumulate per tap per sample and, if symmetric, has exactly linear phase. *First defined in* [11-03](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-03-convolution.md). *See also:* [Multiply-accumulate (MAC)](#multiply-accumulate-mac), [Latency](#latency).

<a id="firewall"></a>**Firewall** — A device or program that permits or blocks traffic by ordered rules on addresses, ports, protocols, connection state or content, normally ending in a default deny. *First defined in* [17-13](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-13-computer-networks-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Intrusion detection system](#intrusion-detection-system), [Security triad (CIA)](#security-triad-cia).

<a id="firmware-image"></a>**Firmware image** — A firmware binary packaged for a bootloader: a header (magic, version, sizes, security counter), the code, and trailer metadata such as a hash, a signature and installation status. *First defined in* [18-08](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-08-boot-and-firmware-update.md). *See also:* [Secure boot](#secure-boot).

<a id="first-droop"></a>**First droop** — The first and usually largest dip in a processor's supply after a fast load step, set by the package inductance against the on-die capacitance: about ΔI·√(L/C), a quarter resonance period after the step. *First defined in* [22-10](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-10-datacenter-power-delivery.md). *See also:* [Target impedance](#target-impedance), [Power delivery network](#power-delivery-network).

<a id="first-order-circuit"></a>**First-order circuit** — A circuit whose behavior is described by a first-order differential equation, typically one with a single (equivalent) capacitor or inductor. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="first-silicon-success"></a>**First-silicon success** — A chip's first manufactured version (A0) being functionally correct and shippable without a respin; reported for a minority of IC/ASIC projects in industry surveys. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="fit-failures-in-time"></a>**FIT (failures in time)** — A failure rate of one failure per 10^9 device-hours; soft-error rates of memories are quoted in FIT per megabit. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="five-transistor-ota"></a>**Five-transistor OTA** — The simplest operational transconductance amplifier, a differential pair with a current-mirror load and a tail source; gain g_m(r_o2 ∥ r_o4), small common-mode gain about 1/(2g_m3R_SS), and the first stage of the classic two-stage op-amp. *First defined in* [12-02](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-02-active-loads-cascodes-multistage.md). *See also:* [Current-mirror load](#current-mirror-load), [Common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR)](#common-mode-rejection-ratio-cmrr).

<a id="fixed-point-arithmetic"></a>**Fixed-point arithmetic** — Representing fractions as integers with an agreed scale 2^−f, so integer hardware does the arithmetic; additions are direct, products must be rescaled, and rounding, overflow and saturation are managed by the programmer. *First defined in* [05-07](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-07-bit-manipulation.md). *See also:* [Q format](#q-format), [Saturation arithmetic](#saturation-arithmetic).

<a id="fixed-ratio-bus-converter"></a>**Fixed-ratio bus converter** — An unregulated converter, usually resonant or switched-capacitor at a fixed duty cycle, that divides its input voltage by a fixed ratio (4:1, 8:1, 64:1) with high efficiency, leaving regulation to the next stage; it needs a narrow input range. *First defined in* [22-10](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-10-datacenter-power-delivery.md). *See also:* [Intermediate bus converter](#intermediate-bus-converter).

<a id="flash-adc"></a>**Flash ADC** — An ADC that compares the input with all 2^N − 1 reference levels at once using 2^N − 1 comparators and encodes the result in one clock cycle; fast, but practical only to about 6 bits. *First defined in* [20-07](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-07-nyquist-adcs.md). *See also:* [Thermometer code](#thermometer-code).

<a id="flash-translation-layer-ftl"></a>**Flash translation layer (FTL)** — The SSD firmware layer that maps logical block addresses to physical flash pages, writes every update out of place and runs garbage collection and wear leveling behind the host's back. *First defined in* [23-07](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-07-ssd-controllers.md). *See also:* [Indirection unit](#indirection-unit), [Garbage collection (SSD)](#garbage-collection-ssd).

<a id="flash-wait-state"></a>**Flash wait state** — An extra clock cycle inserted in each flash read because the flash access time exceeds one clock period; WS = ceil(f t_acc) - 1, so each wait state buys a band of clock frequencies 1/t_acc wide. *First defined in* [18-01](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-01-microcontroller-architecture.md). *See also:* [Prefetch buffer](#prefetch-buffer).

<a id="flat-fading"></a>**Flat fading** — Fading in which the signal bandwidth is much smaller than the coherence bandwidth, so the whole signal sees one complex gain and no intersymbol interference. *First defined in* [17-09](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-09-wireless-channels.md). *See also:* [Frequency-selective fading](#frequency-selective-fading), [Coherence bandwidth](#coherence-bandwidth).

<a id="flat-band-voltage"></a>**Flat-band voltage** — The gate voltage at which the semiconductor's bands are flat up to the surface, V_FB = ψ_g − ψ_s − Q_ox/C_ox; about −1 V for an n⁺ poly gate on p-type silicon. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="flexible-data-placement-fdp"></a>**Flexible Data Placement (FDP)** — An NVMe 2.1 feature letting the host tag writes with placement handles so the SSD keeps data of different lifetimes in different blocks, cutting write amplification without host-managed zones. *First defined in* [23-07](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-07-ssd-controllers.md). *See also:* [Zoned Namespaces (ZNS)](#zoned-namespaces-zns), [Write amplification factor (WAF)](#write-amplification-factor-waf).

<a id="flicker-1-f-noise"></a>**Flicker (1/f) noise** — Noise whose power spectral density falls as 1/f, so every decade of frequency carries equal power; dominant at low frequencies in MOSFETs. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="flicker-noise"></a>**Flicker noise** — Noise whose power spectral density rises as 1/f toward low frequency, from carriers trapped and released at interfaces; strong in MOSFETs, it contributes equal power in every decade and is characterized by its corner frequency with the white floor. *First defined in* [12-10](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-10-noise-in-circuits.md). *See also:* [Thermal noise](#thermal-noise), [Input-referred noise](#input-referred-noise).

<a id="flicker-noise-up-conversion"></a>**Flicker-noise up-conversion** — The conversion of a device's low-frequency 1/f noise into close-in oscillator phase noise falling at −30 dB per decade; it acts through the average (DC) value of the effective ISF, so the 1/f³ corner is the device's flicker corner times (Γ_dc/Γ_rms)², which waveform symmetry keeps small. *First defined in* [21-06](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-06-oscillators-and-vcos.md). *See also:* [Impulse sensitivity function (ISF)](#impulse-sensitivity-function-isf), [Flicker noise](#flicker-noise).

<a id="flip-chip"></a>**Flip-chip** — Mounting a die face down on solder bumps or copper pillars spread over its whole area, giving area-array I/O, short low-inductance connections and many parallel power and ground paths. *First defined in* [25-06](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-06-packaging-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Underfill](#underfill), [Wire bonding](#wire-bonding).

<a id="flit"></a>**Flit** — A fixed-size link-layer unit (256 bytes in PCIe 6.0) carrying data, link information, CRC and FEC parity, so that error correction and retry operate on whole flits. *First defined in* [24-04](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-04-dsp-serdes-and-fec.md). *See also:* [Link-level retry](#link-level-retry).

<a id="floating-gate"></a>**Floating gate** — An electrically isolated conductor between a transistor's control gate and channel; electrons stored on it raise the threshold voltage by Q/C_CG, which is how flash memory stores data without power. *First defined in* [23-06](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-06-nand-flash-and-3d-nand.md). *See also:* [Charge-trap flash](#charge-trap-flash), [Fowler–Nordheim tunneling](#fowler-nordheim-tunneling).

<a id="floating-tap"></a>**Floating tap** — An equalizer tap, or small group of taps, placed at an adaptively chosen delay to cancel a distant reflection without building an equalizer long enough to reach it. *First defined in* [24-04](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-04-dsp-serdes-and-fec.md). *See also:* [Feed-forward equalizer (FFE)](#feed-forward-equalizer-ffe).

<a id="floating-point-number"></a>**Floating-point number** — A number stored as sign, exponent and fraction in binary; IEEE 754 binary64 (Python float, C double) has 53 significant bits (about 16 decimal digits), so most decimals such as 0.1 are approximated. *First defined in* [05-01](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-01-python-fundamentals.md).

<a id="floor-division"></a>**Floor division** — Division that rounds the quotient down toward minus infinity (Python's //), paired with a remainder (%) that takes the divisor's sign; −7 // 2 is −4 in Python but C's integer division gives −3. *First defined in* [05-01](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-01-python-fundamentals.md).

<a id="floorplan"></a>**Floorplan** — The first physical-design step: choosing the die and core outline, the standard-cell rows, the positions of macros and I/O, and the power-distribution network, before any standard cell is placed. *First defined in* [19-11](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-11-place-route-signoff.md). *See also:* [Utilization](#utilization), [IR drop](#ir-drop).

<a id="flush"></a>**Flush** — Discarding instructions fetched down a wrong path (after a taken branch, under predict-not-taken) by turning them into bubbles before they change any state. *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md).

<a id="flux"></a>**Flux** — The surface integral of a vector field's normal component, ∬ F · dA, measuring how much of the field passes through a surface. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="flux-walking"></a>**Flux walking** — The gradual drift of a bridge or push-pull transformer's flux toward saturation when the positive and negative volt-seconds are not exactly equal; prevented by current-mode control or a series blocking capacitor. *First defined in* [22-04](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-04-isolated-converters.md). *See also:* [Full-bridge converter](#full-bridge-converter), [Core reset](#core-reset).

<a id="fly-by-topology"></a>**Fly-by topology** — Routing a module's clock and command/address signals past each DRAM in turn, which keeps the stubs short but makes the clock arrive at each DRAM several bit times apart. *First defined in* [23-04](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-04-dram-interfaces.md). *See also:* [Write leveling](#write-leveling).

<a id="flyback-converter"></a>**Flyback converter** — An isolated buck-boost whose coupled inductor stores energy in its magnetizing inductance during the on-time and releases it through the secondary during the off-time, V = (V_in/n)·D/(1 − D); the usual topology below about 100–150 W. *First defined in* [22-04](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-04-isolated-converters.md). *See also:* [Buck-boost converter](#buck-boost-converter), [Reflected voltage](#reflected-voltage).

<a id="flyback-diode"></a>**Flyback diode** — A diode placed across an inductive load so that, when the driving switch opens, the inductor's current circulates through the diode, clamping the switch voltage to about one diode drop above the supply. Also called a freewheeling diode. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="fm-threshold"></a>**FM threshold** — The carrier-to-noise ratio in the IF bandwidth, roughly 10 dB, below which noise occasionally encircles the carrier phasor, producing 2π phase jumps (clicks) and a rapid collapse of the output SNR. *First defined in* [17-03](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-03-analog-modulation.md). *See also:* [Frequency modulation](#frequency-modulation).

<a id="fmeda"></a>**FMEDA** — Failure modes, effects and diagnostic analysis: a table of every failure mode of every safety-related hardware element, its rate, its effect on the safety goal and the diagnostic coverage of the safety mechanisms, from which SPFM, LFM and PMHF are computed. *First defined in* [25-10](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-10-qualification-and-functional-safety.md). *See also:* [Diagnostic coverage](#diagnostic-coverage).

<a id="fo4-delay"></a>**FO4 delay** — The delay of an inverter driving four copies of itself, t_p0(1 + 4/γ). Because it scales with the process like other gate delays, clock periods quoted in FO4 delays compare designs across nodes. *First defined in* [19-02](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-02-cmos-inverter-dynamic.md). *See also:* [Intrinsic delay](#intrinsic-delay), [Ring oscillator](#ring-oscillator).

<a id="foldback-current-limiting"></a>**Foldback current limiting** — Output short-circuit protection whose current limit falls as the voltage across the output device rises, so that a short circuit, which puts the full supply across the device, draws much less current than a normal peak and stays inside the safe operating area. *First defined in* [12-07](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-07-output-stages.md). *See also:* [Safe operating area](#safe-operating-area).

<a id="folded-cascode"></a>**Folded cascode** — A single-stage op-amp in which the input pair's signal currents are folded into common-gate cascode devices of the opposite type, giving cascode output resistance with more headroom than a telescopic cascode; its load capacitance sets the dominant pole, so GBW = g_m1/(2πC_L). *First defined in* [12-08](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-08-op-amp-internals.md). *See also:* [Two-stage op-amp](#two-stage-op-amp), [Telescopic cascode amplifier](#telescopic-cascode-amplifier).

<a id="folding-hardware"></a>**Folding (hardware)** — Time-multiplexing one arithmetic unit over several operations of an algorithm, trading clock rate for area; a MAC clocked at 400 MHz folded over 16 taps serves a 25 MS/s filter. *First defined in* [16-11](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-11-dsp-hardware-architectures.md). *See also:* [Multiply-accumulate (MAC)](#multiply-accumulate-mac).

<a id="forced-beta"></a>**Forced beta** — The ratio I_C/I_B imposed on a saturated bipolar transistor by its circuit, smaller than the device's β; switches are designed with a forced beta near 10 so every device saturates. *First defined in* [10-03](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-03-bjt-dc-operation-and-biasing.md).

<a id="forced-pwm"></a>**Forced PWM** — A mode that keeps a converter switching at its fixed frequency at all loads, letting the inductor current go negative at light load; it gives predictable ripple and spectrum at the cost of light-load efficiency. *First defined in* [22-02](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-02-buck-converter-steady-state.md). *See also:* [Pulse-frequency modulation (PFM)](#pulse-frequency-modulation-pfm), [Continuous conduction mode (CCM)](#continuous-conduction-mode-ccm).

<a id="force-current-analogy"></a>**Force–current analogy** — The mapping of a mechanical system onto a circuit with force ↔ current and velocity ↔ voltage (mass ↔ C to ground, damping ↔ conductance, stiffness ↔ 1/L); elements sharing a velocity become parallel elements, so the circuit keeps the mechanism's topology. *First defined in* [15-01](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-01-modeling-dynamic-systems.md). *See also:* [Force–voltage analogy](#force-voltage-analogy).

<a id="force-voltage-analogy"></a>**Force–voltage analogy** — The mapping of a mass–spring–damper onto a series RLC circuit (force ↔ voltage, velocity ↔ current, mass ↔ L, damping ↔ R, compliance 1/k_s ↔ C); it turns mechanical systems into circuits that SPICE can simulate. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="form-factor"></a>**Form factor** — RMS value divided by the rectified average; π/(2√2) ≈ 1.111 for a sine. Average-responding meters assume this value. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="formal-verification"></a>**Formal verification** — Using mathematical proof (model checking, equivalence checking) to show that a design satisfies a property for all possible inputs, instead of testing examples. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="forward-converter"></a>**Forward converter** — An isolated buck converter that passes power through its transformer during the on-time into an LC output filter, V = D·V_in/n, and must reset its core during the off-time. *First defined in* [22-04](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-04-isolated-converters.md). *See also:* [Tertiary winding](#tertiary-winding), [Buck converter](#buck-converter).

<a id="forward-error-correction-fec"></a>**Forward error correction (FEC)** — Adding redundant symbols so the receiver can correct errors without retransmission; it lets links run at a raw BER near 1e-4 and still deliver 1e-13 or better. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="forward-transit-time"></a>**Forward transit time** — The ratio τ_F = Q_F/I_C of stored excess charge to collector current in a forward-active bipolar transistor, the sum of emitter, base (W_B²/2D_B for a uniform base) and collector delays; it sets the diffusion capacitance and limits f_T. *First defined in* [09-07](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-07-bipolar-junction-transistor.md).

<a id="forward-active-mode"></a>**Forward-active mode** — The amplifying region of a bipolar transistor, with the base–emitter junction forward biased and the base–collector junction reverse biased, where the collector current is set by V_BE and nearly independent of V_CE. *First defined in* [09-07](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-07-bipolar-junction-transistor.md).

<a id="forward-active-region"></a>**Forward-active region** — The bipolar operating region with the base-emitter junction forward-biased and the base-collector junction reverse-biased, where I_C ≈ βI_B and the collector acts as a current source. *First defined in* [10-03](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-03-bjt-dc-operation-and-biasing.md).

<a id="forwarded-clock"></a>**Forwarded clock** — A clock sent alongside parallel data wires so the receiver samples with it directly instead of recovering timing from the data; it removes the CDR but makes skew between wires the speed limit. *First defined in* [24-06](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-06-d2d-memory-phys-scale-up.md). *See also:* [Clock and data recovery (CDR)](#clock-and-data-recovery-cdr).

<a id="forwarding-bypassing"></a>**Forwarding (bypassing)** — Routing a result from a later pipeline register (EX/MEM or MEM/WB) directly to the inputs of an instruction that needs it, instead of waiting for it to be written to the register file. *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md).

<a id="foster-network"></a>**Foster network** — An RC model written as a series chain of parallel R–C pairs, Z(t) = Σ Rᵢ(1 − e^(−t/τᵢ)); it is a modal (eigenvalue) expansion whose nodes have no physical meaning, so it cannot be cascaded with other stages. *First defined in* [02-09](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-09-systems-of-odes-and-matrix-exponential.md).

<a id="foundry"></a>**Foundry** — A company that manufactures chips designed by its customers, supplying them with a process and its PDK. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="four-point-probe"></a>**Four-point probe** — A sheet-resistance measurement with four collinear probes, driving current through the outer pair and measuring voltage across the inner pair so that contact resistance drops out; for a thin film R_s = (π/ln 2)(V/I) ≈ 4.532 V/I. *First defined in* [09-03](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-03-drift-and-diffusion.md). *See also:* [Sheet resistance](#sheet-resistance).

<a id="four-resistor-bias"></a>**Four-resistor bias** — The standard discrete BJT bias, a base divider with an emitter resistor (and a collector resistor), giving I_E = (V_Th − V_BE)/(R_E + R_Th/(β + 1)), nearly independent of β when R_Th is much less than (β + 1)R_E. *First defined in* [10-03](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-03-bjt-dc-operation-and-biasing.md).

<a id="four-switch-buck-boost"></a>**Four-switch buck-boost** — A non-inverting converter with a buck half bridge at its input and a boost half bridge at its output sharing one inductor; it runs as a buck, a boost or a mixed mode, so a rail can be held while a battery crosses it. *First defined in* [22-03](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-03-boost-buck-boost-topologies.md). *See also:* [Buck-boost converter](#buck-boost-converter).

<a id="four-terminal-kelvin-measurement"></a>**Four-terminal (Kelvin) measurement** — Measuring a resistance or current with one pair of leads that forces the current and a separate pair, attached at the element itself, that senses the voltage while carrying almost no current, so lead, contact and copper resistances drop out. *First defined in* [06-11](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-11-practical-dc-circuits-and-measurement.md). *See also:* [Current-sense shunt](#current-sense-shunt), [Remote sensing](#remote-sensing).

<a id="four-valued-logic"></a>**Four-valued logic** — The simulation model in which each bit is 0, 1, X (unknown) or Z (undriven); 0 dominates AND and 1 dominates OR, other combinations with X or Z give X, and === compares the four values literally. *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md).

<a id="fourier-coefficient"></a>**Fourier coefficient** — The amplitude of one harmonic in a periodic signal, b_n = (2/T)∫ x(t) sin(nωt) dt (and a_n with cosine), found by orthogonality. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="fourier-series"></a>**Fourier series** — The representation of a periodic signal as a sum of complex exponentials at multiples of its fundamental frequency, x(t) = Σ c_k e^{jkω₀t}, with c_k = (1/T₀)∫ x(t) e^{−jkω₀t} dt found by orthogonality. *First defined in* [11-05](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-05-fourier-series.md). *See also:* [Fourier coefficient](#fourier-coefficient), [Harmonic](#harmonic), [Line spectrum](#line-spectrum).

<a id="fourier-transform"></a>**Fourier transform** — X(jω) = ∫ x(t) e^{−jωt} dt, with inverse x(t) = (1/2π)∫ X(jω) e^{jωt} dω: the spectrum of an aperiodic signal, obtained as the limit of the Fourier series as the period grows; X(f) = X(j2πf) in hertz. *First defined in* [11-06](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-06-continuous-time-fourier-transform.md). *See also:* [Fourier series](#fourier-series), [Convolution theorem](#convolution-theorem).

<a id="foveated-rendering"></a>**Foveated rendering** — Rendering only the region the eye's fovea sees at full resolution and the periphery at reduced resolution, usually guided by eye tracking, to cut GPU work several-fold. *First defined in* [27-04](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-04-wearables-earbuds-and-glasses.md). *See also:* [Motion-to-photon latency](#motion-to-photon-latency).

<a id="fowler-nordheim-tunneling"></a>**Fowler–Nordheim tunneling** — Tunneling through a triangular barrier formed when a strong field tilts an insulator's band; the current rises steeply with field (about seven orders of magnitude from 7 to 10 MV/cm in SiO₂) and is used to program and erase flash. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="fp8"></a>**FP8** — The two 8-bit floating-point formats used for AI, E4M3 (largest value 448, no infinities, one NaN code per sign) and E5M2 (largest value 57 344, IEEE-style specials), standardized by the Open Compute Project in 2023. *First defined in* [08-01](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-01-number-systems-and-codes.md). *See also:* [bfloat16](#bfloat16), [Block floating point](#block-floating-point).

<a id="fpga-prototyping"></a>**FPGA prototyping** — Partitioning a chip design across FPGAs to run it at up to tens of megahertz for software development and system testing before silicon, with less signal visibility and longer bring-up than an emulator. *First defined in* [19-13](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-13-verification-methods.md). *See also:* [Emulation](#emulation).

<a id="fractional-n-synthesizer"></a>**Fractional-N synthesizer** — A PLL whose divide ratio switches between integers so that its average is fractional, usually under the control of a ΔΣ modulator that pushes the resulting phase error to high offsets where the loop filters it. *First defined in* [20-10](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-10-plls-and-jitter.md). *See also:* [Phase-locked loop (PLL)](#phase-locked-loop-pll), [Delta-sigma modulator](#delta-sigma-modulator).

<a id="frand"></a>**FRAND** — Fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory licensing terms that holders of standard-essential patents undertake to offer (ETSI IPR Policy clause 6.1); what is "reasonable" and on which royalty base is often disputed. *First defined in* [26-02](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-02-design-reviews-and-standards.md). *See also:* [Standard-essential patent (SEP)](#standard-essential-patent-sep).

<a id="free-distance"></a>**Free distance** — The smallest Hamming weight of a convolutional-code path that leaves the all-zero state and returns to it; it sets the asymptotic soft-decision gain 10·log10(R·d_free). *First defined in* [17-08](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-08-channel-coding.md). *See also:* [Convolutional code](#convolutional-code), [Coding gain](#coding-gain).

<a id="freeze-out"></a>**Freeze-out** — The recapture of carriers by their dopants at low temperature, when kT becomes small compared with the ionization energy; lightly doped silicon begins to lose carriers this way below about 100 K. *First defined in* [09-02](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-02-carriers-doping-fermi-level.md).

<a id="frequency-modulation"></a>**Frequency modulation** — Angle modulation in which the instantaneous frequency follows the message, fi = fc + kf·m(t); constant envelope, Bessel-function sidebands, bandwidth about 2(Δf + W) by Carson's rule, and an output SNR of 3D²·(Pm/max m²)·γ above threshold. *First defined in* [17-03](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-03-analog-modulation.md). *See also:* [Phase modulation](#phase-modulation), [Carson's rule](#carsons-rule), [FM threshold](#fm-threshold), [Instantaneous frequency](#instantaneous-frequency).

<a id="frequency-nadir"></a>**Frequency nadir** — The lowest frequency reached after a loss of generation, when governor and fast responses first match the deficit; deeper and earlier with less inertia or slower response. *First defined in* [22-12](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-12-power-systems-fundamentals.md).

<a id="frequency-prewarping"></a>**Frequency prewarping** — Replacing 2/T in the Tustin substitution by ω_p/tan(ω_pT/2), so the discrete controller matches the continuous one exactly at the chosen frequency ω_p (usually crossover or a notch frequency) despite frequency warping. *First defined in* [15-11](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-11-digital-control.md). *See also:* [Tustin transformation](#tustin-transformation), [Frequency warping](#frequency-warping).

<a id="frequency-resolution"></a>**Frequency resolution** — The smallest separation at which two spectral components appear as distinct peaks; for a record of duration T it is about 1/T hertz with a rectangular window, and roughly twice that with a Hamming window. *First defined in* [11-07](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-07-discrete-time-fourier-transform.md). *See also:* [Window function](#window-function), [Zero-padding](#zero-padding).

<a id="frequency-response"></a>**Frequency response** — The complex gain H(jω) of a linear system at angular frequency ω. Its magnitude scales a sinusoid's amplitude and its angle shifts the sinusoid's phase. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Corner frequency](#corner-frequency).

<a id="frequency-reuse"></a>**Frequency reuse** — Using the same frequencies again in cells far enough apart; with hexagonal clusters of N cells the co-channel distance is D = R√(3N), and modern OFDMA systems reuse every frequency in every cell (N = 1). *First defined in* [17-12](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-12-multiple-access-and-cellular-wifi.md). *See also:* [Cluster size](#cluster-size), [Handover](#handover).

<a id="frequency-warping"></a>**Frequency warping** — The nonlinear frequency map of the bilinear transform, Ω = (2/T) tan(ω/2): nearly linear well below the sample rate, compressing the whole analog axis into ω < π; corrected at one chosen frequency by prewarping. *First defined in* [11-09](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-09-z-transform.md). *See also:* [Bilinear transform](#bilinear-transform).

<a id="frequency-division-multiplexing-fdm"></a>**Frequency-division multiplexing (FDM)** — Sharing a medium by giving each message its own carrier frequency slot, separated by guard bands sized for the selection filters' transition width; OFDM is its digital form. *First defined in* [11-11](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-11-modulation-and-filtering-applications.md).

<a id="frequency-sampling-design"></a>**Frequency-sampling design** — Designing an FIR filter by specifying its response at N equally spaced frequencies and taking the inverse DFT; the response is exact at the samples and ripples between them, and transition samples reduce the ripple. *First defined in* [16-06](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-06-fir-filter-design.md). *See also:* [Discrete Fourier transform (DFT)](#discrete-fourier-transform-dft).

<a id="frequency-selective-fading"></a>**Frequency-selective fading** — Fading in which the signal bandwidth exceeds the coherence bandwidth, so different frequencies fade differently and symbols smear into each other; handled by equalizers or OFDM. *First defined in* [17-09](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-09-wireless-channels.md). *See also:* [Flat fading](#flat-fading), [Coherence bandwidth](#coherence-bandwidth).

<a id="frequency-shift-keying"></a>**Frequency-shift keying** — Sending one of several tones per symbol; binary FSK is orthogonal signalling (3 dB behind BPSK coherently), and its continuous-phase forms (MSK, GFSK) have a constant envelope. *First defined in* [17-06](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-06-bandpass-digital-modulation.md). *See also:* [MSK and GMSK](#msk-and-gmsk), [Orthogonal signalling](#orthogonal-signalling), [Noncoherent detection](#noncoherent-detection).

<a id="fresnel-equations"></a>**Fresnel equations** — The reflection and transmission coefficients of a plane wave at a planar interface as functions of angle, separately for TE (perpendicular) and TM (parallel) polarization; they follow from continuity of the tangential fields. *First defined in* [13-06](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-06-reflection-and-transmission.md). *See also:* [Brewster angle](#brewster-angle), [Snell's law](#snells-law).

<a id="friis-noise-formula"></a>**Friis noise formula** — The cascade rule F = F1 + (F2 − 1)/G1 + (F3 − 1)/(G1G2) + …, with available gains, or Te = Te1 + Te2/G1 + …; each stage's excess noise is divided by the gain ahead of it, so the first stage dominates. *First defined in* [17-02](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-02-noise-and-snr.md). *See also:* [Noise figure](#noise-figure), [Noise measure](#noise-measure).

<a id="friis-transmission-equation"></a>**Friis transmission equation** — P_r/P_t = G_t·G_r·(λ/4πR)² for antennas in each other's far field in free space; the free-space path loss is 20 log₁₀(4πR/λ) dB. *First defined in* [13-11](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-11-radiation-and-antennas.md). *See also:* [Effective aperture](#effective-aperture), [EIRP](#eirp).

<a id="fringing-flux"></a>**Fringing flux** — Flux that bulges outward around an air gap, enlarging the gap's effective area (raising the inductance) and cutting nearby turns, where it induces eddy-current loss. *First defined in* [22-05](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-05-magnetics-design.md). *See also:* [Air gap](#air-gap).

<a id="front-end-of-line-feol"></a>**Front end of line (FEOL)** — The part of wafer processing that builds the transistors in and on the silicon: isolation, wells, channels, the gate stack and the source and drain. It contains the hottest steps. *First defined in* [25-01](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-01-process-flow-overview.md). *See also:* [Middle of line (MOL)](#middle-of-line-mol), [Back end of line (BEOL)](#back-end-of-line-beol).

<a id="front-end-module-pamid"></a>**Front-end module (PAMiD)** — A package integrating a radio's power amplifiers, switches, acoustic duplexers or multiplexers, couplers and often low-noise amplifiers (L-PAMiD) under one control interface, so that filters, matching and switches can be co-designed for coexistence. *First defined in* [21-09](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-09-rf-front-end.md). *See also:* [Duplexer](#duplexer), [Carrier aggregation](#carrier-aggregation).

<a id="fubinis-theorem"></a>**Fubini's theorem** — For well-behaved integrands, a double integral can be evaluated as two nested single integrals in either order; reversing the order can turn an impossible integral into an easy one. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md). *See also:* [Double integral](#double-integral).

<a id="fuel-gauge"></a>**Fuel gauge** — An IC or algorithm that estimates a battery's state of charge, remaining run time and state of health from its voltage, current and temperature, usually by combining coulomb counting with OCV correction and a cell model. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md). *See also:* [Coulomb counting](#coulomb-counting), [State of charge (SOC)](#state-of-charge-soc).

<a id="full-adder"></a>**Full adder** — A block that adds two bits and a carry in, giving S = A XOR B XOR Cin (three-input parity) and Cout = majority(A, B, Cin) = G + P·Cin. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md). *See also:* [Generate and propagate](#generate-and-propagate), [Ripple-carry adder](#ripple-carry-adder).

<a id="full-bridge-converter"></a>**Full-bridge converter** — An isolated converter whose four switches drive the transformer primary to ±V_in, so each switch blocks only V_in and the core is used in both directions; preferred at higher power. *First defined in* [22-04](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-04-isolated-converters.md). *See also:* [Flux walking](#flux-walking).

<a id="full-power-bandwidth"></a>**Full-power bandwidth** — The highest frequency at which an amplifier can deliver a sine of a given peak amplitude V_p without slew-rate limiting, SR/(2πV_p). *First defined in* [10-09](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-09-real-op-amps-nonidealities.md). *See also:* [Slew rate](#slew-rate).

<a id="full-well-capacity"></a>**Full-well capacity** — The largest number of electrons a pixel can hold before saturating; it caps the maximum signal-to-noise ratio at its square root. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="fully-associative-cache"></a>**Fully associative cache** — A cache with a single set, in which any block may occupy any line; it has no conflict misses but needs a tag comparator per line. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Set-associative cache](#set-associative-cache).

<a id="fully-differential-amplifier"></a>**Fully differential amplifier** — An amplifier with differential inputs and differential outputs, which doubles the output swing, rejects common-mode noise and even-order distortion, and needs common-mode feedback to set its output common-mode level. *First defined in* [12-08](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-08-op-amp-internals.md). *See also:* [Common-mode feedback](#common-mode-feedback).

<a id="fully-loaded-cost"></a>**Fully loaded cost** — COGS plus the NRE amortized over lifetime volume (NRE/V); it falls toward COGS as volume grows. *First defined in* [26-03](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-03-engineering-economics-1.md). *See also:* [Non-recurring engineering (NRE)](#non-recurring-engineering-nre).

<a id="function"></a>**Function** — A rule that assigns exactly one output to each allowed input; in engineering both input and output usually carry units (for example voltage as a function of time). *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md). *See also:* [Domain and range](#domain-and-range), [Inverse function](#inverse-function).

<a id="function-prototype"></a>**Function prototype** — A C declaration giving a function's name, return type and parameter types without its body, so that other translation units can call it; usually placed in a header file. *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md).

<a id="functional-completeness"></a>**Functional completeness** — The property of a set of gates that every Boolean function can be built from it; {AND, OR, NOT} is complete, and so are NAND alone and NOR alone, while AND and OR together are not (they cannot make NOT). *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md).

<a id="functional-coverage"></a>**Functional coverage** — A measure of which specified behaviors, input combinations or corner cases a verification run has actually exercised; used to decide when verification is complete. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="functional-organization"></a>**Functional organization** — An organization in which engineers report by discipline (design, verification, physical design), giving deep expertise and flexible staffing but no single owner below the top for each product. *First defined in* [26-06](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-06-team-structures-and-sizing.md). *See also:* [Program organization](#program-organization), [Matrix organization](#matrix-organization).

<a id="fundamental-frequency"></a>**Fundamental frequency** — The reciprocal of a periodic signal's fundamental (smallest) period, f₀ = 1/T₀; all of the signal's harmonics lie at its integer multiples. *First defined in* [11-05](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-05-fourier-series.md).

<a id="fundamental-period"></a>**Fundamental period** — The smallest positive shift that leaves a periodic signal unchanged; a sum of continuous-time periodic signals is periodic only if their periods have a rational ratio, and a discrete-time sinusoid only if ω/2π is rational. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md).

<a id="fundamental-theorem-of-calculus"></a>**Fundamental theorem of calculus** — Part 1, the accumulated area ∫_a^x f has derivative f(x); part 2, ∫_a^b f = F(b) − F(a) for any antiderivative F. Integration and differentiation are inverse operations. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="fused-multiply-add-fma"></a>**Fused multiply-add (FMA)** — An operation that computes a × b + c with a single rounding, more accurate than a separate multiply and add and the building block of dot products. *First defined in* [14-04](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-04-computer-arithmetic-and-number-formats.md).

<a id="letter-g"></a>

## G

<a id="g-t-figure-of-merit"></a>**G/T (figure of merit)** — A receiving system's antenna gain divided by its system noise temperature, in dB/K, which with the transmitter's EIRP and the path loss gives the carrier-to-noise density; about −31.6 dB/K for a handheld phone receiving a satellite. *First defined in* [21-11](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-11-link-budgets.md). *See also:* [Carrier-to-noise-density ratio](#carrier-to-noise-density-ratio).

<a id="gain-boosting"></a>**Gain boosting** — Raising a cascode's output resistance by (1 + A_b) with an auxiliary amplifier of gain A_b that holds the cascode device's source still; it gives multistage gain at single-stage speed, but creates a pole-zero doublet near the booster's unity-gain frequency that slows settling unless that frequency lies above the closed-loop bandwidth (Bult and Geelen, 1990). *First defined in* [20-02](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-02-two-stage-op-amp-design.md). *See also:* [Cascode](#cascode), [Pole–zero doublet](#pole-zero-doublet), [Settling time](#settling-time).

<a id="gain-crossover-frequency"></a>**Gain crossover frequency** — The frequency ω_c at which a loop gain's magnitude |L(jω)| equals 1 (0 dB); the phase margin is read there, and it sets the loop's speed (closed-loop bandwidth is typically 1 to 2 times ω_c). *First defined in* [15-07](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-07-frequency-domain-design.md). *See also:* [Phase margin](#phase-margin).

<a id="gain-margin"></a>**Gain margin** — How far a loop gain's magnitude is below one, in decibels, at the frequency where its phase reaches −180°, −20·log|T(jω180)|; the extra loop gain the loop could tolerate before oscillating. A typical target is at least 10 dB. *First defined in* [12-06](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-06-stability-and-compensation.md). *See also:* [Phase margin](#phase-margin), [Crossover frequency](#crossover-frequency).

<a id="gain-bandwidth-product"></a>**Gain-bandwidth product** — For an op-amp with a single dominant pole, the constant product of open-loop gain and frequency above the pole, equal to the unity-gain frequency; a closed loop's bandwidth is the gain-bandwidth product divided by the noise gain. *First defined in* [10-09](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-09-real-op-amps-nonidealities.md). *See also:* [Noise gain](#noise-gain).

<a id="gain-bandwidth-product-gbw"></a>**Gain–bandwidth product (GBW)** — For a dominant-pole amplifier, the product of DC gain and bandwidth, A0·fa, equal to the unity-gain frequency; with feedback, closed-loop bandwidth ≈ GBW divided by the noise gain 1/β. Datasheets quote it as a typical value, sometimes at a stated gain. *First defined in* [07-07](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-07-frequency-response-and-bode-plots.md). *See also:* [Loop gain](#loop-gain).

<a id="galvanic-isolation"></a>**Galvanic isolation** — Separation of two circuits so that no conductive path connects them, while energy or signals still cross by magnetic, capacitive or optical coupling; required between mains and anything a user can touch. *First defined in* [22-04](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-04-isolated-converters.md). *See also:* [Reinforced insulation](#reinforced-insulation), [Flyback converter](#flyback-converter).

<a id="garbage-collection-ssd"></a>**Garbage collection (SSD)** — Reclaiming flash blocks by copying their still-valid pages elsewhere and erasing them; the copies are the source of write amplification. *First defined in* [23-07](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-07-ssd-controllers.md). *See also:* [Write amplification factor (WAF)](#write-amplification-factor-waf), [Over-provisioning](#over-provisioning).

<a id="gaseous-absorption"></a>**Gaseous absorption** — Attenuation of radio waves by oxygen and water vapour, about 0.1 dB/km at 28 to 39 GHz but about 15 dB/km near the 60 GHz oxygen band at sea level (ITU-R P.676), which limits range and eases frequency reuse there. *First defined in* [21-10](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-10-antennas-arrays-mmwave.md). *See also:* [EIRP](#eirp).

<a id="gate-charge"></a>**Gate charge** — Q_g, the total charge a driver must deliver to turn a switch fully on; gate-drive power is Q_g·V_drv·f_s whatever the gate resistance. *First defined in* [22-06](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-06-converter-losses-and-wide-bandgap.md).

<a id="gate-coupling-ratio"></a>**Gate coupling ratio** — The fraction C_CG/C_T of a control-gate voltage that reaches a flash cell's storage node; it sets the programming voltage needed but not the threshold shift per stored electron. *First defined in* [23-06](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-06-nand-flash-and-3d-nand.md). *See also:* [Floating gate](#floating-gate).

<a id="gate-equivalent-ge"></a>**Gate equivalent (GE)** — A unit of logic area equal to one two-input NAND gate in a named cell library; a block's gate count is its area divided by the NAND2 area. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md).

<a id="gate-all-around-transistor"></a>**Gate-all-around transistor** — A MOSFET whose gate completely surrounds each channel (GAA), as a nanowire or a stack of nanosheets, giving the strongest electrostatic control of the channel. *First defined in* [09-12](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-12-finfet-gaa-cfet-backside-power.md).

<a id="gate-induced-drain-leakage"></a>**Gate-induced drain leakage** — Band-to-band tunneling current in the drain under the gate edge when the gate is low and the drain high (GIDL); it needs band bending beyond the gap and a surface field near 10⁶ V/cm, and grows steeply with drain-to-gate voltage and thinner oxides. *First defined in* [09-10](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-10-short-channel-effects-and-leakage.md).

<a id="gauge-factor"></a>**Gauge factor** — The ratio of a strain gauge's fractional resistance change to the strain, GF = (ΔR/R)/ε; about 2 for metal-foil gauges. *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="gausss-law"></a>**Gauss's law** — The electric flux out of any closed surface equals the enclosed charge divided by ε₀; with symmetry it gives fields of spheres, lines and planes in one line. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md). *See also:* [Divergence theorem](#divergence-theorem).

<a id="gaussian-distribution"></a>**Gaussian distribution** — The normal (bell-curve) distribution with density e^(−(x−μ)²/(2σ²))/(σ√(2π)); thermal noise and sums of many independent small effects follow it. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md). *See also:* [Q-function](#q-function).

<a id="gaussian-elimination"></a>**Gaussian elimination** — Solving Ax = b by subtracting multiples of rows to reach an upper-triangular system, then back-substituting; it costs about (2/3)n³ flops for an n×n system. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md). *See also:* [Pivot](#pivot), [LU factorization](#lu-factorization).

<a id="gaussian-process"></a>**Gaussian process** — A random process all of whose finite sets of samples are jointly Gaussian; it is fixed by its mean and autocorrelation, stays Gaussian through linear systems, and its uncorrelated samples are independent. *First defined in* [17-01](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-01-random-processes-and-psd.md). *See also:* [White noise](#white-noise), [Wide-sense stationary](#wide-sense-stationary).

<a id="gaussian-surface"></a>**Gaussian surface** — An imaginary closed surface chosen to apply Gauss's law, ideally one on which the field is constant and perpendicular (or parallel, carrying no flux), such as a sphere, coaxial cylinder or pillbox. *First defined in* [04-03](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-03-gauss-law.md).

<a id="generate-and-propagate"></a>**Generate and propagate** — In an adder column, generate G = AB means the column produces a carry by itself, and propagate P = A XOR B means it passes an incoming carry on, so Cout = G + P·Cin; the basis of all fast adders. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md).

<a id="generation"></a>**Generation** — The creation of electron–hole pairs, thermally (balanced by recombination in equilibrium) or by light or high fields; net generation occurs where np < n_i², as in a reverse-biased depletion region. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md). *See also:* [Recombination](#recombination).

<a id="generator-matrix"></a>**Generator matrix** — A k × n matrix G whose rows form a basis of a linear code; a message row vector m encodes as c = mG, and in systematic form G = [I | P]. *First defined in* [17-08](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-08-channel-coding.md). *See also:* [Parity-check matrix](#parity-check-matrix), [Linear block code](#linear-block-code).

<a id="geometric-distribution"></a>**Geometric distribution** — The number of independent trials up to and including the first success, with PMF (1 − q)^(k−1) q; it is memoryless. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="geometric-evaluation"></a>**Geometric evaluation** — Reading a frequency response from a pole–zero plot: |H(jω)| is the product of the distances from jω to the zeros divided by the product of the distances to the poles, and the phase is the sum of the zero angles minus the sum of the pole angles. *First defined in* [11-08](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-08-laplace-transform-and-system-functions.md). *See also:* [Poles and zeros](#poles-and-zeros), [Frequency response](#frequency-response).

<a id="geometric-mean"></a>**Geometric mean** — The nth root of the product of n numbers; used to summarize benchmark speed ratios because the ratio of two machines' geometric means does not depend on the reference machine. *First defined in* [14-01](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-01-performance-power-iron-law.md).

<a id="geometric-series"></a>**Geometric series** — Σ a r^k, which sums to a/(1 − r) for |r| < 1 and diverges otherwise; models reflections, feedback loops, digital filters and annuities. *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).

<a id="gibbs-phenomenon"></a>**Gibbs phenomenon** — The persistent overshoot, about 9 % of the jump, of truncated Fourier series near a discontinuity; it narrows but does not shrink as harmonics are added. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="gilbert-cell"></a>**Gilbert cell** — An active double-balanced mixer or multiplier in which a transconductor's output current is steered by a cross-coupled switching quad driven by the LO; introduced by Gilbert in 1968 as a four-quadrant multiplier. *First defined in* [21-05](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-05-mixers.md). *See also:* [Mixer conversion gain](#mixer-conversion-gain).

<a id="glass-core-substrate"></a>**Glass-core substrate** — A package substrate whose core is glass instead of glass-reinforced resin; flatter and stiffer with tunable expansion and fine through-glass vias, but prone to micro-cracking in drilling and dicing and not yet in volume production as of 2026. *First defined in* [25-07](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-07-advanced-packaging-and-chiplets.md).

<a id="glitch"></a>**Glitch** — A brief unintended pulse on a signal while logic settles; harmless on data sampled by flip-flops after settling, but dangerous on clocks, asynchronous resets and signals leaving the clock domain, and a waste of energy everywhere. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md).

<a id="glitch-impulse"></a>**Glitch impulse** — The area of the transient error a DAC output shows when the code changes, caused by cells switching at slightly different times; quoted in pV·s or nV·s and largest at the major carries of a binary DAC. *First defined in* [20-09](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-09-dacs.md). *See also:* [Segmentation (DAC)](#segmentation-dac).

<a id="global-history"></a>**Global history** — A shift register of the outcomes of the most recent conditional branches, used by correlating predictors such as gshare to give the same branch different predictions in different contexts. *First defined in* [14-07](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-07-branch-prediction-and-speculation.md).

<a id="gm-id-design-method"></a>**gm/ID design method** — Analog transistor sizing that chooses each device's transconductance efficiency g_m/I_D and length, takes the current from the required g_m and the width from tabulated current density; it replaces the square law with simulated device curves and does not depend on the threshold voltage. *First defined in* [20-01](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-01-analog-design-fundamentals-gm-id.md). *See also:* [Transconductance efficiency](#transconductance-efficiency), [Inversion coefficient](#inversion-coefficient), [Intrinsic gain](#intrinsic-gain).

<a id="governor-droop"></a>**Governor droop** — A generator's proportional speed regulation: a unit with droop R raises output from zero to full over a fraction R of nominal frequency, so units share load changes in proportion to rating over droop. *First defined in* [22-12](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-12-power-systems-fundamentals.md).

<a id="gradient"></a>**Gradient** — The vector of partial derivatives ∇f; it points in the direction of steepest increase, its length is that steepest rate, and it is perpendicular to level curves. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="gradient-descent"></a>**Gradient descent** — Minimizing a function by repeated steps x ← x − η∇f; stable only for step sizes below 2 divided by the largest curvature, and slow when the condition number is large. The workhorse of neural-network training. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="gradual-channel-approximation"></a>**Gradual-channel approximation** — The assumption that the potential along a MOSFET channel varies slowly compared with the vertical field, so each slice of channel behaves as a MOS capacitor biased by the local channel potential; it yields the long-channel I–V equations. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="gram-schmidt-procedure"></a>**Gram–Schmidt procedure** — Building an orthonormal basis from a set of vectors or waveforms by subtracting from each its projections onto the basis found so far and normalizing what remains; signals already in the span add no dimension. *First defined in* [17-05](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-05-matched-filters-and-detection.md). *See also:* [Signal space](#signal-space).

<a id="graphical-convolution"></a>**Graphical convolution** — Evaluating a convolution integral by flipping one signal, sliding it across the other and integrating the product over the overlap, region by region between breakpoints at the sums of the signals' edges. *First defined in* [11-03](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-03-convolution.md).

<a id="graphics-processing-unit-gpu"></a>**Graphics processing unit (GPU)** — A throughput-oriented processor with many simple cores grouped into streaming multiprocessors, which hides memory latency by running tens of thousands of threads; used for graphics, scientific computing and AI. *First defined in* [14-13](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-13-gpus-and-simt.md). *See also:* [SIMT](#simt), [Streaming multiprocessor (SM)](#streaming-multiprocessor-sm).

<a id="grating-coupler"></a>**Grating coupler** — A periodic grating etched into a waveguide that diffracts light out of the chip surface toward a fiber at a small angle, with period λ/(n_eff − sin θ); usable anywhere on the die and for wafer-level test, but its beam steers by about 0.1° per nm, limiting its bandwidth. *First defined in* [24-08](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-08-silicon-photonics.md). *See also:* [Edge coupler](#edge-coupler), [Silicon photonics](#silicon-photonics).

<a id="grating-lobe"></a>**Grating lobe** — A full-strength copy of an array's main beam that appears in visible space when the element spacing exceeds λ/(1 + |sin θ0|) for scan angle θ0; avoided by half-wavelength spacing. *First defined in* [17-11](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-11-mimo-and-beamforming.md). *See also:* [Array factor](#array-factor), [Steering vector](#steering-vector).

<a id="gray-code"></a>**Gray code** — An ordering of the 2^n bit patterns in which consecutive values differ in exactly one bit; the reflected binary Gray code is G = B XOR (B >> 1), used for encoders, for pointers that cross clock domains, and to label PAM and QAM levels so that a symbol error to a neighbour costs one bit (17-04). *First defined in* [08-01](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-01-number-systems-and-codes.md).

<a id="grid-forming-inverter"></a>**Grid-forming inverter** — An inverter controlled to set its own voltage magnitude and frequency, like a synchronous machine, rather than following the grid with a phase-locked loop; it can supply inertia-like response and support weak grids. *First defined in* [22-12](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-12-power-systems-fundamentals.md).

<a id="gross-margin"></a>**Gross margin** — (ASP − COGS)/ASP, the fraction of each sale left after the cost of making the unit; it funds R&D, sales and administration, and profit. *First defined in* [26-03](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-03-engineering-economics-1.md). *See also:* [Markup](#markup), [Cost of goods sold (COGS)](#cost-of-goods-sold-cogs).

<a id="groszkowski-frequency-shift"></a>**Groszkowski frequency shift** — The lowering of an oscillator's frequency below 1/√(LC) by the harmonic currents of its nonlinear device, about −(1/2)Σ(n² − 1)h_n² for harmonic voltage ratios h_n; −1/(8Q²) for a square-wave current. *First defined in* [21-06](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-06-oscillators-and-vcos.md). *See also:* [Describing function](#describing-function).

<a id="grounding"></a>**Grounding** — Connecting a conductor to a large charge reservoir (the earth or a circuit's ground plane) that can supply or absorb charge freely, fixing its potential and draining the charge induced on its outer surface. *First defined in* [04-03](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-03-gauss-law.md).

<a id="group-delay"></a>**Group delay** — τg = −d∠H/dω, the delay of the envelope of a narrowband signal passing through a system; constant group delay means a pulse keeps its shape. For a single pole it equals the time constant at low frequency. *First defined in* [07-07](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-07-frequency-response-and-bode-plots.md).

<a id="group-velocity"></a>**Group velocity** — The speed dω/dβ at which a narrowband signal's envelope, and its energy and information, travel; equal to the phase velocity only in a non-dispersive medium. *First defined in* [13-05](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-05-plane-waves.md). *See also:* [Phase velocity](#phase-velocity).

<a id="grouped-query-attention"></a>**Grouped-query attention** — A transformer design in which several query heads share each key–value head, shrinking the KV cache by the sharing ratio and raising decode attention's intensity to 2·(n_q/n_kv)/b_kv FLOP per byte. *First defined in* [23-01](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-01-memory-hierarchy-and-memory-wall.md). *See also:* [KV cache](#kv-cache).

<a id="gshare"></a>**gshare** — A correlating branch predictor that indexes a table of 2-bit counters by the XOR of the branch address and the global history. *First defined in* [14-07](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-07-branch-prediction-and-speculation.md). *See also:* [Global history](#global-history).

<a id="guard-band"></a>**Guard band** — Unused spectrum at the edges of a channel (in OFDM, empty subcarriers) that lets the signal's spectrum fall off before the neighbouring channel; NR's 100 MHz carrier at 30 kHz keeps 845 kHz on each side. *First defined in* [17-10](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-10-ofdm.md). *See also:* [OFDM](#ofdm).

<a id="guard-bits"></a>**Guard bits** — Extra high-order bits in an accumulator that keep a sum of many terms from overflowing; a sum of N terms needs ceil(log2 N) of them beyond the width of one term. *First defined in* [08-01](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-01-number-systems-and-codes.md). *See also:* [Fixed-point arithmetic](#fixed-point-arithmetic), [Integer overflow](#integer-overflow).

<a id="guard-ring"></a>**Guard ring** — A heavily doped diffusion ring tied to a supply around a device or block, which collects injected substrate carriers; it prevents latch-up and isolates sensitive circuits from substrate noise. *First defined in* [20-11](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-11-layout-matching-pvt.md). *See also:* [Latch-up](#latch-up).

<a id="guard-round-and-sticky-bits"></a>**Guard, round and sticky bits** — The three bits a floating-point adder keeps below the significand when aligning operands — the first two shifted-out bits plus an OR of all the rest — which suffice for correct rounding. *First defined in* [14-04](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-04-computer-arithmetic-and-number-formats.md).

<a id="guide-wavelength"></a>**Guide wavelength** — The wavelength of a mode along a waveguide, λ_g = 2π/β = λ/√(1 − (f_c/f)²), longer than the free-space wavelength and growing without limit as the frequency approaches cutoff. *First defined in* [13-10](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-10-waveguides-and-resonators.md). *See also:* [Waveguide mode](#waveguide-mode).

<a id="gummel-number"></a>**Gummel number** — The base charge integral G_B = ∫(n_i²/n_iB²)(p/D_B) dx (s/cm⁴) that sets a bipolar transistor's saturation current, I_S = qA_E n_i²/G_B; for a uniform silicon base it is the base dopant count per area divided by D_B. *First defined in* [09-07](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-07-bipolar-junction-transistor.md).

<a id="gummel-plot"></a>**Gummel plot** — A semilog plot of collector and base current against V_BE; its 60 mV/decade slopes, intercepts and the spacing between the curves give I_S, the Gummel numbers and the current gain, and show gain fall-off at low and high current. *First defined in* [09-07](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-07-bipolar-junction-transistor.md).

<a id="gustafsons-law"></a>**Gustafson's law** — The scaled speedup σ + N(1 − σ) obtained when the problem grows with the number of processors N and σ is the serial fraction of the parallel run; it grows linearly with N, unlike Amdahl's fixed-problem speedup. *First defined in* [14-01](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-01-performance-power-iron-law.md). *See also:* [Amdahl's law](#amdahls-law).

<a id="gyroscope-bias"></a>**Gyroscope bias** — A gyroscope's nonzero output at zero rotation rate; integrated, it produces an orientation error that grows linearly with time unless estimated and removed. *First defined in* [18-10](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-10-sensors.md). *See also:* [Complementary filter](#complementary-filter).

<a id="letter-h"></a>

## H

<a id="h-parameters"></a>**h-parameters** — Hybrid parameters with I1 and V2 as inputs; h11 input impedance (output shorted), h12 reverse voltage ratio, h21 forward current gain (β for a bipolar transistor, hfe), h22 output admittance (input open). *First defined in* [07-10](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-10-two-port-networks.md). *See also:* [Two-port network](#two-port-network).

<a id="h-tree"></a>**H-tree** — A recursively H-shaped clock-distribution wire pattern whose 4^k endpoints are all the same wire length from the source, giving nominally zero skew for uniformly spread sinks. *First defined in* [19-11](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-11-place-route-signoff.md). *See also:* [Clock-tree synthesis (CTS)](#clock-tree-synthesis-cts).

<a id="half-adder"></a>**Half adder** — A block that adds two bits, giving sum S = A XOR B and carry C = AB. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md). *See also:* [Full adder](#full-adder).

<a id="half-band-filter"></a>**Half-band filter** — A linear-phase low-pass filter with band edges symmetric about a quarter of the sample rate and equal ripples, whose every other tap is zero except the middle one (1/2); the standard factor-of-two decimation and interpolation stage. *First defined in* [16-09](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-09-multirate-dsp.md). *See also:* [Polyphase decomposition](#polyphase-decomposition).

<a id="half-circuit"></a>**Half-circuit** — One half of a symmetric circuit analyzed alone, using the fact that for differential signals the symmetry plane (such as a pair's tail node) is a virtual ground, and for common-mode signals each half sees twice the shared impedance. *First defined in* [12-01](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-01-differential-pairs.md). *See also:* [Differential pair](#differential-pair).

<a id="half-if-spur"></a>**Half-IF spur** — The (2, 2) spurious response at f_LO ∓ f_IF/2, where the second harmonics of the RF and LO mix to the IF; it lies close to the wanted channel and is suppressed mainly by the mixer's even-order balance. *First defined in* [21-08](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-08-transceiver-architectures.md). *See also:* [Spurious response](#spurious-response).

<a id="half-life"></a>**Half-life** — The time for an exponentially decaying quantity to halve, τ ln 2 ≈ 0.693τ; for growth the same expression is the doubling time. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md).

<a id="half-perimeter-wirelength-hpwl"></a>**Half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL)** — Half the perimeter of the smallest rectangle around a net's pins, (x_max - x_min) + (y_max - y_min): the standard placement estimate of routed length, exact for two- and three-pin nets and a lower bound otherwise. *First defined in* [19-11](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-11-place-route-signoff.md). *See also:* [Steiner tree](#steiner-tree), [Quadratic placement](#quadratic-placement).
