<a id="ionosphere-free-combination"></a>**Ionosphere-free combination** — A weighted difference of GNSS pseudoranges on two frequencies, (f₁²ρ₁ − f₂²ρ₂)/(f₁² − f₂²), that cancels the ionosphere's 1/f² delay exactly at the cost of amplifying uncorrelated noise (about 2.6 times for L1/L5). *First defined in* [21-12](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-12-modem-baseband-and-standards.md). *See also:* [Two-way ranging](#two-way-ranging).

<a id="ipc"></a>**IPC** — (Instructions per cycle.) The reciprocal of CPI; the measure quoted for processors that complete more than one instruction per cycle. *First defined in* [14-01](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-01-performance-power-iron-law.md).

<a id="ipv6"></a>**IPv6** — The successor to IPv4, with 128-bit addresses, a fixed 40-byte header, a hop limit, no fragmentation by routers, and a minimum link MTU of 1280 bytes. *First defined in* [17-13](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-13-computer-networks-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [NAT](#nat).

<a id="ir-drop"></a>**IR drop** — The voltage lost along a power-distribution network by current flowing through its resistance, so circuits far from the supply connections see less than the nominal supply voltage. *First defined in* [06-04](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-04-nodal-analysis.md). *See also:* [Electromigration](#electromigration).

<a id="iron-law-of-performance"></a>**Iron law of performance** — Execution time equals instruction count times average cycles per instruction times clock period, T = IC × CPI / f; each factor is owned by a different part of the design (compiler and ISA, microarchitecture, circuits and process). *First defined in* [14-01](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-01-performance-power-iron-law.md). *See also:* [CPI](#cpi).

<a id="iso-26262"></a>**ISO 26262** — The functional-safety standard for electrical and electronic systems in road vehicles, adapted from IEC 61508; it grades development rigour by ASIL and sets quantitative targets for random hardware faults. *First defined in* [25-10](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-10-qualification-and-functional-safety.md). *See also:* [ASIL](#asil).

<a id="iteration-bound"></a>**Iteration bound** — The fastest a recursive datapath can process samples, max over its loops of (computation time in the loop / registers in the loop); pipelining cannot beat it, only algebraic transformations such as look-ahead. *First defined in* [16-11](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-11-dsp-hardware-architectures.md). *See also:* [Look-ahead transformation](#look-ahead-transformation), [Pipelining](#pipelining).

<a id="iterative-refinement"></a>**Iterative refinement** — Improving a computed solution of Ax = b by computing the residual r = b − Ax in higher precision, solving A d = r with the existing (often low-precision) factors, and updating x ← x + d; it converges when κ·u_low is well below 1. *First defined in* [02-10](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-10-numerical-methods.md).

<a id="i-c"></a>**I²C** — A two-wire, open-drain, multi-drop serial bus (SCL clock, SDA data) with pull-up resistors, 7-bit addresses, per-byte acknowledges, clock stretching and arbitration; standard, fast and fast-mode-plus speeds of 100 kbit/s, 400 kbit/s and 1 Mbit/s. *First defined in* [18-05](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-05-gpio-uart-spi-i2c.md). *See also:* [I3C](#i3c), [Open-drain output](#open-drain-output).

<a id="i-v-characteristic"></a>**i–v characteristic** — The plot of all (voltage, current) pairs an element permits; a resistor's is a line through the origin, an ideal voltage source's a vertical line, an ideal current source's a horizontal line. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md).

<a id="letter-j"></a>

## J

<a id="jacobian"></a>**Jacobian** — The determinant of the matrix of partial derivatives of a change of variables; its magnitude is the local area or volume scale factor, r for polar and ρ² sin φ for spherical coordinates. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="jeita-charging-guidelines"></a>**JEITA charging guidelines** — Japanese industry safety guidelines (2007) that set lithium-ion charge current and voltage by cell temperature: reduced current when cold, reduced charge voltage when warm, no charging outside the limits. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md).

<a id="jensens-inequality"></a>**Jensen's inequality** — For a convex function g, E[g(X)] ≥ g(E[X]); averaging through an exponential or square law raises the result, so leakage or failure rate at the average input underestimates the average. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="jitter"></a>**Jitter** — The deviation of a signal's edges from their ideal times, split into unbounded Gaussian random jitter (RJ) and bounded deterministic jitter (DJ). *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md). *See also:* [Dual-Dirac model](#dual-dirac-model).

<a id="jitter-tolerance"></a>**Jitter tolerance** — The largest sinusoidal jitter a receiver tolerates at each frequency at its BER target; for a first-order CDR with corner f_c and eye margin M it is M·√(1 + (f_c/f)²), rising 20 dB/decade below f_c and flat above. *First defined in* [24-02](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-02-eye-diagrams-jitter-ber.md). *See also:* [Clock and data recovery (CDR)](#clock-and-data-recovery-cdr), [Jitter](#jitter).

<a id="jitter-transfer"></a>**Jitter transfer** — The closed-loop transfer T = L/(1 + L) of a PLL or clock-recovery loop from input (reference) jitter to output jitter; low-pass, with peaking near the loop bandwidth that shrinks as phase margin grows and adds in decibels along a chain of identical stages. *First defined in* [15-12](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-12-control-applications-pll-regulators-thermal.md). *See also:* [Phase-locked loop (PLL)](#phase-locked-loop-pll), [Jitter](#jitter).

<a id="jk-flip-flop"></a>**JK flip-flop** — A flip-flop whose inputs J and K hold (00), reset (01), set (10) or toggle (11) the output at the clock edge, Q⁺ = JQ̄ + K̄Q; in standard-cell chips it is a D flip-flop with logic in front. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md). *See also:* [T flip-flop](#t-flip-flop), [Excitation table](#excitation-table).

<a id="johnson-counter"></a>**Johnson counter** — A twisted-ring counter that feeds the complement of its last stage back to its first, giving 2n states from n flip-flops with one bit changing per step. *First defined in* [08-07](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-07-registers-counters-shift-registers.md). *See also:* [Ring counter](#ring-counter).

<a id="joint-distribution"></a>**Joint distribution** — The joint PMF p(x, y) or PDF f(x, y) of two or more random variables, giving the probability of any combination of values; marginals alone do not determine it. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="jointly-gaussian"></a>**Jointly Gaussian** — Variables whose joint density is the multivariate normal; their marginals and linear combinations are Gaussian, and for them uncorrelated means independent. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="joule-heating"></a>**Joule heating** — The conversion of electrical energy to heat in a resistance, P = I²R = V²/R, or locally p = J · E = ρJ² per unit volume. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="jump-conditions"></a>**Jump conditions** — The values an impulse imposes at t = 0⁺ on an Nth-order differential equation's solution; only the highest derivative contains the impulse, so the next lower derivative jumps by the impulse weight over the leading coefficient and lower derivatives are continuous. *First defined in* [11-04](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-04-lti-systems-and-differential-equations.md).

<a id="jump-discontinuity"></a>**Jump discontinuity** — A point where both one-sided limits exist but differ, as for the unit step at t = 0 or a capacitor's current at a switching instant. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="junction-capacitance"></a>**Junction capacitance** — The small-signal capacitance of a reverse-biased junction, ε/W per unit area, from charge uncovered at the depletion edges; about 1 fF/µm² at W = 0.1 µm, falling with reverse bias. *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md). *See also:* [C–V profiling](#c-v-profiling).

<a id="junction-temperature"></a>**Junction temperature** — The temperature of a chip's active devices (T_J), the quantity reliability and performance limits are set on; it exceeds the case and ambient temperatures by the heat flow times the thermal resistances in between. *First defined in* [15-01](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-01-modeling-dynamic-systems.md).

<a id="junction-voltage-limiting"></a>**Junction voltage limiting** — A Newton-iteration safeguard in SPICE device models that compresses large steps in a pn-junction voltage above a critical voltage to a logarithmic step, preventing the exponential current law from overflowing or stalling convergence. *First defined in* [02-10](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-10-numerical-methods.md).

<a id="jupyter-notebook"></a>**Jupyter notebook** — A document (.ipynb, stored as JSON) of Markdown and code cells whose code runs in a separate kernel process; it saves outputs with the code, so a saved notebook shows results that may not match a fresh run. *First defined in* [05-04](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-04-reproducible-workflows.md). *See also:* [Hidden state](#hidden-state).

<a id="jury-stability-test"></a>**Jury stability test** — An algebraic test, the discrete counterpart of Routh–Hurwitz, for whether all roots of a polynomial in z lie inside the unit circle; for z² + a₁z + a₀ it reduces to |a₀| < 1 and 1 ± a₁ + a₀ > 0. *First defined in* [15-11](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-11-digital-control.md). *See also:* [Stability triangle](#stability-triangle).

<a id="letter-k"></a>

## K

<a id="k-factor-method"></a>**K-factor method** — A compensator design rule that places the zeros a factor k below and the poles a factor k above the crossover frequency, choosing k from the required phase boost. *First defined in* [22-07](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-07-converter-dynamics-and-control.md).

<a id="k-induction"></a>**k-induction** — A proof method that combines a BMC base case (no violation within k − 1 steps) with an inductive step (any k consecutive states satisfying the property are followed by one that does); counterexamples to induction from unreachable states require a larger k or a strengthening lemma. *First defined in* [19-13](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-13-verification-methods.md). *See also:* [Bounded model checking (BMC)](#bounded-model-checking-bmc), [Model checking](#model-checking).

<a id="k1-factor"></a>**k1 factor** — The process-dependent constant in the lithography resolution formula CD = k₁λ/NA; it bundles illumination, mask, resist and layout effects, with a physical floor of 0.25 for dense lines and spaces. *First defined in* [25-02](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-02-lithography.md). *See also:* [Numerical aperture](#numerical-aperture), [Off-axis illumination](#off-axis-illumination).

<a id="kahan-summation"></a>**Kahan summation** — Compensated summation that carries each addition's rounding error forward in a correction variable, giving an error bound independent of the number of terms at four operations per element. *First defined in* [14-04](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-04-computer-arithmetic-and-number-formats.md). *See also:* [Pairwise summation](#pairwise-summation).

<a id="kaiser-window"></a>**Kaiser window** — A window w[n] = I0(β√(1 − ((n − M/2)/(M/2))²))/I0(β) whose parameter β trades sidelobe level against main-lobe width continuously; Kaiser's formulas give β and the order M from an attenuation and a transition width. *First defined in* [16-06](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-06-fir-filter-design.md). *See also:* [Window method (FIR design)](#window-method-fir-design).

<a id="kalman-filter"></a>**Kalman filter** — The optimal linear estimator of a state-space system's state from noisy measurements (Kalman, 1960), alternating model-based prediction with measurement correction; widely used in navigation, tracking and sensor fusion. *First defined in* [02-09](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-09-systems-of-odes-and-matrix-exponential.md).

<a id="karnaugh-map"></a>**Karnaugh map** — A truth table drawn as a grid whose rows and columns are labelled in Gray code, so that cells differing in one variable are adjacent (including across the edges); rectangles of 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 cells are product terms. *First defined in* [08-03](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-03-logic-minimization.md). *See also:* [Prime implicant](#prime-implicant), [Gray code](#gray-code).

<a id="keeper"></a>**Keeper** — A weak PMOS from the supply to a dynamic node, gated by the node's inverted value, that replaces charge lost to leakage and noise while the node is high. It must be weak enough that the pull-down network still wins when it discharges the node. *First defined in* [19-03](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-03-logic-families.md). *See also:* [Dynamic logic](#dynamic-logic).

<a id="kernel-gpu"></a>**Kernel (GPU)** — A function launched on a GPU over a grid of thread blocks, each thread running the same code on its own data. *First defined in* [14-13](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-13-gpus-and-simt.md). *See also:* [SIMT](#simt).

<a id="kickback"></a>**Kickback** — The disturbance a latched comparator's internal voltage swings couple back to its inputs through the input devices' gate capacitances; it can upset the source (a capacitive DAC or reference ladder) before the next decision. *First defined in* [20-05](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-05-comparators-and-sample-and-hold.md). *See also:* [StrongARM latch](#strongarm-latch).

<a id="kinetic-energy"></a>**Kinetic energy** — The energy of motion, ½mv² for translation and ½Iω² for rotation; by the work–energy theorem, net work equals its change. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="kirchhoffs-current-law-kcl"></a>**Kirchhoff's current law (KCL)** — The algebraic sum of the currents entering a node is zero at every instant; it follows from charge conservation and the lumped assumption that nodes store no charge. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md). *See also:* [Kirchhoff's voltage law (KVL)](#kirchhoffs-voltage-law-kvl), [Lumped-matter discipline](#lumped-matter-discipline).

<a id="kirchhoffs-voltage-law-kvl"></a>**Kirchhoff's voltage law (KVL)** — The algebraic sum of the voltages around any loop is zero at every instant; it follows from Faraday's law when no changing magnetic flux links the loop outside the elements. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md). *See also:* [Kirchhoff's current law (KCL)](#kirchhoffs-current-law-kcl), [Lumped-matter discipline](#lumped-matter-discipline).

<a id="kirk-effect"></a>**Kirk effect** — Base push-out at high current density, when mobile electrons in the collector depletion region cancel its donor charge near J = qN_C v_sat; the effective base widens, the transit time rises and f_T and gain collapse. *First defined in* [09-07](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-07-bipolar-junction-transistor.md).

<a id="known-good-die-kgd"></a>**Known-good die (KGD)** — A die tested and confirmed good before assembly into a stack or package; because a stack's yield is the product of its dies' yields, HBM depends on testing every die (and every finished stack) first. *First defined in* [23-05](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-05-hbm-in-depth.md). *See also:* [High Bandwidth Memory (HBM)](#high-bandwidth-memory-hbm).

<a id="kogge-stone-adder"></a>**Kogge–Stone adder** — A parallel-prefix adder with the minimum log2 n levels and fan-out 1, at the cost of about n log2 n operators and many long wires. *First defined in* [08-09](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-09-arithmetic-circuits.md). *See also:* [Parallel-prefix adder](#parallel-prefix-adder), [Brent–Kung adder](#brent-kung-adder).

<a id="kraft-inequality"></a>**Kraft inequality** — The condition Σ 2^(−ℓi) ≤ 1 that binary codeword lengths ℓi must satisfy for a prefix code with those lengths to exist. *First defined in* [17-07](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-07-information-theory-and-shannon.md). *See also:* [Prefix code](#prefix-code).

<a id="kronig-penney-model"></a>**Kronig–Penney model** — An exactly solvable model of an electron in a one-dimensional periodic array of square barriers whose dispersion relation, cos kd = F(E), shows how allowed bands and forbidden gaps arise; energies with |F(E)| ≤ 1 are allowed. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md). *See also:* [Bloch's theorem](#blochs-theorem), [Energy band](#energy-band).

<a id="ktc-noise"></a>**kT/C noise** — The thermal noise sampled onto a capacitor through any resistance, with RMS value √(kT/C), about 64 µV for 1 pF at 300 K; independent of the resistance. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="kv-cache"></a>**KV cache** — The stored keys and values of every earlier token in a transformer's context, 2·L·n_kv·d_h bytes-per-element per token; decoding reads it all for each new token, and unlike the weights it is not shared across a batch, so it caps decode intensity. *First defined in* [23-01](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-01-memory-hierarchy-and-memory-wall.md). *See also:* [Grouped-query attention](#grouped-query-attention), [Decode and prefill](#decode-and-prefill).

<a id="letter-l"></a>

## L

<a id="lhopitals-rule"></a>**L'Hopital's rule** — For 0/0 or ∞/∞ forms, lim f/g = lim f'/g' when the latter exists (named for L'Hôpital); other indeterminate forms are first rewritten as quotients. *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md).

<a id="l-network"></a>**L-network** — A two-element matching network with one series and one shunt reactance; matching R_high to R_low needs Q = √(R_high/R_low − 1), X = Q·R_low and B = Q/R_high, with low-pass and high-pass forms. *First defined in* [13-09](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-09-smith-chart-and-matching.md). *See also:* [Impedance matching](#impedance-matching), [Quality factor](#quality-factor).

<a id="l-section-match"></a>**L-section match** — A lossless two-element network (a series reactance next to the lower resistance and a shunt reactance across the higher) that transforms one resistance into another at one frequency; its Q is √(R_high/R_low − 1). *First defined in* [07-10](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-10-two-port-networks.md). *See also:* [Mismatch loss](#mismatch-loss).

<a id="ladder-filter"></a>**Ladder filter** — A band-pass filter of alternating series and shunt resonators, the shunt ones tuned so their anti-resonance meets the series ones' resonance at the band centre; the shunt series resonance and the series anti-resonance form notches on each side, limiting the bandwidth to about twice the resonance spacing. *First defined in* [21-09](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-09-rf-front-end.md). *See also:* [Butterworth-Van Dyke model](#butterworth-van-dyke-model), [Electromechanical coupling coefficient](#electromechanical-coupling-coefficient).

<a id="lag-compensator"></a>**Lag compensator** — C(s) = (1 + s/z)/(1 + s/p) with z > p, a pole followed by a zero; placed about a decade below crossover, it raises the low-frequency loop gain (and the error constants) by z/p at a cost of a few degrees of phase and a slow settling tail. *First defined in* [15-09](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-09-lead-lag-compensation.md). *See also:* [Lead compensator](#lead-compensator), [Pole–zero doublet](#pole-zero-doublet).

<a id="lagrange-multiplier"></a>**Lagrange multiplier** — The factor λ in ∇f = λ∇g at a constrained optimum; it equals the rate of change of the optimal value with the constraint level, a shadow price. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="lagrange-remainder"></a>**Lagrange remainder** — The error of a degree-n Taylor polynomial, f^(n+1)(ξ)(x − a)^(n+1)/(n + 1)! for some ξ between a and x; bounding f^(n+1) bounds the error. *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).

<a id="lambertian-emitter"></a>**Lambertian emitter** — A surface whose luminance is the same from every viewing angle, so its intensity per unit area falls as the cosine of the angle from the normal; its total luminous flux is pi times its luminance times its area. *First defined in* [27-03](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-03-wearables-smartwatch.md). *See also:* [Luminance](#luminance).

<a id="landauer-limit"></a>**Landauer limit** — The minimum energy to erase one bit of information, kT ln 2 (about 2.9×10^−21 J at 300 K); practical logic uses orders of magnitude more. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="lane-serial-link"></a>**Lane (serial link)** — One pair of differential signal pairs (transmit and receive) of a serial link such as PCIe; links bundle 1 to 16 lanes, and bandwidth scales with the lane count. *First defined in* [14-11](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-11-io-buses-and-interconnect.md). *See also:* [PCI Express (PCIe)](#pci-express-pcie).

<a id="laplace-transform"></a>**Laplace transform** — F(s) = ∫ f(t) e^(−st) dt from 0⁻ to ∞, with s = σ + jω complex; it turns differentiation into multiplication by s (minus initial conditions), so linear constant-coefficient ODEs become algebra. *First defined in* [02-05](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-05-laplace-transform-for-odes.md). *See also:* [Transfer function](#transfer-function), [Partial fractions](#partial-fractions).

<a id="laplaces-equation"></a>**Laplace's equation** — The equation del-squared V = 0 obeyed by the electrostatic potential in a charge-free uniform region; its solutions have no interior maxima or minima, each point being the average of its surroundings. *First defined in* [13-02](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-02-electrostatics-boundary-value-problems.md). *See also:* [Poisson's equation](#poissons-equation), [Uniqueness theorem](#uniqueness-theorem).

<a id="laplacian"></a>**Laplacian** — The divergence of the gradient, ∇²V; in Cartesian coordinates the sum of second partial derivatives. Laplace's equation ∇²V = 0 governs potential in charge-free regions; the vector Laplacian is ∇(∇·A) − ∇×∇×A. *First defined in* [13-01](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-01-vector-calculus-refresher.md). *See also:* [Gradient](#gradient), [Divergence](#divergence).

<a id="latch-inference"></a>**Latch inference** — Synthesis creating a latch because a combinational block leaves an output unassigned on some path, so the output must hold its previous value; prevented by default assignments, complete case/if statements or always_comb. *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md).

<a id="latch-up"></a>**Latch-up** — The triggering of the parasitic PNPN thyristor formed by the wells and diffusions of a CMOS process, which shorts the supply until power is removed. *First defined in* [20-11](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-11-layout-matching-pvt.md). *See also:* [Guard ring](#guard-ring).

<a id="late-stage-reprojection"></a>**Late-stage reprojection** — Re-sampling a finished frame with the newest head pose just before it is scanned out, so rendering and network delays no longer add registration error (also called timewarp). *First defined in* [27-04](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-04-wearables-earbuds-and-glasses.md). *See also:* [Motion-to-photon latency](#motion-to-photon-latency), [Split rendering](#split-rendering).

<a id="latency"></a>**Latency** — The delay between an input event and the corresponding output; a filter that needs M future samples can only run in real time delayed by M samples, so a symmetric N-tap FIR filter has a latency of (N − 1)/2 samples. *First defined in* [11-02](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-02-system-properties.md).

<a id="latent-fault"></a>**Latent fault** — A multiple-point fault that is neither detected by a safety mechanism nor perceived by the driver, typically a fault in a safety mechanism itself; it violates nothing until a second fault arrives. *First defined in* [25-10](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-10-qualification-and-functional-safety.md). *See also:* [Latent-fault metric (LFM)](#latent-fault-metric-lfm).

<a id="latent-fault-metric-lfm"></a>**Latent-fault metric (LFM)** — One minus the fraction of the remaining (non-single-point, non-residual) failure rate that is latent; ISO 26262 targets are at least 60%, 80% and 90% for ASIL B, C and D. *First defined in* [25-10](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-10-qualification-and-functional-safety.md). *See also:* [Latent fault](#latent-fault).

<a id="laterally-excited-bulk-wave-resonator-xbar"></a>**Laterally excited bulk-wave resonator (XBAR)** — A resonator made from a suspended thin lithium-niobate platelet driven by interdigitated electrodes in a shear bulk mode, giving coupling near 25 percent for wide filters at 3 to 6 GHz; first published in 2019, with production reliability still being demonstrated in 2025. *First defined in* [21-09](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-09-rf-front-end.md). *See also:* [Electromechanical coupling coefficient](#electromechanical-coupling-coefficient), [Bulk acoustic wave (BAW) resonator](#bulk-acoustic-wave-baw-resonator).

<a id="lattice-filter"></a>**Lattice filter** — A modular filter structure built stage by stage from reflection coefficients; an FIR lattice realizes A(z), an all-pole lattice 1/A(z), and the filter is stable exactly when every reflection coefficient has magnitude below 1. *First defined in* [16-08](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-08-filter-structures.md). *See also:* [Reflection coefficient (lattice filter)](#reflection-coefficient-lattice-filter).

<a id="lattice-mismatch"></a>**Lattice mismatch** — The fractional difference f = (a_layer − a_substrate)/a_substrate between the lattice constants of an epitaxial layer and its substrate; 4.2% for Ge on Si, 0.14% for AlAs on GaAs. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md). *See also:* [Epitaxy](#epitaxy).

<a id="law-of-large-numbers"></a>**Law of large numbers** — The sample mean of independent, identically distributed variables converges to their expectation as the sample grows; its standard error falls like σ/√n. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="law-of-mass-action"></a>**Law of mass action** — In equilibrium, np = n_i², independent of doping, because thermal generation of electron–hole pairs balances their recombination, which is proportional to np; it fails under illumination or current. *First defined in* [09-02](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-02-carriers-doping-fermi-level.md).

<a id="law-of-the-junction"></a>**Law of the junction** — The boundary condition that the minority-carrier density at each depletion edge equals its equilibrium value times e^(qV_A/kT), because the quasi-Fermi levels stay flat across the depletion region; the starting point of the diode equation. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md). *See also:* [Quasi-Fermi level](#quasi-fermi-level), [Ideal diode equation](#ideal-diode-equation).

<a id="law-of-total-variance"></a>**Law of total variance** — Var(Y) = E[Var(Y | X)] + Var(E[Y | X]): the average spread within groups plus the spread of the group means. Explains why mixed wafers, lots or tools vary far more than any one group. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="layer-mimo"></a>**Layer (MIMO)** — In 3GPP terminology, one spatially multiplexed data stream; NR maps one codeword onto up to four layers and two codewords onto five to eight downlink layers. *First defined in* [17-11](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-11-mimo-and-beamforming.md). *See also:* [Spatial multiplexing](#spatial-multiplexing).

<a id="layout-versus-schematic-lvs"></a>**Layout versus schematic (LVS)** — Automated verification that the circuit extracted from a layout (devices and their connections) matches the intended schematic or netlist, catching shorts, opens and wrong devices that geometric checks cannot. *First defined in* [19-09](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-09-layout-and-standard-cells.md). *See also:* [Design-rule check (DRC)](#design-rule-check-drc).

<a id="lc3-codec"></a>**LC3 codec** — The low-complexity communication codec of LE Audio, coding audio in fixed frames of 7.5 or 10 ms at sample rates up to 48 kHz with a frame size set by the bit rate. *First defined in* [27-04](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-04-wearables-earbuds-and-glasses.md). *See also:* [LE Audio](#le-audio).

<a id="lcr-meter"></a>**LCR meter** — An instrument that measures a component's complex impedance at a chosen test frequency and level and reports it through a two-element series or parallel model (Cs–Rs, Cp–Rp, Ls–Rs, Lp–Rp, D, Q). *First defined in* [07-05](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-05-sinusoidal-steady-state-and-impedance.md).

<a id="ldpc-code"></a>**LDPC code** — A low-density parity-check code, a linear code with a sparse parity-check matrix, decoded by iterative belief propagation; long LDPC codes operate within a fraction of a decibel of capacity and are used in 5G NR data channels, Wi-Fi and DVB-S2. *First defined in* [17-08](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-08-channel-coding.md). *See also:* [Tanner graph](#tanner-graph), [Belief propagation](#belief-propagation), [Parity-check matrix](#parity-check-matrix).

<a id="le-audio"></a>**LE Audio** — Audio over Bluetooth Low Energy using isochronous channels and the LC3 codec, with connected streams to earbuds and hearing aids and broadcast streams to any number of listeners. *First defined in* [27-04](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-04-wearables-earbuds-and-glasses.md). *See also:* [LC3 codec](#lc3-codec), [Connected isochronous stream (CIS)](#connected-isochronous-stream-cis), [Auracast](#auracast).

<a id="lead-compensator"></a>**Lead compensator** — C(s) = (1 + αTs)/(1 + Ts) with α > 1, a zero followed by a pole; it adds up to arcsin((α − 1)/(α + 1)) of phase at ω_m = 1/(T√α), used to raise phase margin and crossover. It is a PD controller with a filtering pole. *First defined in* [15-09](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-09-lead-lag-compensation.md). *See also:* [Lag compensator](#lag-compensator), [Phase margin](#phase-margin).

<a id="leaf-spine-fabric"></a>**Leaf–spine fabric** — A two-tier folded-Clos network in which every leaf switch connects to every spine switch, so any two hosts are at most two switch hops apart through a leaf, a spine and a leaf. *First defined in* [24-05](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-05-pcie-cxl-ethernet.md). *See also:* [Switch radix](#switch-radix).

<a id="leakage-current"></a>**Leakage current** — Current that flows through transistors (and other devices) when they are nominally off; it grows roughly exponentially with temperature and with lower threshold voltages, and dominates a sleeping chip's consumption. *First defined in* [18-09](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-09-ultra-low-power-design.md). *See also:* [Dynamic power](#dynamic-power).

<a id="leakage-inductance"></a>**Leakage inductance** — The part of a winding's inductance whose flux does not link the other winding (k < 1); it appears in series in a transformer's equivalent circuit and causes load-dependent voltage drop. *First defined in* [07-09](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-09-mutual-inductance-and-transformers.md). *See also:* [Coupling coefficient](#coupling-coefficient).

<a id="least-recently-used-lru"></a>**Least recently used (LRU)** — A replacement policy that evicts the block in the set that has gone longest without being accessed; real caches often approximate it (pseudo-LRU). *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Set-associative cache](#set-associative-cache).

<a id="least-significant-bit-lsb"></a>**Least significant bit (LSB)** — The smallest step an N-bit converter resolves, full scale / 2^N; errors and noise are often expressed in LSBs. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="least-squares"></a>**Least squares** — Choosing x̂ to minimize ‖b − Ax‖² when Ax = b has no exact solution; geometrically, Ax̂ is the projection of b onto the column space, so the residual is orthogonal to every column. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md). *See also:* [Normal equations](#normal-equations), [Projection](#projection).

<a id="lees-rule"></a>**Lee's rule** — An empirical stability guideline for single-bit delta-sigma loops limiting the NTF's peak out-of-band gain (to 2 in Lee's 1987 form, about 1.5 in practice); neither necessary nor sufficient. *First defined in* [20-08](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-08-sigma-delta-converters.md). *See also:* [Noise transfer function (NTF)](#noise-transfer-function-ntf).

<a id="legalization"></a>**Legalization** — The placement step that moves cells from their continuous global-placement positions into legal sites in standard-cell rows without overlap, disturbing the placement as little as possible. *First defined in* [19-11](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-11-place-route-signoff.md). *See also:* [Quadratic placement](#quadratic-placement).

<a id="lele-litho-etch-litho-etch"></a>**LELE (litho-etch-litho-etch)** — Multipatterning by splitting a layer into two interleaved patterns, each exposed and etched separately; it halves the pitch at the cost of a second mask and an overlay error between the two sets. *First defined in* [25-02](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-02-lithography.md). *See also:* [Overlay](#overlay).

<a id="lenzs-law"></a>**Lenz's law** — The induced current flows so as to oppose the change in flux that produced it (the minus sign in Faraday's law), a consequence of energy conservation. *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="level-curve"></a>**Level curve** — The set of points where a function of two variables takes a constant value; a contour line. The gradient is perpendicular to it. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="level-shifter"></a>**Level shifter** — A circuit that translates logic levels between two voltage domains so that families with incompatible thresholds can communicate. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="liberty"></a>**Liberty** — The standard text format for standard-cell library models: each cell's function, area, pin capacitances, timing tables, power and design-rule limits, characterized at one process-voltage-temperature corner per file. Maintained by an industry advisory board under IEEE-ISTO. *First defined in* [19-10](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-10-synthesis-and-sta.md). *See also:* [Nonlinear delay model (NLDM)](#nonlinear-delay-model-nldm), [Timing arc](#timing-arc).

<a id="lifetime-killing"></a>**Lifetime killing** — The deliberate shortening of minority-carrier lifetime, by deep-level impurities such as gold or platinum or by irradiation, to speed the turn-off of power diodes and IGBTs at the cost of higher leakage. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="limit"></a>**Limit** — The value L that f(x) approaches as x approaches a (without equaling a), written lim_{x→a} f(x) = L; the value f(a) itself plays no role. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md). *See also:* [One-sided limit](#one-sided-limit), [Continuity](#continuity).

<a id="limit-comparison-test"></a>**Limit comparison test** — If a_k, b_k > 0 and a_k/b_k tends to a finite positive limit, the series Σ a_k and Σ b_k converge or diverge together. *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).

<a id="limit-cycle"></a>**Limit cycle** — A small sustained oscillation in a fixed-point recursive filter with zero or constant input, caused by rounding inside the feedback loop; it cannot occur in the exact linear system. *First defined in* [11-04](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-04-lti-systems-and-differential-equations.md). *See also:* [IIR filter](#iir-filter).

<a id="limited-buffer-rate-matching"></a>**Limited-buffer rate matching** — An NR rule that caps the coded bits a receiver must store per code block at the information bits divided by R_LBRM = 2/3, so the soft buffer holds 1.5 coded bits per information bit rather than the mother code's three (LDPC base graph 1; five for base graph 2). *First defined in* [21-12](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-12-modem-baseband-and-standards.md). *See also:* [Soft buffer](#soft-buffer).

<a id="limiter"></a>**Limiter** — A circuit, also called a clipper, that holds its output below (or above) a set level, typically with diodes from the signal to a reference; the limiting is soft because the diode is exponential. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="line-and-phase-quantities"></a>**Line and phase quantities** — Line voltages are between lines and line currents flow in them; phase quantities belong to each source or load element. In Y, V_L = √3 V_p (leading by 30°) and I_L = I_p; in Δ, V_L = V_p and I_L = √3 I_p. *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md).

<a id="line-code"></a>**Line code** — The mapping of bits to transmitted levels and pulses, chosen for DC balance, enough transitions for clock recovery and limited bandwidth; examples are NRZ, AMI, Manchester and block codes such as 8b/10b, 64b/66b and 128b/130b. *First defined in* [17-04](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-04-baseband-digital-transmission.md). *See also:* [Manchester code](#manchester-code), [Baseline wander](#baseline-wander), [Scrambler](#scrambler).

<a id="line-integral"></a>**Line integral** — The integral of a vector field's component along a path, ∫ F · dr; for a force it is work, for an electric field it is (minus) the voltage difference. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md). *See also:* [Vector field](#vector-field).

<a id="line-regulation"></a>**Line regulation** — The change in a regulator's output per unit change in its input voltage; r_z/(R + r_z) for a Zener shunt regulator. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="line-spectrum"></a>**Line spectrum** — The plot of a periodic signal's Fourier coefficients (magnitude and phase) against frequency; it consists of lines at the harmonic frequencies only. *First defined in* [11-05](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-05-fourier-series.md).

<a id="linear-block-code"></a>**Linear block code** — A block code in which the XOR of any two codewords is a codeword, so the code is a k-dimensional subspace described by a generator matrix G and a parity-check matrix H. *First defined in* [17-08](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-08-channel-coding.md). *See also:* [Generator matrix](#generator-matrix), [Parity-check matrix](#parity-check-matrix), [Syndrome](#syndrome).

<a id="linear-charger"></a>**Linear charger** — A battery charger whose pass transistor drops the input-to-battery voltage difference while carrying the charge current; efficiency V_bat/V_in, so it suits low currents and uses thermal regulation. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md).

<a id="linear-combination"></a>**Linear combination** — A sum c₁v₁ + … + c_kv_k of vectors times scalars. Every matrix–vector product Ax is the linear combination of A's columns with weights x. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="linear-element"></a>**Linear element** — An element whose i–v characteristic is a straight line through the origin (v = Ri); sources, whose lines miss the origin, and diodes are not linear in this sense. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md).

<a id="linear-independence"></a>**Linear independence** — Vectors are independent if the only combination of them equal to 0 has all weights zero; otherwise one of them is a combination of the others. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md).

<a id="linear-phase"></a>**Linear phase** — A frequency response whose phase is −ωτ (plus a constant or sign flips at zeros), so every frequency is delayed by the same τ; a real FIR filter with symmetric or antisymmetric taps has it exactly, with τ = (N − 1)/2 samples. *First defined in* [11-07](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-07-discrete-time-fourier-transform.md). *See also:* [Group delay](#group-delay), [Distortionless transmission](#distortionless-transmission).

<a id="linear-pluggable-optics-lpo"></a>**Linear pluggable optics (LPO)** — A pluggable optical module with linear drivers, optics and TIAs but no DSP or clock recovery; the host switch's SerDes equalizes the whole link, saving module power at the cost of link margin and host–module co-qualification. Specified by the LPO MSA (100G-DR-LPO, 400G-FR4-LPO). *First defined in* [24-09](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-09-lpo-and-cpo.md). *See also:* [Linear receive optics (LRO)](#linear-receive-optics-lro), [Pluggable transceiver](#pluggable-transceiver).

<a id="linear-receive-optics-lro"></a>**Linear receive optics (LRO)** — A half-retimed pluggable: the module keeps a DSP in its transmit path but passes received signals linearly to the host, giving roughly half of LPO's power saving with a cleaner transmitted signal; argued to be the near-term choice at 200 Gb/s per lane. *First defined in* [24-09](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-09-lpo-and-cpo.md). *See also:* [Linear pluggable optics (LPO)](#linear-pluggable-optics-lpo).

<a id="linear-region"></a>**Linear region** — The MOSFET operating region with V_DS below V_Dsat, where I_D = (W/L)μC_ox(V_GS − V_TH − mV_DS/2)V_DS and the device acts as a voltage-controlled resistor for small V_DS (also called the triode region). *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="linear-regulator"></a>**Linear regulator** — A regulator that drops the excess voltage across a series pass device controlled by feedback; its input current equals the load current plus its quiescent current, so its efficiency cannot exceed V_out/V_in. *First defined in* [22-01](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-01-power-conversion-principles.md). *See also:* [Low-dropout regulator (LDO)](#low-dropout-regulator-ldo), [Switching converter](#switching-converter).

<a id="linear-feedback-shift-register-lfsr"></a>**Linear-feedback shift register (LFSR)** — A shift register whose input is the XOR of selected stages (the taps); with taps from a primitive polynomial it steps through all 2^n - 1 nonzero states before repeating. *First defined in* [08-07](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-07-registers-counters-shift-registers.md). *See also:* [Primitive polynomial](#primitive-polynomial), [Pseudo-random bit sequence (PRBS)](#pseudo-random-bit-sequence-prbs).

<a id="linearity"></a>**Linearity** — The property of a system whose response obeys homogeneity and additivity; circuits of resistors, dependent sources, capacitors and inductors are linear, diodes and transistors (beyond small signals) are not. *First defined in* [06-07](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-07-linearity-and-superposition.md). *See also:* [Homogeneity](#homogeneity), [Superposition](#superposition).

<a id="linearity-of-expectation"></a>**Linearity of expectation** — E[aX + bY + c] = aE[X] + bE[Y] + c for any random variables, independent or not; it gives expected counts as sums of probabilities. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md). *See also:* [Indicator variable](#indicator-variable).

<a id="linearization"></a>**Linearization** — Replacing a function near a point by its tangent line, L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x − a); the error grows as the square of the distance from a. *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md). *See also:* [Small-signal model](#small-signal-model).

<a id="linearly-graded-junction"></a>**Linearly graded junction** — A junction whose net doping varies linearly through it, N_D − N_A = ax; its depletion width grows as the cube root of the voltage, W = (12ε(V_bi − V_A)/(qa))^(1/3). *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="link-adaptation"></a>**Link adaptation** — Choosing the modulation and code rate for each transmission from reported channel quality, typically aiming at around 10% block errors that HARQ repairs. *First defined in* [17-12](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-12-multiple-access-and-cellular-wifi.md). *See also:* [Hybrid ARQ (HARQ)](#hybrid-arq-harq).

<a id="link-budget"></a>**Link budget** — The ledger, in dB, of a radio link from transmit power through antenna gains, path loss, environment losses and receive losses to the received power, compared with the receiver's sensitivity plus a margin; it tells whether a link closes and by how much. *First defined in* [21-11](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-11-link-budgets.md). *See also:* [Maximum allowable path loss (MAPL)](#maximum-allowable-path-loss-mapl), [Fade margin](#fade-margin).

<a id="link-margin"></a>**Link margin** — Received power minus receiver sensitivity, in dB; the extra loss a radio link can tolerate before it fails. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md).

<a id="link-level-retry"></a>**Link-level retry** — Resending a unit the receiver's CRC rejects, from a replay buffer in the transmitter; it costs latency only when an error occurs, so PCIe pairs it with a light FEC instead of a strong, slow one. *First defined in* [24-04](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-04-dsp-serdes-and-fec.md). *See also:* [Flit](#flit), [Forward error correction (FEC)](#forward-error-correction-fec).

<a id="linked-list"></a>**Linked list** — A sequence of separately allocated nodes, each pointing to the next; O(1) insertion and removal next to a known node, O(n) search, and poor cache behavior compared with arrays. *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="linker"></a>**Linker** — The build stage that combines object files and libraries into one executable, connecting each use of a function or variable to its single definition; a missing definition gives an "undefined reference" error. *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md).

<a id="linker-relaxation"></a>**Linker relaxation** — A RISC-V linker optimization that shrinks long instruction sequences once final addresses are known, such as replacing an AUIPC + JALR call with a single JAL when the target is within ±1 MiB. *First defined in* [14-03](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-03-assembly-and-the-compilation-stack.md).

<a id="linker-script"></a>**Linker script** — The file that tells the linker which memory regions exist and where each output section goes, including load and run addresses, alignment, exported symbols and size checks; the memory map expressed in software. *First defined in* [18-02](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-02-bare-metal-c-and-toolchain.md). *See also:* [Linker](#linker), [Startup code](#startup-code).

<a id="linting"></a>**Linting** — Static checking of source code for suspicious constructs (width mismatches, inferred latches, unused signals, incomplete sensitivity lists) without simulating it; Verilator's --lint-only mode is a widely used HDL linter. *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md).

<a id="list-comprehension"></a>**List comprehension** — A one-expression loop that builds a list, such as [r \* 1000 for r in values if r > 0]; dict and set comprehensions work the same way. *First defined in* [05-01](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-01-python-fundamentals.md).

<a id="lithium-plating"></a>**Lithium plating** — Deposition of metallic lithium on a graphite anode when lithium arrives faster than it can intercalate, worst at low temperature and high charge rate; it loses capacity and can grow into an internal short. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md).

<a id="litmus-test"></a>**Litmus test** — A tiny multithreaded program, such as store buffering or message passing, whose allowed final outcomes characterize a memory consistency model. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Memory consistency model](#memory-consistency-model).

<a id="littles-law"></a>**Little's law** — For any stable queueing system, average occupancy = throughput × average time in the system; it sizes a processor's window (about width × latency to hide) and the outstanding requests a memory system needs. *First defined in* [14-08](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-08-out-of-order-and-superscalar.md).

<a id="litz-wire"></a>**Litz wire** — Wire made of many fine, individually insulated strands twisted so that each strand takes every position in the bundle, which keeps skin and proximity losses low at high frequency. *First defined in* [22-05](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-05-magnetics-design.md). *See also:* [Proximity effect](#proximity-effect).

<a id="llc-converter"></a>**LLC converter** — A resonant converter whose bridge drives a series inductor and capacitor and a transformer's magnetizing inductance near the tank's resonant frequency, giving a gain near the turns ratio and zero-voltage switching from the magnetizing current. *First defined in* [22-06](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-06-converter-losses-and-wide-bandgap.md). *See also:* [Zero-voltage switching](#zero-voltage-switching).

<a id="lo-leakage"></a>**LO leakage** — Carrier feedthrough at the LO frequency in a direct-conversion transmitter, set by baseband DC offsets and mixer imbalance, about 20 log(V_DC/V_signal) relative to the wanted output; in receivers, LO coupling to the input that self-mixes to DC. *First defined in* [21-08](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-08-transceiver-architectures.md). *See also:* [Direct-conversion (zero-IF) receiver](#direct-conversion-zero-if-receiver).

<a id="load-and-run-addresses"></a>**Load and run addresses** — The two addresses of a section: where its bytes are stored in the image (load address, LMA) and where the program uses it (run address, VMA); for .data the first is in flash and the second in SRAM, and the startup code copies between them. *First defined in* [18-02](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-02-bare-metal-c-and-toolchain.md). *See also:* [Linker script](#linker-script), [Startup code](#startup-code).

<a id="load-factor"></a>**Load factor** — For a hash table, entries divided by slots (α = n/m); linear probing needs about ½(1 + 1/(1 − α)) probes per successful search and ½(1 + 1/(1 − α)²) per miss, so tables resize before α reaches about 0.75. *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="load-line"></a>**Load line** — The straight line i = (V_Th − v)/R_Th that a linear network imposes on the device it drives; the operating point is where it crosses the device's characteristic. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="load-line-voltage-regulator"></a>**Load line (voltage regulator)** — A deliberately finite DC loop gain in a processor voltage regulator (adaptive voltage positioning), so the output behaves as a small resistance R_LL = ΔV/ΔI; it removes overshoot on load release and lets each transient use the whole tolerance band. *First defined in* [15-12](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-12-control-applications-pll-regulators-thermal.md). *See also:* [Target impedance](#target-impedance).

<a id="load-modulation"></a>**Load modulation** — Changing the load impedance a transistor sees as the signal level changes, by injecting current from a second device into a shared node; the principle behind the Doherty and outphasing amplifiers. *First defined in* [21-07](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-07-power-amplifiers.md). *See also:* [Doherty amplifier](#doherty-amplifier).

<a id="load-regulation"></a>**Load regulation** — The change in a regulator's output per unit change in load current, equal to minus its output resistance; −(R ∥ r_z) for a Zener shunt regulator. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="load-switch"></a>**Load switch** — An integrated MOSFET switch with its gate driver and controlled turn-on, used to connect or disconnect a power rail from a load while limiting inrush current. *First defined in* [10-02](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-02-mosfet-dc-operation-and-biasing.md).

<a id="load-pull"></a>**Load-pull** — Measuring a transistor's output power, efficiency and linearity while a tuner sweeps the load impedance, to find the optimum load that the matching network must then present. *First defined in* [21-07](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-07-power-amplifiers.md). *See also:* [Load line](#load-line).

<a id="load-reserved-store-conditional-lr-sc"></a>**Load-reserved/store-conditional (LR/SC)** — A pair of atomic instructions: LR loads a word and registers a reservation, and SC stores only if the reservation is still valid, reporting success or failure, so that a short retry loop implements any atomic update. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Spin lock](#spin-lock).

<a id="load-use-hazard"></a>**Load-use hazard** — A data hazard in which an instruction uses the result of the load just before it; the data arrives too late even for forwarding, so the pipeline stalls one cycle unless the compiler schedules an independent instruction in between. *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md).

<a id="loaded-cost"></a>**Loaded cost** — The full cost of an employee to the company per period, including salary, benefits, taxes, tools, facilities and overhead, not just salary. *First defined in* [26-06](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-06-team-structures-and-sizing.md).

<a id="loaded-q"></a>**Loaded Q** — The quality factor of a resonator as used, including the source and load resistances in parallel (or series) with its own losses; always below the unloaded Q, so the bandwidth f0/Q_L is wider than the resonator alone gives. *First defined in* [07-08](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-08-filters-and-resonance.md). *See also:* [Quality factor](#quality-factor), [Insertion loss](#insertion-loss).

<a id="loader"></a>**Loader** — The part of the operating system that maps an executable's code and data into a process's memory, sets up its stack and jumps to its entry point; on a bare microcontroller, start-up code plays this role. *First defined in* [14-03](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-03-assembly-and-the-compilation-stack.md).

<a id="loading-effect"></a>**Loading effect** — The drop in a source's or divider's output when a load draws current from it; the relative error is about R_source/R_load when the load is much larger. *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="loading-factor"></a>**Loading factor** — An ADC's full-scale amplitude divided by the RMS of a noise-like input, k = V_FS/σ; it trades clipping noise (small k) against granular quantization noise (large k). *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="load-store-architecture"></a>**Load–store architecture** — An ISA in which arithmetic operates only on registers and memory is accessed only by explicit load and store instructions (RISC-V, Arm), in contrast to ISAs such as x86 whose arithmetic can read or write memory directly. *First defined in* [14-02](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-02-isa-risc-v-arm-x86.md).

<a id="local-oscillator-lo"></a>**Local oscillator (LO)** — The periodic signal a mixer multiplies the input by; its frequency sets the translation, and its phase noise, harmonics and leakage become the mixer's. *First defined in* [21-05](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-05-mixers.md). *See also:* [Mixer](#mixer).

<a id="locality"></a>**Locality** — The tendency of programs to reuse data and instructions they accessed recently (temporal locality) and to access addresses near recent ones (spatial locality); the property every cache relies on. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Cache block](#cache-block).

<a id="lockstep"></a>**Lockstep** — Running two identical processor cores on the same instructions, often offset in time and separated physically, with a comparator that flags any difference; a common safety mechanism with very high diagnostic coverage. *First defined in* [25-10](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-10-qualification-and-functional-safety.md). *See also:* [Diagnostic coverage](#diagnostic-coverage).

<a id="log-likelihood-ratio-llr"></a>**Log-likelihood ratio (LLR)** — L = ln[P(b = 0)/P(b = 1)] for a bit b: its sign is the decision and its magnitude the confidence; for BPSK in Gaussian noise L = 2y/σ², and independent evidence adds. *First defined in* [17-08](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-08-channel-coding.md). *See also:* [Soft decision](#soft-decision), [Belief propagation](#belief-propagation).

<a id="log-log-plot"></a>**Log-log plot** — A graph with both axes logarithmic; a power law y = kxⁿ plots as a straight line of slope n. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md).

<a id="log-normal-distribution"></a>**Log-normal distribution** — The distribution of e^X for Gaussian X; skewed right, with median e^μ and mean e^(μ + σ_ℓ²/2), where σ_ℓ is the standard deviation of X. Subthreshold leakage across devices is approximately log-normal. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="logarithmic-differentiation"></a>**Logarithmic differentiation** — Differentiating ln y instead of y, which turns products, quotients and variable exponents into sums; for example (x^x)' = x^x(1 + ln x). *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="logic-equivalence-checking-lec"></a>**Logic equivalence checking (LEC)** — Formal proof that two versions of a design (RTL and synthesized netlist, or netlists before and after an ECO) compute the same function, usually by matching registers and checking the combinational logic between them. *First defined in* [19-13](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-13-verification-methods.md). *See also:* [Miter](#miter), [Formal verification](#formal-verification).

<a id="logic-synthesis"></a>**Logic synthesis** — Automatic translation of a register-transfer-level description into an optimized netlist of library cells, by elaboration, technology-independent optimization, technology mapping and timing-driven refinement. *First defined in* [08-03](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-03-logic-minimization.md). *See also:* [Technology mapping](#technology-mapping), [And-inverter graph (AIG)](#and-inverter-graph-aig).

<a id="logical-effort"></a>**Logical effort** — How much more input capacitance a gate presents than an inverter delivering the same output current: 1 for an inverter, (n + 2)/3 for an n-input NAND and (2n + 1)/3 for an n-input NOR when the PMOS is twice as wide as the NMOS. Also the name of the sizing method built on it. *First defined in* [19-04](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-04-sizing-and-logical-effort.md). *See also:* [Electrical effort](#electrical-effort), [Parasitic delay](#parasitic-delay), [Path effort](#path-effort).

<a id="logistic-equation"></a>**Logistic equation** — N' = rN(1 − N/K), growth proportional to the current base and to the remaining room; its S-shaped solution models adoption, epidemics and populations, rising fastest at N = K/2. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="longest-prefix-match"></a>**Longest-prefix match** — The forwarding rule that a router uses the most specific (longest) table prefix containing the destination address. *First defined in* [17-13](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-13-computer-networks-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Subnet mask and CIDR](#subnet-mask-and-cidr).

<a id="look-ahead-transformation"></a>**Look-ahead transformation** — Rewriting a recursion by substituting it into itself, e.g. y[n] = a²y[n − 2] + a x[n − 1] + x[n], so the feedback loop contains more registers and can be pipelined; it costs extra feed-forward arithmetic. *First defined in* [16-11](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-11-dsp-hardware-architectures.md). *See also:* [Iteration bound](#iteration-bound).

<a id="lookup-table-lut"></a>**Lookup table (LUT)** — A small memory of 2^k configuration bits selected by k inputs, able to implement any k-input function; the basic logic element of FPGAs (usually k = 4 or 6). *First defined in* [08-11](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-11-memories-and-programmable-logic.md). *See also:* [Field-programmable gate array (FPGA)](#field-programmable-gate-array-fpga), [Shannon expansion](#shannon-expansion).

<a id="loop"></a>**Loop** — Any closed path through the branches of a circuit that visits no node more than once. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md).

<a id="loop-analysis"></a>**Loop analysis** — The generalization of mesh analysis to any circuit; one loop current per link of a spanning tree (b − n + 1 fundamental loops), with KVL written around each loop. *First defined in* [06-05](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-05-mesh-analysis.md). *See also:* [Spanning tree](#spanning-tree), [Mesh analysis](#mesh-analysis).

<a id="loop-gain"></a>**Loop gain** — The product Aβ of forward gain and feedback fraction around a feedback loop; the closed-loop gain error is about 1/(Aβ). *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).

<a id="loop-tiling"></a>**Loop tiling** — Restructuring loops to work on blocks (tiles) of data small enough to stay in a cache while they are reused, also called blocking; the key optimization of dense linear algebra. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Locality](#locality).

<a id="loop-unrolling-dfe"></a>**Loop unrolling (DFE)** — Speculative DFE: each slicer is duplicated for every possible value of the previous symbol and the previous decision selects the right result, removing the summer from the one-UI feedback loop; one tap costs M(M − 1) comparators (2 for NRZ, 12 for PAM4). *First defined in* [24-03](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-03-serdes-architecture.md). *See also:* [Decision-feedback equalizer (DFE)](#decision-feedback-equalizer-dfe).

<a id="lora"></a>**LoRa** — Semtech's chirp-spread-spectrum modulation, in which each symbol is a frequency sweep across the bandwidth carrying SF bits in 2^SF chips; LoRaWAN is the network protocol built on it. *First defined in* [27-08](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-08-edge-ai-and-iot.md). *See also:* [Spreading factor (LoRa)](#spreading-factor-lora), [Low-power wide-area network (LPWAN)](#low-power-wide-area-network-lpwan).

<a id="lorentz-force"></a>**Lorentz force** — The total electromagnetic force on a charge, F = q(E + v × B); the magnetic part is perpendicular to the velocity and does no work. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="loss-budget"></a>**Loss budget** — An allocation of a link's allowed insertion loss at its Nyquist frequency among packages, traces, vias, connectors and cables, such as PCIe 5.0's 36 dB at 16 GHz. *First defined in* [24-01](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-01-signal-integrity-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Insertion loss](#insertion-loss), [Nyquist frequency](#nyquist-frequency).

<a id="loss-tangent"></a>**Loss tangent** — tan δ, the ratio of a dielectric's lossy to stored response; it makes waves decay at about πf√ε_r tan δ / c nepers per meter, about 0.025 for FR-4-class laminates and 0.004 for low-loss ones at 10 GHz. *First defined in* [04-08](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-08-maxwell-preview.md).

<a id="lot-tolerance-percent-defective-ltpd"></a>**Lot tolerance percent defective (LTPD)** — The defective percentage that a sampling plan rejects with high confidence (usually 90%); zero failures in 230 samples demonstrates LTPD 1. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="low-dropout-regulator-ldo"></a>**Low-dropout regulator (LDO)** — A linear regulator that can regulate with a small difference between input and output; its input current equals its output current plus a quiescent current, so its efficiency is at most V_out/V_in. *First defined in* [18-09](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-09-ultra-low-power-design.md). *See also:* [Quiescent current](#quiescent-current).

<a id="low-if-receiver"></a>**Low-IF receiver** — A quadrature receiver that converts to an IF of about one channel bandwidth, avoiding DC offsets and most flicker noise; its image is the adjacent channel, which I/Q matching and complex filtering must reject. *First defined in* [21-08](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-08-transceiver-architectures.md). *See also:* [Complex filter](#complex-filter), [Direct-conversion (zero-IF) receiver](#direct-conversion-zero-if-receiver).

<a id="low-k-dielectric"></a>**Low-k dielectric** — An interconnect insulator with permittivity below SiO₂'s 3.9 (SiOF, carbon-doped SiOCH at 2.7–3.0, porous films below 2.5, air gaps at 1), used to cut wire capacitance, delay and power. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md).

<a id="low-level-injection"></a>**Low-level injection** — The condition that excess carrier densities are much smaller than the majority density, so the majority density is essentially unchanged and recombination is linear in the excess, U = Δp/τ. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="low-noise-amplifier-lna"></a>**Low-noise amplifier (LNA)** — The first amplifier after a receiver's antenna or filter, designed for the lowest noise figure at a defined input impedance (usually 50 Ω), with enough gain to make the following stages' noise negligible and enough linearity to tolerate blockers. *First defined in* [21-04](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-04-low-noise-amplifiers.md). *See also:* [Noise figure](#noise-figure), [Inductive source degeneration](#inductive-source-degeneration), [Noise-cancelling LNA](#noise-cancelling-lna).

<a id="low-power-wide-area-network-lpwan"></a>**Low-power wide-area network (LPWAN)** — A radio network for small, infrequent messages over kilometres at very low energy per message, such as LoRaWAN, Sigfox, NB-IoT and LTE-M, trading data rate and latency for range and battery life. *First defined in* [27-08](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-08-edge-ai-and-iot.md). *See also:* [LoRa](#lora), [Time on air](#time-on-air).

<a id="low-rank-approximation"></a>**Low-rank approximation** — Keeping the first k terms of the SVD, A_k = Σ_{i≤k} σᵢuᵢvᵢᵀ, the closest rank-k matrix to A (Eckart–Young), with 2-norm error σ_{k+1}. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="low-voltage-swing-terminated-logic-lvstl"></a>**Low-voltage-swing terminated logic (LVSTL)** — LPDDR4 and LPDDR5 signaling terminated to ground with an I/O supply of about 0.5 V (0.3 V without termination); termination power falls with the square of the supply. *First defined in* [23-04](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-04-dram-interfaces.md). *See also:* [Pseudo-open-drain (POD) I/O](#pseudo-open-drain-pod-i-o).

<a id="lti-system"></a>**LTI system** — A system that is both linear and time-invariant; it is completely described by its impulse response (convolution) and passes complex exponentials unchanged in shape, only scaled. *First defined in* [11-02](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-02-system-properties.md).

<a id="ltpo-backplane"></a>**LTPO backplane** — A display backplane that combines low-temperature polysilicon transistors (high mobility, used to drive pixel current) with oxide-semiconductor switches (very low leakage, used to hold each pixel's voltage), so the panel can refresh as slowly as about 1 Hz. *First defined in* [27-03](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-03-wearables-smartwatch.md). *See also:* [Always-on display (AOD)](#always-on-display-aod).

<a id="lu-factorization"></a>**LU factorization** — A = LU, with L lower triangular holding the elimination multipliers and U upper triangular holding the pivots (PA = LU with row exchanges). Factor once in O(n³), then solve each right-hand side in O(n²). *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="luminance"></a>**Luminance** — Luminous intensity per unit projected area of a surface in a given direction, in candela per square metre (cd/m², also called nits); the quantity a display's brightness is specified in. *First defined in* [27-03](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-03-wearables-smartwatch.md). *See also:* [Lambertian emitter](#lambertian-emitter), [Luminous efficacy](#luminous-efficacy).

<a id="luminous-efficacy"></a>**Luminous efficacy** — Light output in lumens (power weighted by the eye's sensitivity) per watt; 683 lm/W at 555 nm, and about 414 lm/W at most for white light with good color rendering. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="luminous-efficacy-of-radiation"></a>**Luminous efficacy of radiation** — The luminous flux per watt of radiant power for a given spectrum, in lumens per watt; at most 683 lm/W (monochromatic light at 540 THz, the SI definition), lower for broad white spectra; it converts lux to irradiance. *First defined in* [27-08](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-08-edge-ai-and-iot.md). *See also:* [Energy harvesting](#energy-harvesting).

<a id="lumped-matter-discipline"></a>**Lumped-matter discipline** — The conditions under which fields can be replaced by voltages and currents in lumped elements obeying KVL and KCL, chiefly that the circuit is small compared with the signal wavelength (or line delay is short compared with edge time). *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md). *See also:* [Transmission line](#transmission-line), [Wavelength](#wavelength).

<a id="letter-m"></a>

## M

<a id="m-psk"></a>**M-PSK** — M points equally spaced on a circle; minimum distance 2√Es·sin(π/M) and Ps ≈ 2Q(√(2Es/N0)·sin(π/M)); constant symbol envelope but poor distance beyond 8 points. *First defined in* [17-06](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-06-bandpass-digital-modulation.md). *See also:* [QPSK](#qpsk), [QAM](#qam).

<a id="mac-address"></a>**MAC address** — The 48-bit link-layer address of a network interface, used by Ethernet and Wi-Fi to deliver frames within a LAN. *First defined in* [17-13](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-13-computer-networks-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Ethernet frame](#ethernet-frame), [ARP](#arp).

<a id="machine-balance"></a>**Machine balance** — A machine's peak compute divided by its memory bandwidth (FLOP per byte), equal to the roofline's ridge point; it has risen for decades because compute outgrows bandwidth. *First defined in* [23-01](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-01-memory-hierarchy-and-memory-wall.md). *See also:* [Ridge point](#ridge-point), [Memory wall](#memory-wall).

<a id="machine-epsilon"></a>**Machine epsilon** — The gap between 1 and the next representable floating-point number, 2^−52 ≈ 2.22×10^−16 for IEEE 754 double precision; the relative precision of a computation. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="mach-zehnder-modulator"></a>**Mach–Zehnder modulator** — An interferometric modulator that splits light into two arms, shifts their relative phase electro-optically and recombines them, giving P_out = P_in cos²(Δφ/2); usually biased at quadrature. *First defined in* [24-07](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-07-photonics-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Half-wave voltage (Vπ)](#half-wave-voltage-v).

<a id="magic-voltage"></a>**Magic voltage** — The output of a first-order bandgap reference at its zero-temperature-coefficient temperature, V_g0 + (η − m)V_T, independent of saturation current, bias current and resistor values; production tests trim the output to it at one temperature, which removes PTAT-shaped errors at all temperatures. *First defined in* [20-03](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-03-bandgap-references.md). *See also:* [Bandgap reference](#bandgap-reference), [PTAT voltage](#ptat-voltage).

<a id="magnetic-circuit"></a>**Magnetic circuit** — A path of high-permeability material that guides magnetic flux, analysed like a resistive circuit with magnetomotive force as the source, flux as the current and reluctance as the resistance; an air gap usually dominates its reluctance. *First defined in* [13-03](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-03-magnetostatics-and-inductance.md). *See also:* [Reluctance](#reluctance), [Magnetomotive force](#magnetomotive-force).

<a id="magnetic-dipole-moment"></a>**Magnetic dipole moment** — m = NIA for a current loop (A·m²), pointing along the loop's normal; in a field it feels torque m × B and has energy −m · B, and far away it makes a 1/r³ dipole field. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).
