<a id="phase-shedding"></a>**Phase shedding** — Turning off phases of a multiphase converter at light load; each phase adds a fixed loss while N phases divide the conduction loss by N, so N + 1 phases pay above I = √(N(N + 1)P₀/R). *First defined in* [22-01](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-01-power-conversion-principles.md). *See also:* [Pulse-frequency modulation (PFM)](#pulse-frequency-modulation-pfm).

<a id="phase-velocity"></a>**Phase velocity** — The speed ω/β at which points of constant phase move; 1/√(µε) in a lossless medium, and frequency-dependent (dispersive) in conductors, waveguides and real dielectrics. *First defined in* [13-05](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-05-plane-waves.md). *See also:* [Group velocity](#group-velocity).

<a id="phase-based-ranging"></a>**Phase-based ranging** — Measuring distance from the round-trip phase of tones at several frequencies, d = cΔφ/(4πΔf); Bluetooth Channel Sounding uses up to 72 tones at 1 MHz spacing, giving a 150 m unambiguous range and about 2 m multipath resolution. *First defined in* [21-12](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-12-modem-baseband-and-standards.md). *See also:* [Two-way ranging](#two-way-ranging).

<a id="phase-change-memory-pcm"></a>**Phase-change memory (PCM)** — Memory storing a bit in a chalcogenide's crystalline (low-resistance) or amorphous (high-resistance) phase, switched by melt-quench (RESET) and anneal (SET) heat pulses. *First defined in* [23-08](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-08-emerging-memories.md). *See also:* [Resistance drift](#resistance-drift).

<a id="phase-frequency-detector"></a>**Phase-frequency detector** — A PLL block that compares the edges of the reference and the divided output and drives the charge pump up or down for the time between them; it detects frequency as well as phase, so the loop acquires lock from any initial frequency. *First defined in* [20-10](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-10-plls-and-jitter.md). *See also:* [Charge pump](#charge-pump), [Phase-locked loop (PLL)](#phase-locked-loop-pll).

<a id="phase-gate-process"></a>**Phase-gate process** — A process in which a project passes formal decision reviews (gates) between phases, where management decides to continue, change course or stop; chip programs place gates such as specification freeze and tape-out where the cost of change jumps. *First defined in* [26-01](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-01-requirements-and-specifications.md). *See also:* [Specification freeze](#specification-freeze), [Tape-out](#tape-out).

<a id="phase-locked-loop-pll"></a>**Phase-locked loop (PLL)** — A feedback loop that locks an oscillator's phase to a reference, usually multiplying its frequency by a divider ratio N; in the linear phase-domain model the VCO is an integrator of phase, and with a charge pump and an RC loop filter the loop is type 2. *First defined in* [15-12](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-12-control-applications-pll-regulators-thermal.md). *See also:* [Voltage-controlled oscillator](#voltage-controlled-oscillator), [Charge pump (PLL)](#charge-pump-pll), [Jitter transfer](#jitter-transfer).

<a id="phased-array"></a>**Phased array** — A row or grid of antennas fed with progressive phase steps so their waves add in a chosen direction, sin θ = Δφ/(kd); steers beams electronically and needs spacing near λ/2 to avoid grating lobes. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="phasor"></a>**Phasor** — The complex number V = V_m∠φ representing the sinusoid V_m cos(ωt + φ) at a known frequency ω, so that v(t) = Re{V e^{jωt}}. This curriculum uses peak-amplitude, cosine-reference phasors. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Sinusoidal steady state](#sinusoidal-steady-state), [Impedance](#impedance).

<a id="phasor-diagram"></a>**Phasor diagram** — A drawing of a circuit's voltage and current phasors as arrows in the complex plane; KVL makes the voltage arrows around a loop close into a polygon. *First defined in* [07-05](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-05-sinusoidal-steady-state-and-impedance.md).

<a id="phonon"></a>**Phonon** — A quantum of lattice vibration; phonons carry heat, scatter electrons (raising a metal's resistance with temperature) and supply the crystal momentum for light absorption or emission in indirect-gap semiconductors. *First defined in* [04-11](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-11-intro-solid-state-physics.md).

<a id="photoconductive-decay"></a>**Photoconductive decay** — A lifetime measurement that excites carriers with a light pulse and records the exponential decay of the excess conductivity; it reports an effective lifetime that includes surface recombination. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="photoelectric-effect"></a>**Photoelectric effect** — Ejection of electrons from a surface by light, which occurs only if each photon's energy exceeds the work function; the maximum kinetic energy hf − φ grows with frequency, not intensity. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="photon"></a>**Photon** — The quantum of light, a packet of energy E = hf = hc/λ (1239.84 eV·nm divided by the wavelength) and momentum h/λ; light is emitted and absorbed one photon at a time. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="photon-detection-efficiency"></a>**Photon detection efficiency** — The probability that a photon arriving at a single-photon detector produces a counted avalanche (PDE), including absorption, triggering probability and fill factor. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="photonic-integrated-circuit-pic"></a>**Photonic integrated circuit (PIC)** — A chip whose waveguides, splitters, modulators and detectors route and convert light, as a printed circuit board routes current; it is paired with an electronic die (EIC) of drivers and TIAs, monolithically, stacked in 3D or side by side. *First defined in* [24-08](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-08-silicon-photonics.md). *See also:* [Silicon photonics](#silicon-photonics), [Hybrid bonding](#hybrid-bonding).

<a id="photoplethysmography-ppg"></a>**Photoplethysmography (PPG)** — Optical measurement of blood-volume changes: an LED illuminates tissue and a photodiode measures the light returned, whose small pulsatile part follows the heartbeat; used for heart rate and, with red and infrared light, blood-oxygen saturation. *First defined in* [18-10](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-10-sensors.md). *See also:* [Perfusion index](#perfusion-index).

<a id="physical-design"></a>**Physical design** — Converting synthesized logic into a manufacturable layout (floorplanning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing) and closing timing, power and design-rule signoff. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="physical-unclonable-function-puf"></a>**Physical unclonable function (PUF)** — A circuit whose response depends on uncontrollable manufacturing variation, such as the power-up state of SRAM cells, used to derive a device-unique key that is never stored; its noisy readout needs error correction and helper data. *First defined in* [18-11](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-11-hardware-security.md). *See also:* [Secure element](#secure-element).

<a id="physical-vapour-deposition-pvd"></a>**Physical vapour deposition (PVD)** — Deposition by sputtering atoms off a target with plasma ions; line-of-sight arrival makes it fast but poorly conformal; used for barriers, liners and seed layers. *First defined in* [25-03](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-03-deposition-etch-cmp-implant-metrology.md).

<a id="pi-network"></a>**Pi network** — A three-element matching network of a shunt, a series and a shunt reactance; viewed as two back-to-back L-networks through a virtual resistance, it lets the designer choose the loaded Q independently of the resistance ratio. *First defined in* [21-02](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-02-impedance-matching-networks.md). *See also:* [L-network](#l-network).

<a id="pid-controller"></a>**PID controller** — A controller whose output is a weighted sum of the error, its integral and its derivative, u = K_p e + K_i ∫e dt + K_d de/dt, or in standard form K_p(1 + 1/(T_i s) + T_d s); in practice the derivative is filtered and actuator limits are handled with anti-windup. *First defined in* [15-08](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-08-pid-control.md). *See also:* [Integral action](#integral-action), [Integrator windup](#integrator-windup).

<a id="piecewise-linear-diode-model"></a>**Piecewise-linear diode model** — A diode model that is open when off and a voltage V_D0 in series with a resistance r_D when on, fitted to the exponential curve near the expected current. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="pierce-oscillator"></a>**Pierce oscillator** — The standard crystal-oscillator circuit, an inverting amplifier with the crystal from output to input and a capacitor from each end to ground; it presents the crystal with a load capacitance and a negative resistance -g_m/(omega^2 C1 C2) that must exceed the crystal's ESR by a safety factor. *First defined in* [12-09](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-09-oscillators.md). *See also:* [Negative resistance](#negative-resistance), [Barkhausen criterion](#barkhausen-criterion).

<a id="piezoelectric-polarization"></a>**Piezoelectric polarization** — Electric polarization created by mechanical strain in a piezoelectric crystal; in AlGaN grown on GaN it adds to the spontaneous polarization and increases the 2DEG density. *First defined in* [09-13](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-13-compound-and-wide-bandgap-semiconductors.md).

<a id="pilot"></a>**Pilot** — A known symbol (reference signal) inserted on some time-frequency resources so the receiver can estimate the channel; its spacing must be below the coherence bandwidth in frequency and the coherence time in time. *First defined in* [17-10](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-10-ofdm.md). *See also:* [Coherence bandwidth](#coherence-bandwidth), [Coherence time](#coherence-time).

<a id="pinch-off"></a>**Pinch-off** — The vanishing of a MOSFET's inversion charge at the drain end of the channel when V_DS reaches V_Dsat; beyond it, the extra drain voltage drops across a short depleted region that carriers cross at high field. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="ping-pong-buffering"></a>**Ping-pong buffering** — Double buffering for streams: a DMA fills one buffer while the CPU processes the other, then they swap; safe when service latency plus processing time fits in one block time, N >= (a + L) fs / (1 - b fs). *First defined in* [18-04](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-04-dma-and-data-movement.md). *See also:* [Direct memory access (DMA)](#direct-memory-access-dma), [Circular buffer](#circular-buffer).

<a id="pipeline-adc"></a>**Pipeline ADC** — An ADC built from cascaded stages, each of which resolves a few bits, subtracts them and passes an amplified residue to the next stage; every stage works on a different sample, so throughput is one sample per clock. *First defined in* [20-07](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-07-nyquist-adcs.md). *See also:* [Residue](#residue), [Multiplying DAC (MDAC)](#multiplying-dac-mdac).

<a id="pipeline-hazard"></a>**Pipeline hazard** — A situation in which the next instruction cannot execute in the following cycle without giving a wrong result — a data, control or structural hazard — resolved by forwarding, stalling or flushing (distinct from a logic hazard, a glitch). *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md). *See also:* [Data hazard](#data-hazard), [Control hazard](#control-hazard), [Structural hazard](#structural-hazard).

<a id="pipeline-parallelism"></a>**Pipeline parallelism** — Placing consecutive layers of a model on different devices and streaming micro-batches through them; activations pass point to point between stages, and idle bubbles of (p − 1)/(m + p − 1) of the time arise for p stages and m micro-batches. *First defined in* [27-07](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-07-ai-datacenter-server-and-rack.md). *See also:* [Tensor parallelism](#tensor-parallelism).

<a id="pipeline-register"></a>**Pipeline register** — The register between two pipeline stages that holds an instruction's data and control signals from one clock edge to the next; its clock-to-Q and setup time are the pipeline's per-stage overhead. *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md). *See also:* [Pipelining](#pipelining).

<a id="pipelined-fft"></a>**Pipelined FFT** — A streaming FFT architecture with one butterfly per stage and delay lines between stages, taking one sample per clock; the radix-2 single-path delay-feedback (R2SDF) form uses log₂N butterflies, log₂N − 2 general multipliers and N − 1 words of delay. *First defined in* [16-04](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-04-the-fft.md). *See also:* [Fast Fourier transform (FFT)](#fast-fourier-transform-fft).

<a id="pipelining"></a>**Pipelining** — Inserting registers to split long combinational paths into stages, raising the clock rate and throughput at the cost of latency and register overhead. *First defined in* [08-10](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-10-timing-metastability-cdc.md).

<a id="pitch-walk"></a>**Pitch walk** — The alternating-space error of spacer patterning: a mandrel width error δ makes neighbouring spaces differ by 2δ. *First defined in* [25-02](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-02-lithography.md).

<a id="pivot"></a>**Pivot** — The diagonal entry used to eliminate the entries below it at each step of Gaussian elimination; it must be nonzero, and should not be small relative to the entries below it. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="placement"></a>**Placement** — The implementation step that assigns every primitive of a synthesized netlist to a physical site on the chip, keeping connected and timing-critical cells close; often randomized, so results depend on a seed. *First defined in* [08-12](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-12-fpga-implementation-flow.md). *See also:* [Routing](#routing).

<a id="planar-circuit"></a>**Planar circuit** — A circuit that can be drawn on a plane with no crossing branches; only planar circuits have meshes. By Kuratowski's theorem a circuit is planar unless it contains a subdivision of K5 or K3,3. *First defined in* [06-05](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-05-mesh-analysis.md). *See also:* [Mesh](#mesh), [Loop analysis](#loop-analysis).

<a id="planar-magnetics"></a>**Planar magnetics** — Inductors and transformers with flat windings made from PCB layers or stamped copper on low-profile cores, giving repeatable leakage and capacitance and a low height. *First defined in* [22-05](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-05-magnetics-design.md).

<a id="plant"></a>**Plant** — In control engineering, the system being controlled (a motor, a heater, a converter, a chip's thermal path), described by a model of how its outputs respond to its inputs. *First defined in* [15-01](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-01-modeling-dynamic-systems.md). *See also:* [State-space model](#state-space-model).

<a id="platform-team"></a>**Platform team** — A shared team that builds IP, methodology or tools used by several product programs; the organizational form of reuse. *First defined in* [26-06](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-06-team-structures-and-sizing.md).

<a id="pluggable-transceiver"></a>**Pluggable transceiver** — A self-contained optical module in a standard form factor (OSFP, QSFP-DD) that plugs into a switch or network card's front panel; a retimed module contains a DSP, drivers, optics and TIAs and runs at about 20 pJ/bit at 800 Gb/s and 1.6 Tb/s. *First defined in* [24-08](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-08-silicon-photonics.md). *See also:* [Retiming](#retiming), [Co-packaged optics](#co-packaged-optics).

<a id="pmhf"></a>**PMHF** — Probabilistic metric for random hardware failures: the average rate at which random hardware faults violate a safety goal, with targets below 100 FIT for ASIL B and C and below 10 FIT for ASIL D. *First defined in* [25-10](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-10-qualification-and-functional-safety.md). *See also:* [Single-point fault metric (SPFM)](#single-point-fault-metric-spfm).

<a id="pn-junction"></a>**PN junction** — The boundary between p-type and n-type regions of one crystal, where carrier diffusion leaves a depleted layer of fixed ions, an internal field and a built-in potential; the basis of diodes, bipolar transistors and the source and drain of MOSFETs. *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md). *See also:* [Depletion region](#depletion-region), [Built-in potential](#built-in-potential).

<a id="pointer"></a>**Pointer** — A variable holding a memory address, with a type saying what is stored there (int \*p points to an int); &x gives an address and \*p the object at it. Pointers let functions modify caller data and pass buffers without copying. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md). *See also:* [Dereference](#dereference), [Null pointer](#null-pointer), [Pointer arithmetic](#pointer-arithmetic).

<a id="pointer-arithmetic"></a>**Pointer arithmetic** — Adding an integer to a pointer advances it by whole elements (sizeof the pointed-to type), so a[i] is \*(a + i); subtracting two pointers into one array gives the number of elements between them. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="poisson-distribution"></a>**Poisson distribution** — The count of rare independent events with mean λ: P(k) = e^(−λ) λ^k/k!, the limit of the binomial as n grows with np = λ fixed. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="poisson-process"></a>**Poisson process** — Events occurring independently at a constant average rate; counts in an interval are Poisson and the gaps between events are exponential. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="poisson-yield-model"></a>**Poisson yield model** — Yield = e^(−A·D₀): the probability that no killer defect lands on a die when defects are independent and uniform. *First defined in* [25-04](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-04-yield-and-die-cost.md).

<a id="poissons-equation"></a>**Poisson's equation** — The relation d²V/dx² = −ρ/ε between electrostatic potential and charge density (or dE/dx = ρ/ε); solved across junctions and MOS structures to find fields and potentials. *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="polar-code"></a>**Polar code** — A code built by recursively combining channel uses so that synthesized bit-channels polarize into nearly perfect and nearly useless ones; information rides on the reliable ones, decoded by successive cancellation (with a list and CRC in 5G NR control channels). *First defined in* [17-08](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-08-channel-coding.md). *See also:* [Channel capacity](#channel-capacity), [Cyclic redundancy check (CRC)](#cyclic-redundancy-check-crc).

<a id="polar-form"></a>**Polar form** — Writing a complex number by its magnitude and angle, z = r∠θ = r(cos θ + j sin θ) = re^{jθ}. Convenient for multiplication, division, powers and roots. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md). *See also:* [Rectangular form](#rectangular-form), [Euler's formula](#eulers-formula).

<a id="polarization-dielectric"></a>**Polarization (dielectric)** — The dipole moment per unit volume P (C/m²) induced in a dielectric by electronic, ionic or orientational response; at the dielectric's faces it appears as bound surface charge σ_b = P. *First defined in* [04-04](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-04-potential-capacitance-and-dielectrics.md).

<a id="polarization-light"></a>**Polarization (light)** — The direction in which a transverse wave's electric field oscillates; a polarizer transmits I₀ cos²θ (Malus's law), and reflection at Brewster's angle tan θ_B = n₂/n₁ removes one polarization. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="pole-placement"></a>**Pole placement** — Choosing a state-feedback gain K so that the closed-loop matrix A − BK has prescribed eigenvalues; possible for any eigenvalues when (A, B) is controllable, for example with Ackermann's formula. *First defined in* [15-10](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-10-state-space-introduction.md). *See also:* [Controllability](#controllability).

<a id="pole-splitting"></a>**Pole splitting** — The separation of a two-stage amplifier's two poles by a capacitor bridging the inverting second stage: Miller multiplication pushes the lower pole down to about 1/(g_m2R_1R_2C_c), and the capacitor's shorting of the second stage at high frequency pushes the upper pole up to about g_m2/(C_1 + C_2). *First defined in* [12-04](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-04-high-frequency-analysis-methods.md). *See also:* [Miller effect](#miller-effect), [Right-half-plane zero](#right-half-plane-zero).

<a id="poles-and-zeros"></a>**Poles and zeros** — The roots of a rational transfer function's denominator (poles) and numerator (zeros). Each pole p gives a natural mode e^(pt), so all poles in the left half-plane means stable; zeros set how much of each mode appears. *First defined in* [02-05](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-05-laplace-transform-for-odes.md). *See also:* [Transfer function](#transfer-function), [Characteristic equation](#characteristic-equation).

<a id="pole-zero-cancellation"></a>**Pole–zero cancellation** — A zero that coincides with a pole, removing that mode from one transfer function; the mode still exists inside the system, so cancelling an unstable pole leaves a hidden instability that disturbances or initial conditions excite. *First defined in* [15-02](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-02-transfer-functions-and-block-diagrams.md). *See also:* [Poles and zeros](#poles-and-zeros).

<a id="pole-zero-doublet"></a>**Pole–zero doublet** — A pole and a zero very close together; nearly invisible in the frequency response, it leaves a slow settling tail of amplitude about (z − p)/z decaying with the time constant 1/p, which dominates precision settling. *First defined in* [15-03](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-03-time-response.md). *See also:* [Settling time](#settling-time).

<a id="polling"></a>**Polling** — Checking a device's status register repeatedly in software to learn whether it needs service; simple and fast to respond, but every unproductive check wastes CPU time. *First defined in* [14-11](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-11-io-buses-and-interconnect.md). *See also:* [Interrupt](#interrupt).

<a id="poly-gate-depletion"></a>**Poly-gate depletion** — The depletion of a thin layer of a polysilicon gate at its oxide interface in inversion, W_dpoly = ε_ox E_ox/(qN_poly), which adds W_dpoly/3 to the electrical oxide thickness; eliminated by metal gates. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="polyphase-decomposition"></a>**Polyphase decomposition** — Writing H(z) = Σ z^(−k) E_k(z^M) with E_k[n] = h[nM + k]; it turns a decimator or interpolator into M short filters running at the low rate, cutting the arithmetic by M without changing the output. *First defined in* [16-09](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-09-multirate-dsp.md). *See also:* [Noble identities](#noble-identities), [Decimation](#decimation).

<a id="polyphase-filter"></a>**Polyphase filter** — An RC network that produces quadrature (or multiphase) signals; a single RC-CR stage gives exactly 90° at all frequencies but equal amplitudes only at ω = 1/RC, so multistage versions with staggered centres widen its band. *First defined in* [21-06](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-06-oscillators-and-vcos.md). *See also:* [Image-rejection ratio (IRR)](#image-rejection-ratio-irr).

<a id="polysilicon-emitter"></a>**Polysilicon emitter** — A bipolar emitter made of a thick heavily doped polysilicon layer over a shallow single-crystal emitter, which raises the effective emitter Gummel number and current gain and avoids defects from deep emitter implants. *First defined in* [09-07](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-07-bipolar-junction-transistor.md).

<a id="population-inversion"></a>**Population inversion** — A state in which more electrons occupy the upper energy states than the lower ones, so stimulated emission outweighs absorption and light is amplified; in a diode it needs E_Fn − E_Fp > E_g. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="pose-prediction"></a>**Pose prediction** — Extrapolating head motion forward by the known pipeline latency so the rendered or reprojected image matches where the head will be when the photons arrive. *First defined in* [27-04](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-04-wearables-earbuds-and-glasses.md). *See also:* [Motion-to-photon latency](#motion-to-photon-latency).

<a id="positive-definite-matrix"></a>**Positive definite matrix** — A symmetric matrix with xᵀAx > 0 for every nonzero x; equivalently all eigenvalues positive, or all pivots positive. Grounded conductance matrices, nonsingular covariance matrices and Hessians at strict minima are examples. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="positive-real-function"></a>**Positive-real function** — A function Z(s) that is real for real s and has Re Z ≥ 0 whenever Re s ≥ 0; exactly the driving-point impedances realizable from passive R, L, C (and transformers), as shown by Brune (1931). *First defined in* [07-04](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-04-laplace-domain-circuit-analysis.md).

<a id="post-regulation"></a>**Post-regulation** — Following a switching converter with a linear regulator from a slightly higher rail, so the switcher does the large voltage step efficiently and the LDO removes its ripple at a small V_out/V_in penalty. *First defined in* [22-01](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-01-power-conversion-principles.md). *See also:* [Linear regulator](#linear-regulator), [Low-dropout regulator (LDO)](#low-dropout-regulator-ldo).

<a id="post-silicon-validation"></a>**Post-silicon validation** — Testing first silicon in the lab at full speed with real software and systems, to find the functional and electrical bugs that pre-silicon verification missed; visibility is limited to on-chip debug features. *First defined in* [19-13](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-13-verification-methods.md). *See also:* [Design verification](#design-verification), [Respin](#respin).

<a id="potential-energy"></a>**Potential energy** — Energy stored by position against a conservative force, with F = −dU/dx; mgh for gravity near the Earth and ½k_s x² for a spring. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="powder-core"></a>**Powder core** — A core pressed from insulated magnetic-metal particles, whose many tiny gaps act as a distributed air gap; it has high saturation flux density and saturates softly, which suits inductors carrying DC current. *First defined in* [22-05](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-05-magnetics-design.md). *See also:* [Soft saturation](#soft-saturation), [Air gap](#air-gap).

<a id="power-angle"></a>**Power angle** — The angle δ between a synchronous machine's terminal voltage and its field EMF; three-phase power is 3VE_f sin δ/X_s, maximum (pull-out) at δ = 90°. *First defined in* [22-11](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-11-electric-machines.md).

<a id="power-delivery-network"></a>**Power delivery network** — The regulators, board and package wiring, and decoupling capacitors that carry current from the supply to the transistors; its inductance and the die's capacitance form a resonant tank that causes supply droop on load steps. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="power-density"></a>**Power density** — Rated output power divided by the volume of a stated box, in W/in³ or W/cm³; bounded by passive size at a given switching frequency and by heat removal, ρ ≤ q·η/(1 − η) for a box that can reject q per unit volume. *First defined in* [22-01](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-01-power-conversion-principles.md). *See also:* [Efficiency](#efficiency).

<a id="power-factor"></a>**Power factor** — Real power divided by apparent power; cos φ for sinusoids with phase difference φ, and lower still when the current is distorted. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="power-flow"></a>**Power flow** — The steady-state solution of a network's bus voltages and branch flows given loads and generation; between two buses, real power is V1V2 sin δ/X (set by the angle) and reactive power is driven by the voltage magnitudes. *First defined in* [22-12](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-12-power-systems-fundamentals.md).

<a id="power-gating"></a>**Power gating** — Disconnecting an idle block from its supply through a high-threshold sleep transistor to cut its leakage, at the cost of the transistor's area and IR drop, state loss or retention, wake-up latency and recharge energy; it saves energy only for sleeps longer than the break-even time. *First defined in* [19-06](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-06-power-and-low-power-design.md). *See also:* [Static power](#static-power).

<a id="power-law"></a>**Power law** — A relation y = kxⁿ; doubling x multiplies y by 2ⁿ, and on log-log axes it is a straight line with slope n. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md). *See also:* [Log-log plot](#log-log-plot).

<a id="power-mode"></a>**Power mode** — One of an MCU's operating states (run, sleep, stop or deep sleep, standby or shutdown), each stopping more clocks and power domains in exchange for lower current and a longer, costlier wake-up. *First defined in* [18-09](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-09-ultra-low-power-design.md). *See also:* [Always-on domain](#always-on-domain), [Break-even time](#break-even-time).

<a id="power-over-ethernet-poe"></a>**Power over Ethernet (PoE)** — Delivering DC power over Ethernet cabling (IEEE 802.3af, at and bt) at up to 57 V; the device receives the source's class power minus the cable's I²R loss (90 W at the source gives 71.3 W at the device for Type 4). *First defined in* [06-08](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-08-thevenin-and-norton.md). *See also:* [Thevenin equivalent](#thevenin-equivalent).

<a id="power-path"></a>**Power path** — A charger arrangement that supplies the system load from the input first and charges the battery with the remainder, so a device can run with a dead battery and charge termination is not confused by the load. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md).

<a id="power-rating"></a>**Power rating** — The power a component can dissipate continuously at a stated ambient temperature, derated above it; designers usually run parts well below it. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md).

<a id="power-rule"></a>**Power rule** — d/dx xⁿ = n xⁿ⁻¹, valid for every real exponent n (for x > 0). *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="power-sequencing"></a>**Power sequencing** — Enabling a system's rails in a required order with programmed delays, each after the previous rail reports power-good, and disabling them in a defined order, so that no block is powered before the blocks it depends on. *First defined in* [22-08](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-08-pmics.md). *See also:* [Power-good signal](#power-good-signal).

<a id="power-series"></a>**Power series** — Σ c_k (x − a)^k; it converges inside a radius of convergence, where it can be differentiated and integrated term by term. *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).

<a id="power-signal"></a>**Power signal** — A signal with finite, nonzero average power P = lim (1/2T)∫|x|² dt over [−T, T], and hence infinite energy; periodic signals are power signals, with P equal to the average over one period. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md). *See also:* [Energy signal](#energy-signal), [RMS value](#rms-value).

<a id="power-smoothing"></a>**Power smoothing** — Using local energy storage and control to keep a load's power drawn from the grid steadier than its actual consumption, for example capacitors in AI rack power supplies that absorb training-step swings. *First defined in* [22-10](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-10-datacenter-power-delivery.md).

<a id="power-spectral-density"></a>**Power spectral density** — The distribution of a stationary process's average power over frequency, in power per hertz; the Fourier transform of the autocorrelation. Circuit noise densities are usually one-sided. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="power-tree"></a>**Power tree** — The chain of converters that feeds each load from the battery or supply; battery power is the sum of load powers divided by their converters' efficiencies, and every converter loss also heats the product. *First defined in* [27-01](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-01-system-analysis-method.md). *See also:* [Budget tree](#budget-tree).

<a id="power-usage-effectiveness-pue"></a>**Power usage effectiveness (PUE)** — A datacenter's total facility power divided by the power delivered to its IT equipment; 1.0 would mean no cooling or distribution overhead. *First defined in* [22-10](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-10-datacenter-power-delivery.md).

<a id="power-wall"></a>**Power wall** — The limit on clock frequency set by power density and cooling once supply voltages stopped scaling; processors reached it around 2004 and turned to multicore designs. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="power-added-efficiency-pae"></a>**Power-added efficiency (PAE)** — (P_out − P_in)/P_DC, the drain efficiency penalized by the drive power; it trails drain efficiency badly when the stage's gain is low, as at millimetre waves. *First defined in* [21-07](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-07-power-amplifiers.md). *See also:* [Drain efficiency](#drain-efficiency).

<a id="power-delay-profile"></a>**Power-delay profile** — The average received power of a multipath channel as a function of excess delay; its Fourier transform is the channel's frequency correlation. *First defined in* [17-09](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-09-wireless-channels.md). *See also:* [RMS delay spread](#rms-delay-spread), [Coherence bandwidth](#coherence-bandwidth).

<a id="power-factor-correction"></a>**Power-factor correction** — Raising a load's power factor, by parallel capacitors that supply the lagging reactive current locally (C = P(tan θ₁ − tan θ₂)/(ωV_rms²)), or, for distorted currents, by an active converter stage that draws sinusoidal current. *First defined in* [07-06](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-06-ac-power-and-power-factor.md). *See also:* [Power factor](#power-factor).

<a id="power-good-signal"></a>**Power-good signal** — A regulator's output flag that its rail has risen above an under-voltage threshold and is in regulation; sequencers and processors wait for it before the next step. *First defined in* [22-08](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-08-pmics.md). *See also:* [Power sequencing](#power-sequencing).

<a id="power-loss-protection-plp"></a>**Power-loss protection (PLP)** — Capacitors that hold an SSD's rails up long enough after a power failure to write buffered data and mapping updates to flash; sized from E = ½C(V₁² − V₂²). *First defined in* [23-07](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-07-ssd-controllers.md). *See also:* [Flash translation layer (FTL)](#flash-translation-layer-ftl).

<a id="power-management-ic-pmic"></a>**Power-management IC (PMIC)** — A chip that supplies a system's many rails: several buck converters and LDOs, load switches, a sequencer, a control interface through which the processor sets voltages and modes, and often a charger, fuel gauge and monitoring ADC. *First defined in* [22-08](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-08-pmics.md). *See also:* [Post-regulation](#post-regulation), [Power sequencing](#power-sequencing).

<a id="power-supply-rejection-ratio-psrr"></a>**Power-supply rejection ratio (PSRR)** — The ratio of a change in supply voltage to the input-referred offset change it causes, in dB or µV/V; it falls with frequency, so supply ripple leaks through more at high frequency. *First defined in* [10-09](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-09-real-op-amps-nonidealities.md).

<a id="poynting-vector"></a>**Poynting vector** — S = E × B/µ₀ (W/m²), the power flow per unit area in an electromagnetic field; it shows energy entering resistors and capacitors through the surrounding fields, and gives a plane wave's intensity E₀²/(2η₀). *First defined in* [04-08](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-08-maxwell-preview.md).

<a id="ppk"></a>**Ppk** — The process performance index, Cpk's formula with the overall standard deviation of all the data (including drift and lot-to-lot shifts) instead of the within-subgroup σ; equal to Cpk only for a process in statistical control. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="pre-adder"></a>**Pre-adder** — An adder in front of a DSP block's multiplier, used to add the two samples that share a coefficient in a symmetric FIR filter, which halves the number of multiplications. *First defined in* [16-06](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-06-fir-filter-design.md). *See also:* [FIR filter](#fir-filter), [Multiply-accumulate (MAC)](#multiply-accumulate-mac).

<a id="pre-emphasis"></a>**Pre-emphasis** — A high-frequency boost 1 + j2πfτ applied to audio before FM, undone after detection, which removes much of FM's parabolic noise (about 13 dB for τ = 75 µs over 15 kHz); 75 µs in the US, 50 µs in Europe. *First defined in* [17-03](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-03-analog-modulation.md). *See also:* [Frequency modulation](#frequency-modulation).

<a id="precharge"></a>**Precharge** — A low-current charge phase that a charger applies to a deeply discharged lithium-ion cell before allowing full current. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md).

<a id="precise-exception"></a>**Precise exception** — An exception taken so that the architectural state is exactly as if every instruction before the faulting one had completed and none after it had started, which lets the operating system handle it and resume the program. *First defined in* [14-08](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-08-out-of-order-and-superscalar.md). *See also:* [Reorder buffer (ROB)](#reorder-buffer-rob).

<a id="precision-rectifier"></a>**Precision rectifier** — A rectifier with its diode inside an op-amp's feedback loop, so the diode's forward drop is divided by the loop gain; its accuracy at high frequency is limited by the op-amp's slew through about two diode drops at each zero crossing. *First defined in* [10-10](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-10-op-amp-application-circuits.md).

<a id="precision-to-tolerance-ratio"></a>**Precision-to-tolerance ratio** — P/T = 6σ_m/(USL − LSL), a gauge's measurement noise relative to the specification window; about 0.1 or less is good, above about 0.3 inadequate. *First defined in* [25-03](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-03-deposition-etch-cmp-implant-metrology.md).

<a id="precursor-tap"></a>**Precursor tap** — An equalizer tap that weights a sample received after the one being decided, cancelling energy that the channel delivers before the main pulse; needed because channels are generally not minimum phase, so their stable inverse is partly anticausal. *First defined in* [16-02](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-02-dtft-and-z-transform-for-dsp.md). *See also:* [Feed-forward equalizer (FFE)](#feed-forward-equalizer-ffe), [Minimum-phase system](#minimum-phase-system).

<a id="prefetch-dram"></a>**Prefetch (DRAM)** — The number of bits per data pin a DRAM's core delivers in one column access (8n for DDR4, 16n for DDR5), serialized onto the pin; it lets the pin rate grow while the core's column rate stays at a few hundred megahertz. *First defined in* [23-04](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-04-dram-interfaces.md). *See also:* [Burst length](#burst-length).

<a id="prefetch-buffer"></a>**Prefetch buffer** — A buffer that reads whole flash lines ahead of the program counter so sequential code runs without wait-state stalls; taken branches still pay the wait states unless a cache holds the target. *First defined in* [18-01](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-01-microcontroller-architecture.md). *See also:* [Flash wait state](#flash-wait-state).

<a id="prefetching"></a>**Prefetching** — Fetching blocks into a cache before they are requested, by hardware that predicts the access pattern (next-line, stride) or by software hints; judged by coverage, accuracy and timeliness. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Memory-level parallelism (MLP)](#memory-level-parallelism-mlp).

<a id="prefill-and-decode"></a>**Prefill and decode** — The two phases of language-model inference; prefill processes the prompt in parallel and is compute-bound, while decode generates one token at a time, reading every weight per token, and is memory-bandwidth-bound. *First defined in* [27-05](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-05-pc-soc.md). *See also:* [Unified memory](#unified-memory).

<a id="prefix-code"></a>**Prefix code** — A code in which no codeword is the beginning of another, so a concatenated stream decodes without separators; its lengths must satisfy the Kraft inequality. *First defined in* [17-07](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-07-information-theory-and-shannon.md). *See also:* [Kraft inequality](#kraft-inequality), [Huffman code](#huffman-code).

<a id="preprocessor"></a>**Preprocessor** — The first stage of a C build, which rewrites source text according to lines starting with *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md).

<a id="preselector"></a>**Preselector** — The band filter ahead of a receiver's first mixer that attenuates the image and other out-of-band signals; for an order-n Butterworth, each order adds about 20 log of the normalized image distance in dB. *First defined in* [21-08](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-08-transceiver-architectures.md). *See also:* [Image frequency](#image-frequency).

<a id="prestons-equation"></a>**Preston's equation** — The empirical CMP law RR = K_p P v: removal rate proportional to local pressure and relative velocity; raised features carry more pressure and polish faster. *First defined in* [25-03](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-03-deposition-etch-cmp-implant-metrology.md). *See also:* [Dishing and erosion](#dishing-and-erosion).

<a id="prime-implicant"></a>**Prime implicant** — An implicant that cannot be enlarged by removing a literal without covering a 0 of the function; some minimal sum of products always consists of prime implicants only. *First defined in* [08-03](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-03-logic-minimization.md). *See also:* [Essential prime implicant](#essential-prime-implicant), [Implicant](#implicant).

<a id="primitive-polynomial"></a>**Primitive polynomial** — An irreducible polynomial of degree n over GF(2) whose root generates all 2^n - 1 nonzero field elements; used as an LFSR's feedback, it gives maximal length. *First defined in* [08-07](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-07-registers-counters-shift-registers.md). *See also:* [Linear-feedback shift register (LFSR)](#linear-feedback-shift-register-lfsr).

<a id="principal-component-analysis"></a>**Principal component analysis** — Finding the eigenvectors of a data set's covariance matrix (equivalently the singular vectors of the centered data), ordered by the variance they carry, to describe or compress the data with a few uncorrelated components. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="priority-ceiling-protocol"></a>**Priority ceiling protocol** — A mutex protocol in which each mutex has a ceiling (the highest priority of its users) and a holder runs at that ceiling; a task is then blocked at most once, by one critical section, and deadlock between mutexes cannot occur. *First defined in* [18-07](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-07-rtos-concepts.md). *See also:* [Priority inheritance](#priority-inheritance), [Deadlock](#deadlock).

<a id="priority-encoder"></a>**Priority encoder** — A block that outputs the number of the highest-priority active input, plus a valid flag that is 0 when no input is active; used for interrupt arbitration and leading-one detection. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md).

<a id="priority-inheritance"></a>**Priority inheritance** — A mutex protocol in which a task holding a mutex temporarily runs at the priority of the highest-priority task waiting for it, bounding priority inversion to the holder's critical section (once per mutex). *First defined in* [18-07](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-07-rtos-concepts.md). *See also:* [Priority inversion](#priority-inversion), [Mutex](#mutex).

<a id="priority-inversion"></a>**Priority inversion** — A high-priority task waiting for a lower-priority task that holds a resource it needs; unbounded when medium-priority tasks preempt the holder, as on Mars Pathfinder in 1997. *First defined in* [18-07](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-07-rtos-concepts.md). *See also:* [Priority inheritance](#priority-inheritance), [Priority ceiling protocol](#priority-ceiling-protocol).

<a id="privilege-mode"></a>**Privilege mode** — The level of authority at which code runs (RISC-V machine, supervisor and user modes), determining which instructions, registers and pages it may use. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Trap (processor)](#trap-processor).

<a id="probability-density-function"></a>**Probability density function** — A non-negative function f(x) with total area 1, whose area over an interval is the probability of landing in it; the density itself is not a probability and can exceed 1. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="probability-mass-function-pmf"></a>**Probability mass function (PMF)** — For a discrete random variable, p_X(k) = P(X = k); the values are non-negative and sum to 1. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="probe-card"></a>**Probe card** — The fixture of fine needles or micro-springs that contacts a die's pads at wafer sort, connecting them to the tester; fine pitch, many sites and high current make advanced probe cards costly. *First defined in* [25-11](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-11-test-ate-sort-burn-in.md). *See also:* [Wafer sort](#wafer-sort).

<a id="process-capability-cp-cpk"></a>**Process capability (Cp, Cpk)** — Cp = (USL − LSL)/(6σ) compares the specification window with the process spread; Cpk = min(USL − μ, μ − LSL)/(3σ) also charges for an off-center mean. Automotive defaults (AIAG, 1995 manuals): Cpk ≥ 1.33 for stable ongoing production; preliminary studies and significant characteristics are judged on Ppk, expecting ≥ 1.67. *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="process-design-kit-pdk"></a>**Process design kit (PDK)** — The files a foundry gives designers to use its process, including device models, design rules, layer definitions and often standard-cell libraries, abstracting the fab's recipes. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="processing-element-pe"></a>**Processing element (PE)** — One cell of an accelerator array, typically a multiply-accumulate unit with a few registers, connected to its neighbours. *First defined in* [14-14](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-14-ai-accelerators.md). *See also:* [Systolic array](#systolic-array), [Multiply-accumulate (MAC)](#multiply-accumulate-mac).

<a id="processing-gain"></a>**Processing gain** — The amount by which narrowing the analysis bandwidth raises a signal above the noise without changing the signal-to-noise-density ratio. For an FFT it is the per-bin floor drop, 10 log10(N/(2·ENBW)) dB (16-05); in spread spectrum it is the chip rate times the integration time, the SNR gained by correlating with the code (17-02). *First defined in* [16-05](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-05-spectral-analysis-and-windowing.md). *See also:* [Equivalent noise bandwidth (ENBW)](#equivalent-noise-bandwidth-enbw), [Eb/N0](#eb-n0).

<a id="processing-in-memory-pim"></a>**Processing-in-memory (PIM)** — Placing simple compute units beside the banks of a memory die, so memory-bound operations use the die's internal bandwidth instead of its pins; also called near-memory computing. *First defined in* [23-09](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-09-compute-in-memory.md). *See also:* [Compute-in-memory (CIM)](#compute-in-memory-cim), [Arithmetic intensity](#arithmetic-intensity).

<a id="product-of-sums-pos"></a>**Product of sums (POS)** — An AND of OR terms; the canonical POS ANDs the maxterms of the rows where the function is 0, and it maps onto two-level OR-AND or NOR-NOR logic. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md).

<a id="product-requirements-document-prd"></a>**Product requirements document (PRD)** — The document that states what a product shall do in measurable terms (functions, performance, interfaces, environment, cost, schedule) without saying how; the bridge from the MRD to the architecture specification. *First defined in* [26-01](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-01-requirements-and-specifications.md). *See also:* [Market requirements document (MRD)](#market-requirements-document-mrd), [Requirement](#requirement).

<a id="product-rule"></a>**Product rule** — (fg)' = f'g + fg'; the derivative of a product has one term for each factor's change. *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="professional-engineer-pe"></a>**Professional engineer (PE)** — An engineer licensed by a US state, usually after an accredited degree, the FE exam, about four years of experience and the PE exam; required to sign and seal engineering work offered to the public. *First defined in* [26-07](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-07-engineering-ethics.md).

<a id="program-counter-pc"></a>**Program counter (PC)** — The register holding the address of the instruction being executed; it advances by 4 or is loaded with a branch or jump target each instruction. *First defined in* [14-05](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-05-single-cycle-datapath.md).

<a id="program-organization"></a>**Program organization** — An organization in which each product or program has its own dedicated team of every discipline, giving clear ownership at the cost of duplicated methods and idle specialists between peaks. *First defined in* [26-06](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-06-team-structures-and-sizing.md).

<a id="program-suspend"></a>**Program suspend** — A NAND feature that pauses a long program or erase so the controller can serve waiting reads, trading write throughput for read tail latency. *First defined in* [23-07](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-07-ssd-controllers.md). *See also:* [Garbage collection (SSD)](#garbage-collection-ssd).

<a id="programmable-logic-array-pla"></a>**Programmable logic array (PLA)** — A two-level logic structure with a programmable AND plane forming product terms and a programmable OR plane summing them into outputs; its size grows with the number of products rather than with 2^n. *First defined in* [08-11](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-11-memories-and-programmable-logic.md).

<a id="programmable-power-supply-pps"></a>**Programmable Power Supply (PPS)** — A USB Power Delivery mode in which the sink requests the adapter's output voltage in fine steps and the adapter limits current, enabling direct charging. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md).

<a id="projected-range"></a>**Projected range** — The mean depth R_p at which implanted ions stop, with straggle ΔR_p as its standard deviation; the as-implanted profile is approximately Gaussian about R_p. *First defined in* [25-03](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-03-deposition-etch-cmp-implant-metrology.md).

<a id="projection"></a>**Projection** — The closest point to b on the line through a, p = (a·b / a·a) a, characterized by the error b − p being perpendicular to a; the basis of least squares. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="proof-mass"></a>**Proof mass** — The suspended mass in an accelerometer or gyroscope whose displacement relative to its package measures acceleration (deflection a/ω₀² below resonance) or rotation. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="propagation-constant"></a>**Propagation constant** — γ = α + jβ, with a wave varying as e^(−γz); α (Np/m) is the attenuation and β (rad/m) the phase constant. For a plane wave γ = √(jωµ(σ + jωε)); for a transmission line γ = √((R + jωL)(G + jωC)). *First defined in* [13-05](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-05-plane-waves.md). *See also:* [Neper](#neper).

<a id="propagation-delay"></a>**Propagation delay** — The time from an input transition to the output crossing 50 % of its swing; for an RC model, τ·ln 2 ≈ 0.69τ. In digital timing, t_pd is the longest such delay from any input change until the output is final, and the delays along a path add (08-04). *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md). *See also:* [Contamination delay](#contamination-delay), [Critical path](#critical-path).

<a id="proportional-fair-scheduling"></a>**Proportional-fair scheduling** — Serving, in each slot, the user with the largest ratio of instantaneous achievable rate to its own recent average throughput; it keeps most of the multi-user diversity gain while sharing resources fairly. *First defined in* [17-12](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-12-multiple-access-and-cellular-wifi.md). *See also:* [Multi-user diversity](#multi-user-diversity), [OFDMA](#ofdma).

<a id="proximity-effect"></a>**Proximity effect** — Eddy currents induced in a conductor by the magnetic field of neighbouring conductors; in a multilayer winding it raises the AC resistance roughly as the square of the number of layers. *First defined in* [22-05](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-05-magnetics-design.md). *See also:* [Skin effect](#skin-effect), [Dowell's equation](#dowells-equation).

<a id="pseudo-channel"></a>**Pseudo-channel** — Half of an HBM channel, operating independently with its own banks; an HBM4 stack has 32 channels and 64 pseudo-channels of 32 data bits each. *First defined in* [23-05](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-05-hbm-in-depth.md). *See also:* [High Bandwidth Memory (HBM)](#high-bandwidth-memory-hbm).

<a id="pseudo-instruction"></a>**Pseudo-instruction** — An assembler mnemonic that expands into one or more real instructions, such as li, mv, j, ret and call in RISC-V. *First defined in* [14-03](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-03-assembly-and-the-compilation-stack.md).

<a id="pseudo-nmos-logic"></a>**Pseudo-NMOS logic** — A ratioed logic style with an NMOS pull-down network and a single always-on PMOS load. It needs N + 1 transistors and light input loads, but its low level V_OL is set by the ratio k_n/k_p and it draws static current whenever the output is low. *First defined in* [19-03](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-03-logic-families.md). *See also:* [Static CMOS](#static-cmos).

<a id="pseudo-open-drain-pod-i-o"></a>**Pseudo-open-drain (POD) I/O** — DDR4 and DDR5 signaling in which each line is terminated to the I/O supply; a 1 draws no static current and a 0 draws V_DDQ/(R_on + R_TT). *First defined in* [23-04](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-04-dram-interfaces.md). *See also:* [Data bus inversion (DBI)](#data-bus-inversion-dbi).

<a id="pseudo-random-bit-sequence-prbs"></a>**Pseudo-random bit sequence (PRBS)** — A deterministic, periodic bit stream with noise-like statistics, normally the output of a maximal-length LFSR, used as a standard test pattern for links (PRBS7, PRBS15, PRBS23, PRBS31). *First defined in* [08-07](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-07-registers-counters-shift-registers.md). *See also:* [Linear-feedback shift register (LFSR)](#linear-feedback-shift-register-lfsr), [Scrambler](#scrambler).

<a id="ptat-voltage"></a>**PTAT voltage** — A voltage proportional to absolute temperature, such as the difference (kT/q) ln(I_1/I_2) between two diodes or transistors at different current densities; the basis of on-chip temperature sensors and bandgap references. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md).

<a id="pull-up-and-pull-down-networks"></a>**Pull-up and pull-down networks** — The pMOS switch network connecting a CMOS gate's output to the supply and the nMOS network connecting it to ground; series connections in one are parallel in the other, the circuit form of De Morgan's theorem. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md).

<a id="pull-up-ratio"></a>**Pull-up ratio** — In a 6T SRAM cell, the strength of the pull-up PMOS relative to the access transistor, k_P/k_A; it must be small enough for a low bitline to overpower the pull-up and write the cell (about 0.67 or less for the conservative criterion in this course's square-law cell; rules of thumb in W/L terms run near 1–1.5 because the PMOS's mobility is lower). *First defined in* [19-08](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-08-sram-design.md). *See also:* [Cell ratio](#cell-ratio), [SRAM](#sram).

<a id="pulse-compression"></a>**Pulse compression** — Transmitting a long, wideband pulse (often a linear chirp) and matched filtering it on reception, so that detection depends on the long pulse's energy while range resolution is that of a short pulse, about c/(2B); the compression ratio is the time–bandwidth product. *First defined in* [17-05](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-05-matched-filters-and-detection.md). *See also:* [Matched filter](#matched-filter).

<a id="pulse-amplitude-modulation"></a>**Pulse-amplitude modulation** — Sending a sequence of levels a_k as amplitudes of a repeated pulse, x(t) = Σ a_k p(t − kT); M levels carry log2 M bits per symbol, and equally spaced levels ±1, ±3, … have mean energy (M² − 1)/3. *First defined in* [17-04](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-04-baseband-digital-transmission.md). *See also:* [PAM4](#pam4), [Symbol rate](#symbol-rate), [Gray code](#gray-code).

<a id="pulse-density-modulation-pdm"></a>**Pulse-density modulation (PDM)** — A 1-bit, high-rate bit stream whose density of ones follows the signal, produced by a sigma-delta modulator (as in digital MEMS microphones) and turned into multibit samples by a decimation filter. *First defined in* [18-10](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-10-sensors.md). *See also:* [Decimation](#decimation).

<a id="pulse-frequency-modulation-pfm"></a>**Pulse-frequency modulation (PFM)** — A light-load control mode in which a converter delivers bursts of switching pulses and then idles, so its switching-related fixed loss falls roughly with load; the price is ripple at a load-dependent frequency. *First defined in* [22-01](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-01-power-conversion-principles.md). *See also:* [Phase shedding](#phase-shedding).

<a id="pulse-width-modulation-pwm"></a>**Pulse-width modulation (PWM)** — A digital output that switches at a fixed frequency with a variable fraction of each period high (the duty cycle); a timer generates it by comparing its count with a compare register, trading frequency against duty resolution. *First defined in* [18-03](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-03-interrupts-exceptions-timers.md). *See also:* [Input capture](#input-capture), [PWM DAC](#pwm-dac).

<a id="puncturing"></a>**Puncturing** — Deleting coded bits in a fixed pattern to raise a mother code's rate (e.g. rate 1/2 to 3/4) so one decoder serves several rates; deleted positions are decoded as erasures. *First defined in* [17-08](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-08-channel-coding.md). *See also:* [Code rate](#code-rate), [Convolutional code](#convolutional-code).

<a id="push-pull-output"></a>**Push-pull output** — An output stage that actively drives both high and low through transistors to each rail; fast and strong, but two push-pull outputs must never drive the same line in opposite states. *First defined in* [18-05](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-05-gpio-uart-spi-i2c.md). *See also:* [Open-drain output](#open-drain-output).

<a id="pvt-corner"></a>**PVT corner** — A process-voltage-temperature condition at which a cell library is characterized, such as slow transistors at low voltage and high temperature; timing is signed off at several corners, often with separate wire (RC) corners. *First defined in* [19-10](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-10-synthesis-and-sta.md). *See also:* [On-chip variation (OCV)](#on-chip-variation-ocv).

<a id="pwm-dac"></a>**PWM DAC** — A digital-to-analog converter made from a pulse-width-modulated output and a low-pass filter; the filter keeps the average A·D and attenuates the switching harmonics, leaving a ripple set by the PWM frequency and filter order. *First defined in* [11-05](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-05-fourier-series.md). *See also:* [Duty cycle](#duty-cycle).

<a id="pwm-modulator-gain"></a>**PWM modulator gain** — The small-signal gain 1/V_M from the control voltage to the duty cycle of a pulse-width modulator with a sawtooth of peak V_M. *First defined in* [22-07](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-07-converter-dynamics-and-control.md).

<a id="letter-q"></a>

## Q

<a id="q-format"></a>**Q format** — Notation Qm.f for fixed-point numbers with m integer and f fractional bits; Q15 is a 16-bit signed fraction in [−1, 1 − 2^−15] with resolution 3.05×10^−5. *First defined in* [05-07](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-07-bit-manipulation.md).

<a id="q-function"></a>**Q-function** — Q(x), the probability that a standard normal random variable exceeds x; it gives error probabilities for decisions in Gaussian noise and falls off extremely fast (Q(6) ≈ 1e-9). *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="qam"></a>**QAM** — Quadrature amplitude modulation, independent PAM on I and Q; square M-QAM has Es = 2(M − 1)/3 for unit half-spacing and costs about 5–6 dB of SNR per extra two bits per symbol, but fills the plane better than PSK. *First defined in* [17-06](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-06-bandpass-digital-modulation.md). *See also:* [Constellation](#constellation), [M-PSK](#m-psk), [Error vector magnitude](#error-vector-magnitude).

<a id="qpsk"></a>**QPSK** — Quadrature phase-shift keying, four points (±a, ±a); with Gray labels it is two independent BPSK streams in quadrature, doubling BPSK's bit rate at the same bit-error rate. *First defined in* [17-06](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-06-bandpass-digital-modulation.md). *See also:* [BPSK](#bpsk), [M-PSK](#m-psk).

<a id="quadratic-convergence"></a>**Quadratic convergence** — Convergence in which each error is proportional to the square of the previous one, so the number of correct digits roughly doubles per step. *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md).

<a id="quadratic-placement"></a>**Quadratic placement** — Placing cells by minimizing the sum of weighted squared connection lengths with some pins fixed; setting the gradient to zero gives a sparse linear system in which each cell sits at the weighted average of its neighbors. Real placers add spreading to undo the resulting overlap. *First defined in* [19-11](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-11-place-route-signoff.md). *See also:* [Legalization](#legalization), [Half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL)](#half-perimeter-wirelength-hpwl).

<a id="quadrature-vco-qvco"></a>**Quadrature VCO (QVCO)** — Two LC oscillators coupled so that each injects into the other, locking 90° apart at the LO frequency without a divider; coupling costs phase noise and tank mismatch becomes I/Q phase error. *First defined in* [21-06](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-06-oscillators-and-vcos.md). *See also:* [Injection locking](#injection-locking), [Image-rejection ratio (IRR)](#image-rejection-ratio-irr).

<a id="qualification"></a>**Qualification** — A standard set of accelerated stress tests (HTOL, temperature cycling, humidity, storage, ESD, latch-up) run on samples of a new or changed product to show it has no gross reliability weakness; it does not by itself demonstrate a field failure rate. *First defined in* [25-10](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-10-qualification-and-functional-safety.md). *See also:* [AEC-Q100](#aec-q100), [HTOL](#htol).

<a id="quality-factor"></a>**Quality factor** — Q = 1/(2ζ) = ω₀ × energy stored / power dissipated; the amplitude decays by a factor e in Q/π cycles, and Q also sets the sharpness of resonance. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md). *See also:* [Damping ratio](#damping-ratio).

<a id="quantization-neural-networks"></a>**Quantization (neural networks)** — Representing a model's weights or activations in a narrow format (INT8, FP8, FP4) with scale factors, x ≈ s(q − z), to cut memory, bandwidth and arithmetic cost at some loss of accuracy. *First defined in* [14-04](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-04-computer-arithmetic-and-number-formats.md). *See also:* [Block floating point](#block-floating-point), [Requantization](#requantization).

<a id="quantization-noise"></a>**Quantization noise** — The rounding error of an ADC, modeled as uniform over ±½ LSB, with RMS Δ/√12 ≈ 0.29 LSB; it sets the ideal SNR of 6.02N + 1.76 dB. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md).

<a id="quantum-confinement"></a>**Quantum confinement** — The rise and spreading of energy levels when a particle is squeezed into a region comparable to its de Broglie wavelength, E_n = n²h²/(8mL²) for an infinite well; it tunes quantum-well lasers and quantum-dot colors. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="quantum-efficiency"></a>**Quantum efficiency** — The number of electrons collected per incident photon (or, for an emitter, photons out per injected electron), combining reflection, absorption and collection or extraction losses. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="quantum-tunneling"></a>**Quantum tunneling** — Passage of a particle through a barrier higher than its energy, with probability falling roughly as e^(−2κd), κ = √(2m(V₀ − E))/ħ; it causes gate-oxide leakage and enables flash memory, STM and tunnel diodes. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="quarter-wave-transformer"></a>**Quarter-wave transformer** — A layer (or transmission-line section) a quarter wavelength thick whose impedance is the geometric mean of those on either side, √(η₁η₃); it cancels reflection at its design frequency, as in antireflection coatings. *First defined in* [13-06](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-06-reflection-and-transmission.md). *See also:* [Reflection coefficient](#reflection-coefficient).

<a id="quasi-fermi-level"></a>**Quasi-Fermi level** — A separate Fermi level for electrons (E_Fn) or holes (E_Fp) when a semiconductor is out of equilibrium but each carrier population is in equilibrium with itself; np = n_i² e^((E_Fn − E_Fp)/kT), and each current flows down its own quasi-Fermi-level gradient. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="quasi-neutral-region"></a>**Quasi-neutral region** — The part of a doped region outside a depletion layer, where majority carriers balance the dopant charge and the field is small. *First defined in* [09-05](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-05-pn-junction-electrostatics.md).

<a id="quasi-resonant-flyback"></a>**Quasi-resonant flyback** — A flyback that waits after the magnetizing current reaches zero and turns its switch on at a valley of the drain's ringing, cutting capacitive turn-on loss at the cost of a load- and line-dependent frequency. *First defined in* [22-04](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-04-isolated-converters.md). *See also:* [Flyback converter](#flyback-converter).

<a id="quasi-static-approximation"></a>**Quasi-static approximation** — Treating time-varying fields as if static at each instant, valid when the structure is much smaller than a wavelength (a common rule is below λ/10); it is the assumption behind lumped circuit theory. *First defined in* [13-04](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-04-maxwells-equations.md). *See also:* [Maxwell's equations](#maxwells-equations).

<a id="qubit"></a>**Qubit** — A two-level quantum system in a superposition α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ with |α|² + |β|² = 1; measurement returns 0 or 1 with probabilities |α|² and |β|², and n qubits need 2ⁿ amplitudes to describe classically. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="queue"></a>**Queue** — A first-in-first-out collection with enqueue at the back and dequeue at the front, O(1) each; implemented with a ring buffer or a linked list. A priority queue instead removes the smallest key first. *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="quiescent-current"></a>**Quiescent current** — The current a regulator or other circuit draws for its own operation with no (or negligible) load; it matters most when the load current is microamps. *First defined in* [18-09](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-09-ultra-low-power-design.md). *See also:* [Low-dropout regulator (LDO)](#low-dropout-regulator-ldo).

<a id="quine-mccluskey-method"></a>**Quine–McCluskey method** — A tabular algorithm for two-level minimization that merges terms differing in one bit (grouped by their number of 1s) to find all prime implicants, then selects a cover from a prime implicant chart. *First defined in* [08-03](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-03-logic-minimization.md). *See also:* [Petrick's method](#petricks-method), [Prime implicant](#prime-implicant).

<a id="quotient-rule"></a>**Quotient rule** — (f/g)' = (f'g − fg')/g², valid where g ≠ 0. *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="letter-r"></a>

## R

<a id="race-condition"></a>**Race condition** — A situation in which a simulation result depends on the arbitrary order in which concurrent processes execute, typically from blocking assignments in clocked blocks that read each other's outputs. *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md).

<a id="race-to-idle"></a>**Race to idle** — Running a task at full speed and then power-gating the hardware, instead of running it slowly; it uses less energy when leakage or the power of the rest of the system is large. *First defined in* [14-01](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-01-performance-power-iron-law.md). *See also:* [Dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS)](#dynamic-voltage-and-frequency-scaling-dvfs).

<a id="rack-scale-system"></a>**Rack-scale system** — An AI system designed and sold as a whole rack rather than as servers, with dozens of accelerators joined by one scale-up fabric, shared power shelves and liquid cooling, so that the rack behaves as one large accelerator. *First defined in* [27-07](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-07-ai-datacenter-server-and-rack.md). *See also:* [Scale-up fabric](#scale-up-fabric), [NVLink](#nvlink).

<a id="radian"></a>**Radian** — The angle that subtends an arc equal to the radius; 2π rad = 360° and 1 rad ≈ 57.30°. Calculus formulas for sin and cos hold only in radians. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md).

<a id="radiation-efficiency"></a>**Radiation efficiency** — The fraction of the power accepted by an antenna that it radiates, R_rad/(R_rad + R_loss); small antennas have low radiation resistance and hence often low efficiency. *First defined in* [13-11](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-11-radiation-and-antennas.md). *See also:* [Radiation resistance](#radiation-resistance), [Antenna gain](#antenna-gain).

<a id="radiation-pattern"></a>**Radiation pattern** — The angular distribution of an antenna's radiated power (or field) in the far field, usually normalized to its maximum and characterized by its half-power beamwidth, nulls and sidelobes. *First defined in* [13-11](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-11-radiation-and-antennas.md). *See also:* [Directivity](#directivity).

<a id="radiation-resistance"></a>**Radiation resistance** — The resistance that, carrying the antenna's terminal current, would dissipate the power it radiates, R_rad = 2P_rad/|I₀|²; about 73 Ω for a half-wave dipole and well under 1 Ω for electrically small antennas. *First defined in* [13-11](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-11-radiation-and-antennas.md). *See also:* [Hertzian dipole](#hertzian-dipole), [Radiation efficiency](#radiation-efficiency).

<a id="radiative-recombination"></a>**Radiative recombination** — Band-to-band recombination that emits a photon, at rate B(np − n_i²); weak in indirect-gap silicon (B = 1.1×10⁻¹⁴ cm³/s) and strong in direct-gap GaAs (7×10⁻¹⁰ cm³/s), where it powers LEDs and lasers. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="radius-of-convergence"></a>**Radius of convergence** — The distance from a power series' center within which it converges; it equals the distance to the nearest singularity, including complex ones. *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).
