<a id="second-order-intercept-point-ip2"></a>**Second-order intercept point (IP2)** — The extrapolated power at which second-order intermodulation products, growing 2 dB per dB, would equal the fundamental; critical in zero-IF receivers, where second-order products fall at DC on top of the wanted signal. *First defined in* [21-03](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-03-noise-figure-and-linearity.md). *See also:* [Third-order intercept point (IP3)](#third-order-intercept-point-ip3).

<a id="second-order-sections-sos"></a>**Second-order sections (SOS)** — The standard implementation of an IIR filter as a cascade of biquads, each holding one pole pair and one zero pair, which keeps coefficient rounding from moving the poles far (or outside the unit circle). *First defined in* [16-07](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-07-iir-filter-design.md). *See also:* [Biquad](#biquad), [IIR filter](#iir-filter).

<a id="secure-boot"></a>**Secure boot** — Booting only images whose signature verifies against a public key held in immutable or protected storage, starting from an immutable first stage (the root of trust). *First defined in* [18-08](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-08-boot-and-firmware-update.md). *See also:* [Bootloader](#bootloader), [Anti-rollback counter](#anti-rollback-counter).

<a id="secure-element"></a>**Secure element** — A separate tamper-resistant chip (or an isolated on-die enclave) that stores keys and performs cryptography, evaluated against physical side-channel and fault attacks. *First defined in* [18-11](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-11-hardware-security.md). *See also:* [Physical unclonable function (PUF)](#physical-unclonable-function-puf).

<a id="security-triad-cia"></a>**Security triad (CIA)** — Confidentiality, integrity and availability, the three properties network and information security aim to protect. *First defined in* [17-13](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-13-computer-networks-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Firewall](#firewall), [Penetration testing](#penetration-testing).

<a id="segmentation-dac"></a>**Segmentation (DAC)** — Building a DAC's most significant bits from equal (unary, thermometer-decoded) cells and its least significant bits from binary-weighted cells, trading decoder cost for much better DNL and smaller glitches at the major carries. *First defined in* [20-09](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-09-dacs.md). *See also:* [Current-steering DAC](#current-steering-dac), [Thermometer code](#thermometer-code).

<a id="selection-combining"></a>**Selection combining** — Using only the strongest of N diversity branches; it achieves diversity order N with one receiver chain, but its mean SNR gain is only Σ 1/k (1.5 for two branches) instead of MRC's N. *First defined in* [17-11](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-11-mimo-and-beamforming.md). *See also:* [Maximal-ratio combining](#maximal-ratio-combining), [Diversity order](#diversity-order).

<a id="selector-memory"></a>**Selector (memory)** — A two-terminal device in series with each cell of a cross-point array that conducts only above a threshold, blocking sneak-path currents through half-selected cells; 3D XPoint used an ovonic threshold switch. *First defined in* [23-08](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-08-emerging-memories.md). *See also:* [Sneak path](#sneak-path), [Threshold switching](#threshold-switching).

<a id="self-aligned-double-and-quadruple-patterning-sadp-saqp"></a>**Self-aligned double and quadruple patterning (SADP, SAQP)** — Spacer-based pitch division: sidewall spacers formed on a sacrificial mandrel become the pattern, halving (SADP) or quartering (SAQP) the pitch without a second critical exposure. *First defined in* [25-02](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-02-lithography.md). *See also:* [Pitch walk](#pitch-walk).

<a id="self-boosting-nand-program-inhibit"></a>**Self-boosting (NAND program inhibit)** — Protecting cells that share a programmed wordline: their bitlines are raised so the string floats, and its channel is capacitively boosted toward the program voltage, leaving too little field for tunneling. *First defined in* [23-06](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-06-nand-flash-and-3d-nand.md). *See also:* [Incremental step pulse programming (ISPP)](#incremental-step-pulse-programming-ispp), [NAND string](#nand-string).

<a id="self-checking-testbench"></a>**Self-checking testbench** — A testbench that compares the design's outputs with independently computed expected values and reports pass or fail automatically, rather than relying on a human reading waveforms. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="self-discharge"></a>**Self-discharge** — The loss of a battery's stored charge with no external load, quoted as a fraction of capacity per month or year; for multi-year products it can rival the electronics' own consumption. *First defined in* [18-09](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-09-ultra-low-power-design.md). *See also:* [Duty cycling](#duty-cycling).

<a id="self-loading"></a>**Self-loading** — The part of a gate's load that is its own drain (diffusion) capacitance and Miller-doubled gate–drain capacitance; it grows with the gate's width. Its ratio to the gate's input capacitance, γ = C_int/C_g, is typically between about 0.5 and 1. *First defined in* [19-02](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-02-cmos-inverter-dynamic.md). *See also:* [Intrinsic delay](#intrinsic-delay).

<a id="self-resonant-frequency"></a>**Self-resonant frequency** — The frequency at which an inductor's winding capacitance resonates with its inductance; above it the part behaves as a capacitor, not an inductor. *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="semantic-versioning"></a>**Semantic versioning** — MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version numbers where MAJOR signals incompatible changes, MINOR compatible new features and PATCH compatible fixes. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="semaphore"></a>**Semaphore** — A kernel counter with take (wait while zero, then decrement) and give (increment, waking a waiter); binary semaphores signal events such as an interrupt to a task, counting semaphores count events or free resources. It has no owner. *First defined in* [18-07](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-07-rtos-concepts.md). *See also:* [Mutex](#mutex).

<a id="semi-insulating-substrate"></a>**Semi-insulating substrate** — An undoped or compensated wafer (for example GaAs, with about 10⁸ Ω·cm intrinsic resistivity) that barely conducts, so microwave circuits built on it lose little signal to the substrate. *First defined in* [09-13](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-13-compound-and-wide-bandgap-semiconductors.md).

<a id="semihosting"></a>**Semihosting** — A debug mechanism in which target code executes BKPT 0xAB with a request in R0 and a debugger or emulator performs the I/O (print, file access, exit); convenient for tests, but it halts the core on each request. *First defined in* [18-02](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-02-bare-metal-c-and-toolchain.md). *See also:* [Debug probe](#debug-probe).

<a id="semilog-plot"></a>**Semilog plot** — A graph with one logarithmic axis (usually the vertical); an exponential function plots as a straight line on it. *First defined in* [01-01](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-01-functions-models-and-units.md).

<a id="sense-amplifier"></a>**Sense amplifier** — A regenerative circuit, usually a cross-coupled latch, that amplifies a small bitline voltage difference (around 100 mV) to full logic levels, so that memory reads need not wait for a full bitline swing. *First defined in* [19-08](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-08-sram-design.md). *See also:* [SRAM](#sram), [Metastability](#metastability).

<a id="sensitivity-tornado-analysis"></a>**Sensitivity (tornado) analysis** — Varying each input of a model by a set amount, one at a time, and ranking the inputs by the swing they cause in the output; the chart of sorted bars is called a tornado. *First defined in* [26-03](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-03-engineering-economics-1.md).

<a id="sensitivity-function"></a>**Sensitivity function** — S(s) = 1/(1 + L(s)), the transfer function from reference to error in a unity-feedback loop; it scales how much of a disturbance reaches the output and how strongly plant variations affect the closed loop. Small |S| means good tracking and rejection. *First defined in* [15-02](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-02-transfer-functions-and-block-diagrams.md). *See also:* [Complementary sensitivity](#complementary-sensitivity), [Desensitivity factor](#desensitivity-factor).

<a id="sensitivity-peak"></a>**Sensitivity peak** — M_s = max |S(jω)| = 1/(min |1 + L(jω)|), the reciprocal of the Nyquist plot's closest approach to −1; a single robustness number that guarantees GM ≥ M_s/(M_s − 1) and PM ≥ 2 arcsin(1/(2M_s)). *First defined in* [15-07](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-07-frequency-domain-design.md). *See also:* [Sensitivity function](#sensitivity-function).

<a id="sensor-hub"></a>**Sensor hub** — A low-power processor (or dedicated block) that collects and processes sensor data (fusion, step counting, gesture and activity detection) while the main application processor sleeps. *First defined in* [18-10](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-10-sensors.md). *See also:* [Duty cycling](#duty-cycling).

<a id="separable-equation"></a>**Separable equation** — A first-order equation y' = a(t)b(y), solved by integrating dy/b(y) = a(t) dt; constant solutions where b(y) = 0 must be checked separately. *First defined in* [02-02](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-02-first-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="separation-of-variables"></a>**Separation of variables** — Solving a partial differential equation by trying products of one-variable functions; each factor satisfies an ordinary differential equation with a separation constant, and boundary conditions select a series of such products. *First defined in* [13-02](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-02-electrostatics-boundary-value-problems.md). *See also:* [Laplace's equation](#laplaces-equation), [Fourier series](#fourier-series).

<a id="separation-principle"></a>**Separation principle** — With state feedback acting on observer estimates, the closed-loop eigenvalues are those of A − BK together with those of A − LC, so the controller and the observer can be designed independently. *First defined in* [15-10](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-10-state-space-introduction.md). *See also:* [Pole placement](#pole-placement), [State observer](#state-observer).

<a id="sepic"></a>**SEPIC** — The single-ended primary-inductance converter, a non-inverting step-up/step-down converter with two inductors and a series coupling capacitor that averages the input voltage, V = D·V_in/(1 − D), with continuous input current. *First defined in* [22-03](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-03-boost-buck-boost-topologies.md). *See also:* [Ćuk converter](#cuk-converter).

<a id="sequence"></a>**Sequence** — An ordered list a₁, a₂, a₃, …; it converges to L if its terms approach L as n grows. *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).

<a id="sequencing-overhead"></a>**Sequencing overhead** — The part of every clock cycle consumed by registers rather than logic, t_pcq + t_setup for flip-flops, plus clock uncertainty. Its share of the cycle grows as pipelines deepen; it is often quoted in FO4 delays. *First defined in* [19-07](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-07-sequential-timing-and-clocking.md). *See also:* [Setup time](#setup-time), [FO4 delay](#fo4-delay).

<a id="sequential-consistency"></a>**Sequential consistency** — The memory model (Lamport, 1979) in which every execution behaves as if all cores' operations occurred in one global order that respects each core's program order. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Memory consistency model](#memory-consistency-model).

<a id="serializer-and-deserializer"></a>**Serializer and deserializer** — The circuits (SerDes) that convert a parallel word into a fast serial bit stream for transmission and back again at the receiver, built around shift registers and a clock multiplied or recovered to the bit rate. *First defined in* [08-07](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-07-registers-counters-shift-registers.md). *See also:* [Shift register](#shift-register).

<a id="series"></a>**Series** — An infinite sum Σ a_k, defined as the limit of its partial sums; it converges if that limit is finite. *First defined in* [01-08](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-08-sequences-series-and-taylor.md).

<a id="series-connection"></a>**Series connection** — Elements joined end to end with nothing else connected at the nodes between them, so they carry the same current; series resistances add. *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md). *See also:* [Voltage divider](#voltage-divider).

<a id="series-termination"></a>**Series termination** — A resistor at a driver that brings its output resistance up to the line's Z₀, so that the reflection from an open receiver is absorbed at the source; the receiver sees one clean edge and no DC power is spent. *First defined in* [13-07](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-07-transmission-lines-time-domain.md). *See also:* [Parallel termination](#parallel-termination).

<a id="series-parallel-equivalent"></a>**Series–parallel equivalent** — The pair of two-element models (R_s + jX_s in series, or R_p ∥ jX_p) that have the same impedance at one frequency; R_p = R_s(1 + Q²) and X_p = X_s(1 + 1/Q²). LCR meters report capacitance and inductance in either model, and the two differ by the factor 1 + D². *First defined in* [07-05](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-05-sinusoidal-steady-state-and-impedance.md).

<a id="set-associative-cache"></a>**Set-associative cache** — A cache divided into sets of A lines (ways); a block may be placed in any way of the one set its index selects, and a replacement policy picks the victim within the set. *First defined in* [14-09](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-09-memory-hierarchy-and-caches.md). *See also:* [Direct-mapped cache](#direct-mapped-cache), [Fully associative cache](#fully-associative-cache).

<a id="set-cover-problem"></a>**Set-cover problem** — Choosing the fewest (or cheapest) sets from a collection so that their union covers every element; it is NP-hard, which is why exact logic minimization does not scale and tools use heuristics. *First defined in* [08-03](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-03-logic-minimization.md).

<a id="setpoint-weighting"></a>**Setpoint weighting** — Applying a PID's proportional and derivative actions to b·r − y and c·r − y (with 0 ≤ b, c ≤ 1) instead of the full error; it softens the response to setpoint changes without changing stability, steady-state accuracy or disturbance rejection. *First defined in* [15-08](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-08-pid-control.md). *See also:* [PID controller](#pid-controller), [Derivative kick](#derivative-kick).

<a id="settling-time"></a>**Settling time** — The time a response takes to come and stay within a specified error band of its final value; τ·ln(1/ε) for a first-order system, and (N+1)·ln 2 · τ to reach ½ LSB of an N-bit converter. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md).

<a id="setup-time"></a>**Setup time** — The minimum time a flip-flop's data input must be stable before the active clock edge; together with clock-to-Q and logic delay it sets the minimum clock period, t_pcq + t_pd + t_setup ≤ T_c. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md). *See also:* [Hold time](#hold-time), [Clock-to-Q delay](#clock-to-q-delay).

<a id="shadow-price"></a>**Shadow price** — The value of one more unit of a binding constraint in the units of the objective; under a power cap with dynamic power proportional to f³, a watt is worth 1/(3P_dyn) of performance at the margin. *First defined in* [27-01](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-01-system-analysis-method.md). *See also:* [Sustained power](#sustained-power).

<a id="shadowing"></a>**Shadowing** — Location-to-location variation of the local mean received power caused by obstacles, modelled as a Gaussian term in decibels with standard deviation σ (about 3–8 dB); covering it with probability p needs a margin σ·Q⁻¹(1 − p). *First defined in* [17-09](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-09-wireless-channels.md). *See also:* [Path loss](#path-loss), [Outage probability](#outage-probability).

<a id="shallow-trench-isolation-sti"></a>**Shallow trench isolation (STI)** — Oxide-filled trenches etched between transistors to isolate them electrically, lined with a thin thermal oxide and planarized by chemical-mechanical polishing. *First defined in* [25-01](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-01-process-flow-overview.md).

<a id="shannon-capacity"></a>**Shannon capacity** — The maximum error-free data rate of a channel with bandwidth B and signal-to-noise ratio SNR, C = B log2(1 + SNR). *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="shannon-expansion"></a>**Shannon expansion** — F = A'·F(A=0) + A·F(A=1), splitting a function on one variable into two cofactors; it is the logic of a 2:1 multiplexer and the basis of decision diagrams and lookup tables. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md).

<a id="shannon-limit"></a>**Shannon limit** — The minimum Eb/N0 for reliable communication at spectral efficiency η, (2^η − 1)/η; it falls to ln 2 = −1.59 dB as bandwidth grows without limit. *First defined in* [17-07](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-07-information-theory-and-shannon.md). *See also:* [Shannon–Hartley theorem](#shannon-hartley-theorem), [Eb/N0](#eb-n0).

<a id="shannon-hartley-theorem"></a>**Shannon–Hartley theorem** — The capacity of a band-limited channel with additive white Gaussian noise, C = B log2(1 + S/(N0·B)) bits per second; linear in bandwidth and logarithmic in power at high SNR, proportional to power at low SNR. *First defined in* [17-07](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-07-information-theory-and-shannon.md). *See also:* [Channel capacity](#channel-capacity), [Shannon limit](#shannon-limit), [Shannon capacity](#shannon-capacity).

<a id="shared-memory-gpu"></a>**Shared memory (GPU)** — A software-managed on-chip scratchpad in each SM, shared by the threads of a block and divided into banks, used to stage data for reuse. *First defined in* [14-13](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-13-gpus-and-simt.md). *See also:* [Bank conflict](#bank-conflict).

<a id="sheet-resistance"></a>**Sheet resistance** — The resistance of a square of a thin film, R_s = ρ/t (Ω/□); a trace's resistance is R_s times its number of squares, L/W. *First defined in* [04-05](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-05-current-resistance-and-conduction.md).

<a id="shielding-effectiveness"></a>**Shielding effectiveness** — The reduction, in dB, of a field by a barrier; for a solid conducting sheet roughly the absorption loss 8.686 t/δ plus the reflection loss 20 log₁₀(η₀/4|η_c|). Real enclosures are usually limited by seams and apertures instead. *First defined in* [13-06](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-06-reflection-and-transmission.md). *See also:* [Skin depth](#skin-depth).

<a id="shift-register"></a>**Shift register** — A chain of flip-flops in which each clock edge moves every bit one stage along; with parallel load and output it converts between parallel words and serial bit streams. *First defined in* [08-07](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-07-registers-counters-shift-registers.md). *See also:* [Register](#register), [Serializer and deserializer](#serializer-and-deserializer).

<a id="shmoo-plot"></a>**Shmoo plot** — A pass/fail map of a chip over two swept conditions, usually supply voltage and frequency; its boundary is the operating envelope, and holes or bends in it point to marginal circuits. *First defined in* [25-12](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-12-post-silicon-validation.md). *See also:* [Minimum operating voltage (Vmin)](#minimum-operating-voltage-vmin).

<a id="shockley-read-hall-recombination"></a>**Shockley–Read–Hall recombination** — Two-step recombination through a trap level in the gap, at net rate (np − n_i²)/[τ_p0(n + n_1) + τ_n0(p + p_1)]; the dominant mechanism in moderately doped silicon, most effective for traps near mid-gap. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md). *See also:* [Trap](#trap), [Capture cross section](#capture-cross-section).

<a id="shoreline-bandwidth-density"></a>**Shoreline bandwidth density** — Die-to-die bandwidth per millimetre of die edge, the areal density of the bump field times its usable depth; it decides whether a die has enough edge for its memory, I/O and chiplet links. *First defined in* [24-06](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-06-d2d-memory-phys-scale-up.md). *See also:* [Bump pitch](#bump-pitch).

<a id="short-circuit"></a>**Short circuit** — An element or connection with zero voltage across it whatever its current (R = 0); an ideal wire or a closed ideal switch. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md). *See also:* [Open circuit](#open-circuit).

<a id="short-diode"></a>**Short diode** — A diode whose neutral region is much shorter than a diffusion length, so the excess-carrier profile is a straight line, the diffusion length in I_s is replaced by the region width, and the stored charge is set by the transit time W²/2D rather than the lifetime. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md).

<a id="short-channel-effects"></a>**Short-channel effects** — The departures of a small MOSFET from long-channel behavior caused by velocity saturation and by the source and drain sharing control of the channel with the gate, chiefly threshold roll-off, DIBL, degraded swing and higher output conductance. *First defined in* [09-10](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-10-short-channel-effects-and-leakage.md).

<a id="short-circuit-current"></a>**Short-circuit current** — The current a source or network would deliver into a short circuit, I_sc = V_oc/R_int for a linear model; a model parameter, not a safe operating point. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md).

<a id="short-circuit-power"></a>**Short-circuit power** — Power drawn while both transistors of a CMOS gate conduct during an input transition. For an unloaded symmetric inverter with input ramps of duration τ, Veendrick's formula gives (β/12)(V_DD − 2V_TH)³τ/T; it vanishes when V_DD < 2V_T. *First defined in* [19-06](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-06-power-and-low-power-design.md). *See also:* [Dynamic power](#dynamic-power).

<a id="short-circuit-ratio"></a>**Short-circuit ratio** — The fault MVA at a connection point divided by the rating of the plant or load connected there; low ratios (a weak grid) make voltage swing with power and challenge inverter controls. *First defined in* [22-12](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-12-power-systems-fundamentals.md).

<a id="short-circuit-time-constants"></a>**Short-circuit time constants** — The time constants R_isC_i of coupling and bypass capacitors, each found with the other low-frequency capacitors shorted; the sum Σ 1/(R_isC_i) is a conservative estimate of the lower −3 dB frequency. *First defined in* [12-04](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-04-high-frequency-analysis-methods.md). *See also:* [Open-circuit time constants](#open-circuit-time-constants).

<a id="shot-noise"></a>**Shot noise** — Noise from the random, independent arrival of discrete charges across a barrier, with one-sided density 2qI; it follows from Poisson statistics. *First defined in* [03-06](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-06-random-processes-preview.md).

<a id="si-base-units"></a>**SI base units** — The seven base units of the International System of Units (kg, m, s, A, K, mol, cd), from which all others, including V, Ω, F and H, are derived. *First defined in* [00-03](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-03-how-to-study-this-curriculum.md).

<a id="side-channel"></a>**Side channel** — An unintended leak of information through physical behavior such as timing, power consumption or electromagnetic emission, which can reveal secrets that the logical abstraction hides. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md).

<a id="side-channel-attack"></a>**Side-channel attack** — Extracting secrets from physical effects of computation (time, power, electromagnetic emission) rather than from the algorithm's inputs and outputs. *First defined in* [18-11](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-11-hardware-security.md). *See also:* [Correlation power analysis (CPA)](#correlation-power-analysis-cpa), [Constant-time code](#constant-time-code).

<a id="sifting-property"></a>**Sifting property** — ∫ f(t) δ(t − t₀) dt = f(t₀) when t₀ lies inside the integration range (and 0 otherwise); in discrete time, Σ f[n] δ[n − n₀] = f[n₀]. It is the defining action of the impulse. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md). *See also:* [Unit impulse](#unit-impulse).

<a id="sign-extension"></a>**Sign extension** — Widening a two's-complement value by copying its sign bit into the new high bits (8-bit 0xFB, −5, becomes 16-bit 0xFFFB); needed by hand for odd-width fields such as 12-bit sensor readings, e.g. (x XOR 2^(k−1)) − 2^(k−1). *First defined in* [05-07](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-07-bit-manipulation.md).

<a id="sign-sign-lms"></a>**Sign-sign LMS** — The hardware form of least-mean-squares adaptation, c_k ← c_k + μ·sgn(e_n)·sgn(x_{n−k}), needing only comparators and counters; it converges where the error is uncorrelated with each tap's input and then dithers by ±μ. *First defined in* [24-03](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-03-serdes-architecture.md). *See also:* [Decision-feedback equalizer (DFE)](#decision-feedback-equalizer-dfe).

<a id="signal-space"></a>**Signal space** — The representation of a set of waveforms as vectors in an orthonormal basis, in which energies are squared lengths, distances set error probabilities, and white noise has independent components of variance N0/2 in every direction. *First defined in* [17-05](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-05-matched-filters-and-detection.md). *See also:* [Gram–Schmidt procedure](#gram-schmidt-procedure), [Sufficient statistic](#sufficient-statistic).

<a id="signal-transfer-function-stf"></a>**Signal transfer function (STF)** — In the linear model of a delta-sigma modulator, the transfer function from the input to the output; usually a pure delay or a gentle low-pass in band. *First defined in* [20-08](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-08-sigma-delta-converters.md). *See also:* [Noise transfer function (NTF)](#noise-transfer-function-ntf).

<a id="signal-flow-graph"></a>**Signal-flow graph** — A graph whose nodes are signals and whose directed branches carry gains; each node equals the sum of its incoming branch gains times their source nodes. It is the input form for Mason's gain formula. *First defined in* [15-02](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-02-transfer-functions-and-block-diagrams.md). *See also:* [Mason's gain formula](#masons-gain-formula), [Block diagram](#block-diagram).

<a id="signal-to-noise-ratio"></a>**Signal-to-noise ratio** — The ratio of a signal's power to the noise power in the same bandwidth, usually in decibels, 10 log(P_s/P_n) = 20 log(V_s,rms/v_n,rms); a noise density alone does not fix it until the bandwidth is stated. *First defined in* [12-10](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-10-noise-in-circuits.md). *See also:* [Noise figure](#noise-figure), [Thermal noise](#thermal-noise).

<a id="signoff"></a>**Signoff** — The final set of independent checks a design must pass before tape-out: timing at every mode and corner with extracted parasitics, IR drop and electromigration, DRC, LVS, antenna and density rules, and logical equivalence. *First defined in* [19-11](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-11-place-route-signoff.md). *See also:* [Tape-out](#tape-out), [Design-rule check (DRC)](#design-rule-check-drc), [Layout versus schematic (LVS)](#layout-versus-schematic-lvs).

<a id="silent-data-corruption"></a>**Silent data corruption** — Wrong results produced by hardware without any error being signaled; at datacenter scale, rare defective or degrading processor cores make it a measurable fleet-level problem addressed by in-field screening. *First defined in* [19-12](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-12-design-for-test.md). *See also:* [Built-in self-test (BIST)](#built-in-self-test-bist).

<a id="silicon-bridge-emib-lsi"></a>**Silicon bridge (EMIB, LSI)** — A small silicon die with fine wiring embedded only where two dies meet, either in the package substrate (Intel's EMIB) or in an RDL interposer (TSMC's local silicon interconnect in CoWoS-L), giving interposer-class wiring without a full silicon interposer. *First defined in* [25-07](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-07-advanced-packaging-and-chiplets.md). *See also:* [2.5D integration](#2-5d-integration).

<a id="silicon-interposer"></a>**Silicon interposer** — A silicon substrate with fine wiring on which a processor and HBM stacks sit side by side, providing thousands of short, unterminated connections between them (2.5D packaging). *First defined in* [23-05](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-05-hbm-in-depth.md). *See also:* [CoWoS](#cowos).

<a id="silicon-photonics"></a>**Silicon photonics** — Building optical components (waveguides, splitters, modulators, multiplexers and germanium photodiodes) on silicon wafers in CMOS-style fabs; silicon is transparent at 1310 and 1550 nm but cannot detect that light or lase, so detectors are germanium and lasers are III-V. *First defined in* [24-08](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-08-silicon-photonics.md). *See also:* [Photonic integrated circuit (PIC)](#photonic-integrated-circuit-pic), [Grating coupler](#grating-coupler).

<a id="silicon-on-insulator"></a>**Silicon-on-insulator** — A wafer with a thin crystalline silicon layer on a buried oxide over a silicon substrate (SOI), made for example by hydrogen implantation, bonding and splitting; it removes junction capacitance and enables thin-body transistors. *First defined in* [09-12](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-12-finfet-gaa-cfet-backside-power.md).

<a id="silicon-proven-ip"></a>**Silicon-proven IP** — An IP block that already works in a manufactured and tested chip on the target process, which lowers the respin and schedule risk of using it. *First defined in* [26-04](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-04-engineering-economics-2.md).

<a id="simd"></a>**SIMD** — Single instruction, multiple data; one instruction operates on several values packed in a wide register (for example eight 16-bit lanes of a 128-bit vector), multiplying the MACs per instruction. *First defined in* [16-11](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-11-dsp-hardware-architectures.md). *See also:* [VLIW](#vliw).

<a id="similarity-transformation"></a>**Similarity transformation** — A change of state coordinates x = T z, which turns (A, B, C) into (T⁻¹AT, T⁻¹B, CT); it preserves the eigenvalues and the transfer function, and is used to reach canonical (controllable or modal) forms. *First defined in* [15-10](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-10-state-space-introduction.md). *See also:* [State-space model](#state-space-model).

<a id="simple-harmonic-oscillator"></a>**Simple harmonic oscillator** — A system whose restoring force is proportional to displacement, m ẍ = −k_s x, which oscillates sinusoidally at ω₀ = √(k_s/m) while energy sloshes between kinetic and potential stores. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md). *See also:* [Quality factor](#quality-factor), [Force–voltage analogy](#force-voltage-analogy).

<a id="simpsons-rule"></a>**Simpson's rule** — Numerical integration fitting parabolas through triples of samples, with weights h/3 × (1, 4, 2, 4, …, 4, 1); its error falls as h⁴. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="simt"></a>**SIMT** — Single instruction, multiple threads; the GPU execution model in which scalar per-thread programs are grouped into warps that share one instruction stream, with an active mask handling divergence. *First defined in* [14-13](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-13-gpus-and-simt.md). *See also:* [Warp](#warp), [Branch divergence](#branch-divergence).

<a id="simultaneous-switching-noise-ssn"></a>**Simultaneous switching noise (SSN)** — Ground or supply bounce L·N·ΔI/tr when many drivers sharing a return or supply inductance switch together; differential signalling largely avoids it. *First defined in* [24-01](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-01-signal-integrity-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Target impedance](#target-impedance), [Crosstalk](#crosstalk).

<a id="sinad"></a>**SINAD** — Signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio: the power of the fundamental over everything else except DC, in dB; ENOB = (SINAD − 1.76)/6.02 for a full-scale test. *First defined in* [16-05](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-05-spectral-analysis-and-windowing.md). *See also:* [Effective number of bits (ENOB)](#effective-number-of-bits-enob), [Spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR)](#spurious-free-dynamic-range-sfdr).

<a id="sinc-function"></a>**Sinc function** — sin(x)/x (sometimes normalized as sin(πx)/(πx)); its removable discontinuity at 0 is filled with the limit 1. It appears throughout sampling and Fourier analysis. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="sinc-interpolation"></a>**Sinc interpolation** — Ideal reconstruction of a band-limited signal from its samples, x(t) = Σ x[n] sinc((t − nT)/T): each sample launches a sinc pulse that passes through its own sample and through zero at all the others. *First defined in* [11-10](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-10-sampling-aliasing-reconstruction.md). *See also:* [Sampling theorem](#sampling-theorem), [Zero-order hold](#zero-order-hold).

<a id="single-cycle-processor"></a>**Single-cycle processor** — A processor that completes every instruction in one clock cycle (CPI = 1), so its clock period is set by the slowest instruction, typically a load. *First defined in* [14-05](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-05-single-cycle-datapath.md). *See also:* [Multi-cycle processor](#multi-cycle-processor).

<a id="single-event-upset-seu"></a>**Single-event upset (SEU)** — A bit flipped in a storage element by the charge from a particle strike, without permanent damage; a concern for state registers in automotive, aerospace and large-fleet systems. *First defined in* [08-08](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-08-finite-state-machines.md). *See also:* [Illegal state](#illegal-state).

<a id="single-photon-avalanche-diode"></a>**Single-photon avalanche diode** — A junction biased above breakdown so that one photogenerated carrier triggers a self-sustaining avalanche (SPAD, Geiger mode), giving a digital pulse per detected photon, followed by quenching and a dead time. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md). *See also:* [Avalanche photodiode](#avalanche-photodiode), [Photon detection efficiency](#photon-detection-efficiency).

<a id="single-point-fault-metric-spfm"></a>**Single-point fault metric (SPFM)** — One minus the fraction of the safety-related failure rate made up of single-point and residual faults; ISO 26262 targets are at least 90%, 97% and 99% for ASIL B, C and D. *First defined in* [25-10](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-10-qualification-and-functional-safety.md). *See also:* [Latent-fault metric (LFM)](#latent-fault-metric-lfm), [PMHF](#pmhf).

<a id="single-sideband-modulation"></a>**Single-sideband modulation** — Amplitude modulation that transmits only one sideband, (A/2)·[m cos(ωct) ∓ m̂ sin(ωct)], halving the bandwidth to W with the same output SNR as DSB for the same received power; it needs coherent detection but tolerates small frequency errors as a pitch shift. *First defined in* [17-03](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-03-analog-modulation.md). *See also:* [Hilbert transform](#hilbert-transform), [DSB-SC modulation](#dsb-sc-modulation).

<a id="single-stub-matching"></a>**Single-stub matching** — Matching with a length of line that brings the load's admittance onto the unit-conductance circle, followed by a shunt stub that cancels the remaining susceptance; there are two solutions per half wavelength. *First defined in* [13-09](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-09-smith-chart-and-matching.md). *See also:* [Stub](#stub), [Smith chart](#smith-chart).

<a id="singular-matrix"></a>**Singular matrix** — A square matrix whose columns are dependent, so Ax = b has no solution for most b and infinitely many for the rest; elimination on it cannot produce a full set of nonzero pivots. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="singular-value-decomposition"></a>**Singular value decomposition** — A = UΣVᵀ for any matrix, with orthogonal U and V and non-negative singular values on the diagonal of Σ; it maps the unit sphere to an ellipsoid with semi-axes σᵢ. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md). *See also:* [Low-rank approximation](#low-rank-approximation), [Condition number](#condition-number).

<a id="sinusoid"></a>**Sinusoid** — A signal of the form A cos(ωt + φ), with amplitude A, angular frequency ω and phase φ. This curriculum always uses the cosine as the reference form. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="sinusoidal-steady-state"></a>**Sinusoidal steady state** — The response of a stable linear system to a sinusoidal input after transients have died out, a sinusoid at the input frequency whose amplitude and phase follow from phasor analysis. *First defined in* [02-01](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-01-complex-numbers-euler-and-phasors.md).

<a id="skin-depth"></a>**Skin depth** — The depth δ = 1/√(πfµσ) at which a field entering a good conductor falls by a factor e; 2.1 µm in copper at 1 GHz. The current flows mostly within a few skin depths of the surface. *First defined in* [13-05](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-05-plane-waves.md). *See also:* [Skin effect](#skin-effect), [Surface resistance](#surface-resistance).

<a id="skin-effect"></a>**Skin effect** — The crowding of AC current toward a conductor's surface, within a skin depth δ = √(ρ/(πfμ)) (about 0.21 mm in copper at 100 kHz), which raises resistance at high frequency. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="slack"></a>**Slack** — The margin by which a timing path meets its constraint, the required time minus the arrival time; negative slack is a violation. *First defined in* [08-10](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-10-timing-metastability-cdc.md). *See also:* [Static timing analysis (STA)](#static-timing-analysis-sta).

<a id="slc-cache"></a>**SLC cache** — Flash blocks run temporarily in one-bit-per-cell mode to absorb write bursts at high speed; data is later folded into TLC or QLC blocks, and writes slow sharply once the cache is full. *First defined in* [23-07](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-07-ssd-controllers.md). *See also:* [Multi-level cell (MLC, TLC, QLC)](#multi-level-cell-mlc-tlc-qlc).

<a id="slew-rate"></a>**Slew rate** — The maximum rate of change dv/dt an amplifier's output can produce, usually in V/µs; it limits the full-power bandwidth to SR/(2πV_p). *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="slip"></a>**Slip** — The induction machine's fractional speed deficit, s = (n_s − n)/n_s; it sets the rotor's current frequency sf, and the rotor copper loss is s times the air-gap power. *First defined in* [22-11](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-11-electric-machines.md). *See also:* [Synchronous speed](#synchronous-speed), [Induction machine](#induction-machine).

<a id="slope-compensation"></a>**Slope compensation** — An artificial ramp added to the sensed current (or subtracted from the control level) in peak current-mode control; a slope above half the inductor's down-slope makes the current loop stable at every duty cycle. *First defined in* [22-07](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-07-converter-dynamics-and-control.md).

<a id="small-ripple-approximation"></a>**Small-ripple approximation** — Treating a converter's output voltage as constant at its DC value when writing the inductor's voltage in each subinterval, valid because the output ripple is a small fraction of the DC value; never applied to the inductor current, whose ripple is deliberately large. *First defined in* [22-02](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-02-buck-converter-steady-state.md). *See also:* [Volt-second balance](#volt-second-balance), [Charge balance](#charge-balance).

<a id="small-signal-conductance"></a>**Small-signal conductance** — The slope dI/dV of a nonlinear device's I–V curve at its operating point; for a diode g_d ≈ I/V_T, so r_d = V_T/I ≈ 26 Ω at 1 mA. *First defined in* [01-03](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-03-derivatives.md).

<a id="small-signal-model"></a>**Small-signal model** — A linear model of a nonlinear device valid for small deviations about a DC operating point, built from slopes such as g_d = dI/dV or a transistor's g_m. *First defined in* [01-04](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-04-applications-of-derivatives.md).

<a id="small-signal-resistance"></a>**Small-signal resistance** — The inverse slope of a diode's exponential characteristic at its bias point, r_d = nV_T/I_D (25.9 Ω at 1 mA for n = 1), valid for signals much smaller than 2nV_T. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md). *See also:* [Small-signal model](#small-signal-model).

<a id="smallest-saleable-compliant-implementation"></a>**Smallest saleable compliant implementation** — In IEEE SA's patent policy, the smallest product that implements the standard (often a chip), named as one optional value level for judging a reasonable royalty, alongside other appropriate value levels. *First defined in* [26-02](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-02-design-reviews-and-standards.md). *See also:* [Royalty stacking](#royalty-stacking).

<a id="smart-power-stage"></a>**Smart power stage** — A single package (often 5 × 6 mm) holding a buck phase's high- and low-side MOSFETs, gate driver and current and temperature monitors, rated for tens of amperes; also called DrMOS. *First defined in* [22-10](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-10-datacenter-power-delivery.md).

<a id="smith-chart"></a>**Smith chart** — The unit disc of the reflection coefficient Γ with circles of constant normalized resistance and reactance drawn on it, so that impedance transformations along lines and by series or shunt elements become rotations and moves along circles. *First defined in* [13-09](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-09-smith-chart-and-matching.md). *See also:* [Reflection coefficient](#reflection-coefficient), [Normalized impedance](#normalized-impedance).

<a id="sneak-path"></a>**Sneak path** — A parasitic current path through unselected cells of a transistor-less cross-point array that swamps the selected cell's signal unless each cell has a selector. *First defined in* [23-08](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-08-emerging-memories.md). *See also:* [Selector (memory)](#selector-memory).

<a id="snells-law"></a>**Snell's law** — n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂ for refraction at a boundary (angles from the normal), from requiring wavefronts to match along the surface. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="snooping"></a>**Snooping** — Cache coherence by broadcast, in which every cache observes all requests on a shared bus or broadcast network and updates or supplies its copies accordingly; simple and fast, but limited in scalability. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Directory protocol](#directory-protocol).

<a id="snubber"></a>**Snubber** — A network, usually a resistor in series with a capacitor, placed across a ringing switch or tank to damp it; the rule of thumb is R ≈ √(L/C) of the parasitic tank and C several times its capacitance, at a cost of C·V²·f_sw in power. *First defined in* [07-03](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-03-second-order-rlc-transients.md).

<a id="soft-buffer"></a>**Soft buffer** — The memory in which a receiver keeps the soft values (LLRs) of each unfinished HARQ block so that retransmissions can be combined; tens of megabytes for a wide carrier at peak rate. *First defined in* [21-12](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-12-modem-baseband-and-standards.md). *See also:* [Hybrid ARQ (HARQ)](#hybrid-arq-harq), [Limited-buffer rate matching](#limited-buffer-rate-matching).

<a id="soft-decision"></a>**Soft decision** — Passing the demodulator's reliability information (amplitude or log-likelihood ratio) to the decoder instead of hard bits; worth about 1.6–2 dB of Eb/N0 for binary signalling. *First defined in* [17-07](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-07-information-theory-and-shannon.md). *See also:* [Shannon limit](#shannon-limit).

<a id="soft-error"></a>**Soft error** — A non-destructive change of a stored bit caused by a particle strike (neutrons or alpha particles); it is corrected by rewriting, and its rate is quoted in FIT per megabit. *First defined in* [03-02](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-02-random-variables-and-distributions.md).

<a id="soft-ip"></a>**Soft IP** — An IP block delivered as synthesizable RTL, portable across processes but needing synthesis, timing closure and verification on each one. *First defined in* [26-04](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-04-engineering-economics-2.md). *See also:* [Hard IP](#hard-ip).

<a id="soft-saturation"></a>**Soft saturation** — The gradual fall of a powder core's inductance with DC bias as its particles saturate progressively, in contrast with the abrupt collapse of a gapped ferrite. *First defined in* [22-05](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-05-magnetics-design.md). *See also:* [Powder core](#powder-core), [Saturation current](#saturation-current).

<a id="soft-start"></a>**Soft start** — Ramping a regulator's output or a load switch's current slowly at turn-on so the charging current C dV/dt stays small; it lowers the peak inrush current but not the energy dissipated, which is ½CV² whatever the ramp. *First defined in* [22-08](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-08-pmics.md). *See also:* [Inrush current](#inrush-current), [Load switch](#load-switch).

<a id="soft-switching"></a>**Soft switching** — Arranging a converter so that each switch turns on at zero voltage or off at zero current, removing the overlap and output-charge losses; the energy is recycled by the circuit's inductance instead. *First defined in* [22-06](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-06-converter-losses-and-wide-bandgap.md). *See also:* [Zero-voltage switching](#zero-voltage-switching), [Zero-current switching](#zero-current-switching).

<a id="software-defined-radio-sdr"></a>**Software-defined radio (SDR)** — A radio whose frequency, bandwidth and waveform are set largely in software, either by digitizing close to the antenna or by a widely tunable analog front end followed by programmable sampling and filtering. *First defined in* [21-08](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-08-transceiver-architectures.md). *See also:* [Direct RF sampling](#direct-rf-sampling).

<a id="software-defined-vehicle"></a>**Software-defined vehicle** — A vehicle whose features are defined mainly by software running on central compute with headroom, a service-oriented platform and over-the-air updates, so behaviour can change over the vehicle's life. *First defined in* [27-06](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-06-automotive-ee-architecture.md). *See also:* [Central compute (vehicle)](#central-compute-vehicle), [Over-the-air (OTA) update](#over-the-air-ota-update).

<a id="solenoid"></a>**Solenoid** — A long helical coil whose interior field is nearly uniform, B = µ₀nI with n turns per meter, and whose exterior field is small. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="solid-angle"></a>**Solid angle** — The 3-D analogue of an angle, Ω = A/r², the area a cone cuts from a sphere over the radius squared, in steradians; a full sphere is 4π sr. *First defined in* [04-03](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-03-gauss-law.md).

<a id="solid-electrolyte-interphase-sei"></a>**Solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI)** — A passivating film that forms on a lithium-ion anode from electrolyte decomposition; its slow, diffusion-limited growth consumes lithium and causes calendar capacity fade roughly proportional to √t. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md). *See also:* [Calendar aging](#calendar-aging).

<a id="sound-pressure-level-spl"></a>**Sound pressure level (SPL)** — 20 log10 of the rms sound pressure relative to 20 µPa; 1 Pa rms is 94 dB SPL, the reference level at which microphone sensitivity and SNR are specified. *First defined in* [18-10](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-10-sensors.md). *See also:* [Pulse-density modulation (PDM)](#pulse-density-modulation-pdm).

<a id="source-degeneration"></a>**Source degeneration** — A resistor R_S in a transistor's source (or R_E in a bipolar emitter) that feeds back a voltage opposing the input, cutting the gain to about −R_D/(R_S + 1/g_m) but making it set by resistors rather than by the device. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [Transconductance](#transconductance).

<a id="source-follower"></a>**Source follower** — The common-drain MOSFET stage, with the input at the gate and the output at the source; a voltage buffer with gain g_mR_eq/(1 + g_mR_eq), below 1/(1 + χ) with the body effect, and output resistance about 1/(g_m + g_mb). *First defined in* [10-06](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-06-mos-single-stage-amplifiers.md). *See also:* [Buffer amplifier](#buffer-amplifier), [Body transconductance](#body-transconductance).

<a id="source-injection-velocity"></a>**Source injection velocity** — The x-directed thermal velocity v_thx (about 1.6 × 10⁷ cm/s for electrons in silicon MOSFETs) with which carriers enter the channel from the source; it sets the ceiling I_Dsat = W B v_thx C_ox (V_GS − V_TH), where B is the fraction not scattered back. *First defined in* [09-10](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-10-short-channel-effects-and-leakage.md). *See also:* [Ballistic transport](#ballistic-transport), [Velocity saturation](#velocity-saturation).

<a id="source-transformation"></a>**Source transformation** — Replacing a voltage source V_s in series with R by a current source V_s/R in parallel with R, or the reverse; the two are equivalent at their terminals but not internally. *First defined in* [06-07](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-07-linearity-and-superposition.md). *See also:* [Millman's theorem](#millmans-theorem).

<a id="space-vector-pwm"></a>**Space-vector PWM** — Inverter modulation, equivalent to adding a common-mode third harmonic to sine-triangle PWM, that raises the maximum linear line-to-line output from 0.612 V_dc to V_dc/√2 (15.5% more). *First defined in* [22-11](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-11-electric-machines.md).

<a id="spaced-repetition"></a>**Spaced repetition** — A review method, often implemented in flashcard software such as Anki, that schedules each item at expanding intervals just before it would be forgotten. *First defined in* [00-03](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-03-how-to-study-this-curriculum.md).

<a id="spacing-effect"></a>**Spacing effect** — The finding that practice distributed over time produces more durable learning than the same practice massed together; the best gap grows with how long the material must be retained. *First defined in* [00-03](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-03-how-to-study-this-curriculum.md). *See also:* [Spaced repetition](#spaced-repetition).

<a id="span-of-control"></a>**Span of control** — The number of people reporting directly to one manager; N people need about N/(s − 1) managers in about log_s N layers for a span s. *First defined in* [26-06](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-06-team-structures-and-sizing.md).

<a id="spanning-tree"></a>**Spanning tree** — A set of n − 1 branches that connects all n nodes of a circuit without forming a loop; each remaining branch (a link) closes one independent loop, giving b − n + 1 independent KVL equations. *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md).

<a id="spare-cells"></a>**Spare cells** — Unused logic gates scattered through a layout so that later logic fixes can be made by rewiring them in the metal layers alone. *First defined in* [26-05](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-05-schedule-and-respin-risk.md).

<a id="sparse-matrix"></a>**Sparse matrix** — A matrix whose entries are almost all zero, stored and factored by keeping only the nonzeros; circuit and power-grid matrices have a few nonzeros per row. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="spatial-multiplexing"></a>**Spatial multiplexing** — Sending several independent data streams (layers) over multiple antennas in the same band and time, separated by the receiver using the channel's spatial structure; it multiplies capacity by up to min(Nt, Nr). *First defined in* [17-11](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-11-mimo-and-beamforming.md). *See also:* [MIMO capacity](#mimo-capacity), [Layer (MIMO)](#layer-mimo).

<a id="spec-cpu"></a>**SPEC CPU** — The Standard Performance Evaluation Corporation's processor benchmark suites (SPECspeed and SPECrate, integer and floating point), scored as the geometric mean of reference-time ratios, with mandatory base and optional peak results; SPEC CPU 2026 replaced SPEC CPU 2017 in 2026. *First defined in* [14-15](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-15-roofline-and-benchmarks.md). *See also:* [Benchmark](#benchmark), [Geometric mean](#geometric-mean).

<a id="specific-absorption-rate-sar"></a>**Specific absorption rate (SAR)** — RF power absorbed per kilogram of tissue (W/kg); exposure limits include 1.6 W/kg averaged over 1 g (US FCC) and 2 W/kg over 10 g (ICNIRP), so limits must be compared with their averaging mass. *First defined in* [04-08](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-08-maxwell-preview.md).

<a id="specific-contact-resistivity"></a>**Specific contact resistivity** — The resistance of a contact times its area, ρ_c in Ω·cm², which falls exponentially with √N and with barrier height; about 10⁻⁷ Ω·cm² for Hu's measured TiSi₂ contact, and much lower values are needed as contacts shrink. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md).

<a id="specific-current"></a>**Specific current** — I_spec = 2nμC_ox(W/L)V_T², the current scale of the charge-based MOSFET model, set by the device's size and the process rather than its bias; the inversion coefficient is the drain current in units of it. *First defined in* [20-01](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-01-analog-design-fundamentals-gm-id.md). *See also:* [Inversion coefficient](#inversion-coefficient).

<a id="specific-energy"></a>**Specific energy** — Stored energy per unit mass of a cell or pack, in Wh/kg; energy density is the same per unit volume, in Wh/L. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md).

<a id="specific-on-resistance"></a>**Specific on-resistance** — A power device's on-resistance multiplied by its active area (Ω·cm²), the area-independent figure for comparing technologies; Baliga's limit for a drift layer is 4V_B²/(εμE_c³). *First defined in* [09-13](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-13-compound-and-wide-bandgap-semiconductors.md).

<a id="specification-freeze"></a>**Specification freeze** — In a standards release, the point at which it stops accepting new functionality (Stage 3) and then fixes its message encoding (ASN.1); features become real only after freeze, conformance testing, certification and deployment, often years apart. In a chip program, the gate after which the architecture and block specifications are baselined and change only through change control (26-01, 26-02). *First defined in* [21-12](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-12-modem-baseband-and-standards.md). *See also:* [Peak data rate (3GPP)](#peak-data-rate-3gpp).

<a id="spectral-efficiency"></a>**Spectral efficiency** — Bit rate per hertz of occupied bandwidth; log2 M/(1 + α) b/s/Hz for M-point constellations with raised-cosine roll-off α, times the code rate; bounded by log2(1 + SNR). *First defined in* [17-06](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-06-bandpass-digital-modulation.md). *See also:* [Roll-off factor](#roll-off-factor), [Eb/N0](#eb-n0).

<a id="spectral-leakage"></a>**Spectral leakage** — The spreading of an off-bin tone's energy across all DFT bins, because a sinusoid that does not complete a whole number of cycles in the record is not orthogonal to any DFT basis vector; controlled with windows. *First defined in* [16-03](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-03-the-dft.md). *See also:* [Scalloping loss](#scalloping-loss).

<a id="spectral-line"></a>**Spectral line** — A delta function in a power spectral density, the spectral signature of a periodic or constant component (a DC mean, a carrier, or the symbol-rate lines of a PAM signal with nonzero-mean symbols); its power sits at one frequency rather than per hertz. *First defined in* [17-01](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-01-random-processes-and-psd.md). *See also:* [Power spectral density](#power-spectral-density), [Cyclostationary process](#cyclostationary-process).

<a id="spectral-theorem"></a>**Spectral theorem** — Every real symmetric matrix has real eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors, A = QΛQᵀ = Σ λᵢqᵢqᵢᵀ. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="spectre"></a>**Spectre** — A family of attacks, disclosed in January 2018, that use speculatively executed instructions to leave secret-dependent traces in caches and other microarchitectural state, read back by timing (CVE-2017-5753 and CVE-2017-5715). *First defined in* [14-07](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-07-branch-prediction-and-speculation.md). *See also:* [Side channel](#side-channel), [Speculative execution](#speculative-execution).

<a id="spectrum"></a>**Spectrum** — A signal's content as a function of frequency: lines at the harmonics for a periodic signal (Fourier series), a continuous function for an aperiodic one (Fourier transform). *First defined in* [11-06](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-06-continuous-time-fourier-transform.md).

<a id="speculative-execution"></a>**Speculative execution** — Executing instructions beyond an unresolved branch (or other prediction) before it is known that they should run, discarding their results without trace in architectural state if the prediction was wrong. *First defined in* [14-07](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-07-branch-prediction-and-speculation.md). *See also:* [Branch prediction](#branch-prediction), [Spectre](#spectre).

<a id="speed-binning"></a>**Speed binning** — Sorting tested parts into grades by the highest frequency (or lowest voltage) at which they pass, so that process variation becomes a price ladder rather than scrap. *First defined in* [25-11](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-11-test-ate-sort-burn-in.md).

<a id="speedup"></a>**Speedup** — The ratio of old to new execution time for the same work; "30% faster" means a speedup of 1.3, so the new time is 77% of the old. *First defined in* [14-01](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-01-performance-power-iron-law.md).

<a id="spherical-coverage"></a>**Spherical coverage** — A 3GPP millimetre-wave handset requirement on the EIRP reached at a given percentile of directions over the full sphere, for example 11.5 dBm at the 50th percentile in n257, which forces phones to carry several antenna modules. *First defined in* [21-10](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-10-antennas-arrays-mmwave.md). *See also:* [Total radiated power (TRP)](#total-radiated-power-trp).

<a id="spi"></a>**SPI** — Serial Peripheral Interface: a de facto synchronous, full-duplex bus with a controller-driven clock, two data lines and one chip select per target, configured by clock polarity and phase (modes 0 to 3); there is no formal standard. *First defined in* [18-05](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-05-gpio-uart-spi-i2c.md). *See also:* [I²C](#i-c).

<a id="spice"></a>**SPICE** — Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis, the standard family of circuit simulators that solve a netlist's nodal equations for DC, AC and transient behavior; ngspice is an open-source version. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md). *See also:* [Netlist](#netlist), [Modified nodal analysis](#modified-nodal-analysis).

<a id="spin-lock"></a>**Spin lock** — A lock acquired by repeatedly attempting an atomic operation until it succeeds; spinning on ordinary reads first (test-and-test-and-set) avoids flooding the interconnect with coherence traffic. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Load-reserved/store-conditional (LR/SC)](#load-reserved-store-conditional-lr-sc).

<a id="spin-transfer-torque-stt"></a>**Spin-transfer torque (STT)** — Switching a magnetic free layer with a spin-polarized current through it; the critical current scales with the thermal stability factor, so stability costs write energy. *First defined in* [23-08](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-08-emerging-memories.md). *See also:* [Thermal stability factor](#thermal-stability-factor), [Magnetic tunnel junction](#magnetic-tunnel-junction).

<a id="spiral-model"></a>**Spiral model** — Boehm's risk-driven process (1988), in which each cycle identifies the largest remaining risk, builds just enough (a prototype, model or test chip) to resolve it, and plans the next cycle. *First defined in* [26-01](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-01-requirements-and-specifications.md). *See also:* [Waterfall model](#waterfall-model).

<a id="split-rendering"></a>**Split rendering** — Rendering a headset's frames on a phone, PC or server and streaming them to the headset, which moves power and heat off the head at the cost of encoding, network and decoding latency. *First defined in* [27-04](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-04-wearables-earbuds-and-glasses.md). *See also:* [Late-stage reprojection](#late-stage-reprojection).

<a id="spontaneous-polarization"></a>**Spontaneous polarization** — The built-in electric polarization of an unstrained polar crystal such as wurtzite GaN or AlN along its c-axis; its change at a heterojunction leaves a fixed bound sheet charge. *First defined in* [09-13](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-13-compound-and-wide-bandgap-semiconductors.md).

<a id="spread-spectrum-clocking"></a>**Spread-spectrum clocking** — Varying a clock's frequency slightly over time so that each harmonic is smeared over a band, lowering the peak that narrow-band emissions measurements report; the total harmonic energy is unchanged. *First defined in* [11-05](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-05-fourier-series.md).

<a id="spreading-factor-lora"></a>**Spreading factor (LoRa)** — The number of bits per LoRa symbol, SF, from 7 to 12 in LoRaWAN; each step doubles the symbol time 2^SF/BW, roughly halving the bit rate and doubling airtime and energy, in exchange for about 2.5 dB lower required SNR. *First defined in* [27-08](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-08-edge-ai-and-iot.md). *See also:* [LoRa](#lora), [Adaptive data rate (ADR)](#adaptive-data-rate-adr).

<a id="spreading-resistance"></a>**Spreading resistance** — The extra thermal resistance incurred when heat from a small source must spread sideways into a larger body; for a uniform-flux disk of radius a on a large block it is about 0.27/(ka). *First defined in* [25-08](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-08-thermal-engineering.md). *See also:* [Hotspot](#hotspot).

<a id="spurious-response"></a>**Spurious response** — A receiver response to an input frequency other than the wanted one, wherever |m f_LO − n f_RF| equals the IF for integers m and n, caused by LO harmonics and RF-path nonlinearity; frequency planning lists them in a spur chart. *First defined in* [21-08](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-08-transceiver-architectures.md). *See also:* [Half-IF spur](#half-if-spur).

<a id="spurious-free-dynamic-range-sfdr"></a>**Spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR)** — The ratio of the fundamental to the largest other spectral component (harmonic or not), in dB. *First defined in* [16-05](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-05-spectral-analysis-and-windowing.md). *See also:* [SINAD](#sinad).

<a id="sqnr"></a>**SQNR** — Signal-to-quantization-noise ratio: signal power over the power of the rounding error; 6.02N + 1.76 dB for a full-scale sine on an N-bit quantizer, less for signals with higher crest factor once they are backed off to avoid clipping. *First defined in* [16-10](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-10-quantization-and-fixed-point.md). *See also:* [Quantization noise](#quantization-noise), [Crest factor](#crest-factor).

<a id="square-law"></a>**Square law** — The long-channel saturation current I_Dsat = (W/2mL)μC_ox(V_GS − V_TH)², with m = 1 in its simplest form; the first-order model of analog design and the basis of SPICE level 1. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="squeeze-theorem"></a>**Squeeze theorem** — If g(x) ≤ f(x) ≤ h(x) near a and g and h share the limit L, then f also tends to L. Used to prove sin θ/θ → 1. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="squirrel-cage-rotor"></a>**Squirrel-cage rotor** — An induction-machine rotor made of bars shorted by end rings, rugged and brushless; its bar resistance sets the trade between starting torque and running efficiency. *First defined in* [22-11](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-11-electric-machines.md).

<a id="sr-latch"></a>**SR latch** — A bistable built from two cross-coupled NOR (or NAND) gates with set and reset inputs; it holds when both are inactive, and both active at once is forbidden because it forces equal outputs and an unpredictable release. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md).

<a id="sram"></a>**SRAM** — Static random-access memory: each bit is held by two cross-coupled inverters (six transistors in the standard 6T cell, with two access transistors to a pair of bitlines), so it needs no refresh while powered. It is the densest memory a logic process builds, used for caches, register files and on-chip buffers. *First defined in* [19-08](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-08-sram-design.md). *See also:* [Cell ratio](#cell-ratio), [Static noise margin](#static-noise-margin), [Sense amplifier](#sense-amplifier).

<a id="sram-macro"></a>**SRAM macro** — A complete SRAM block as placed on a chip: the bitcell array plus row decoders, wordline drivers, precharge, column multiplexers, sense amplifiers, write drivers, timing and redundancy; its density is lower than the bitcell's. *First defined in* [23-02](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-02-sram-technology.md). *See also:* [Bitcell](#bitcell), [Array efficiency](#array-efficiency).

<a id="stability-of-a-circuit"></a>**Stability (of a circuit)** — The property that every bounded input gives a bounded output; for a linear circuit, every pole of its transfer functions lies in the open left half-plane. Passive RLC circuits cannot be unstable; circuits with gain can. *First defined in* [07-04](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-04-laplace-domain-circuit-analysis.md).

<a id="stability-circle"></a>**Stability circle** — The circle in the source or load reflection-coefficient plane on which a two-port's input or output reflection has unit magnitude; it separates terminations that keep the device stable from those that can make it oscillate. *First defined in* [21-01](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-01-s-parameters.md). *See also:* [Rollett stability factor](#rollett-stability-factor).

<a id="stability-triangle"></a>**Stability triangle** — The region |a₂| < 1, |a₁| < 1 + a₂ of the coefficient plane in which a second-order denominator 1 + a₁z^{−1} + a₂z^{−2} has both poles inside the unit circle; poles are complex above the parabola a₁² = 4a₂. *First defined in* [11-09](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-09-z-transform.md). *See also:* [Biquad](#biquad).

<a id="stack-data-structure"></a>**Stack (data structure)** — A last-in-first-out collection with push and pop at one end, O(1) each; used for function calls, undo histories, expression evaluation and bracket matching. *First defined in* [05-08](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-08-data-structures-and-algorithms.md).

<a id="stack-memory"></a>**Stack (memory)** — The region holding local variables and function call frames, allocated on function entry and released on return; fast but small (megabytes on desktops, kilobytes on MCUs), and a pointer to a returned function's local dangles. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="stack-effect"></a>**Stack effect** — The large reduction in leakage when two or more off transistors are in series: the intermediate node rises slightly, reverse-biasing the upper device's gate and removing most of the drain bias, and with it the DIBL, from the lower one. *First defined in* [19-06](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-06-power-and-low-power-design.md). *See also:* [Drain-induced barrier lowering](#drain-induced-barrier-lowering).

<a id="stack-frame"></a>**Stack frame** — The block of stack memory a function reserves on entry, by moving the stack pointer down, for its saved registers, return address and local data; RISC-V frames are multiples of 16 bytes. *First defined in* [14-03](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-03-assembly-and-the-compilation-stack.md).

<a id="stage-effort"></a>**Stage effort** — The effort a single gate bears, f = g h, the part of its delay proportional to its load. A path is fastest when every stage bears the same effort, about 4 in practice (3.59 for an inverter parasitic delay of 1). *First defined in* [19-04](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-04-sizing-and-logical-effort.md). *See also:* [Path effort](#path-effort), [FO4 delay](#fo4-delay).

<a id="stall"></a>**Stall** — Holding an instruction (and those behind it) in its pipeline stage for a cycle while a bubble moves ahead, to wait out a hazard. *First defined in* [14-06](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-06-pipelining-and-hazards.md). *See also:* [Bubble](#bubble).

<a id="stamp"></a>**Stamp** — The fixed pattern of matrix entries one circuit element contributes to the nodal or MNA equations; a resistor of conductance g between nodes a and b adds +g at (a, a) and (b, b) and −g at (a, b) and (b, a). *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="standard-cell"></a>**Standard cell** — A pre-drawn, characterized logic gate or flip-flop built to a library template (fixed height in routing tracks, power rails along its edges, width in whole placement sites, pins on a grid), so that tools can place and route millions of them in rows. *First defined in* [19-09](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-09-layout-and-standard-cells.md). *See also:* [Utilization](#utilization).

<a id="standard-deviation"></a>**Standard deviation** — The square root of the variance, σ, in the units of the random variable; for a signal it is the AC RMS value. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md).

<a id="standard-error"></a>**Standard error** — The standard deviation of an estimate; for the mean of n independent samples, σ/√n. *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="standard-essential-patent-sep"></a>**Standard-essential patent (SEP)** — A patent that cannot be avoided when implementing a standard; standards bodies ask its holder to commit in advance to license it on fair, reasonable and non-discriminatory terms. *First defined in* [26-02](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-02-design-reviews-and-standards.md). *See also:* [FRAND](#frand), [Royalty stacking](#royalty-stacking).

<a id="standards-development-organization"></a>**Standards development organization** — A body that develops standards under published due-process rules (for example IEEE SA, ETSI or ISO/IEC); industry bodies such as JEDEC, PCI-SIG or UCIe write specifications by and for their member companies. *First defined in* [26-02](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-02-design-reviews-and-standards.md).

<a id="standing-wave"></a>**Standing wave** — The sum of equal waves travelling in opposite directions, 2A cos(kx) cos(ωt), with fixed nodes half a wavelength apart; confined between reflectors it sets resonant modes such as f_n = nv/(2L). *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="star-ground"></a>**Star ground** — A grounding layout in which each circuit has its own return conductor to a single common point at the supply, so that no return impedance is shared between noisy and sensitive circuits. *First defined in* [06-05](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-05-mesh-analysis.md). *See also:* [Common-impedance coupling](#common-impedance-coupling).

<a id="startup-circuit"></a>**Startup circuit** — Circuitry that forces a self-biased reference or bias loop out of its zero-current operating point at power-up and then turns off; any current it leaks in normal operation becomes an error in the reference. *First defined in* [20-03](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-03-bandgap-references.md). *See also:* [Beta multiplier](#beta-multiplier), [Bandgap reference](#bandgap-reference).

<a id="startup-code"></a>**Startup code** — The code that runs from reset before main on a bare-metal system: it relies on the vector table for the initial stack pointer, copies .data from flash to SRAM, zeroes .bss, optionally configures clocks and the FPU, and calls main. *First defined in* [18-02](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-02-bare-metal-c-and-toolchain.md). *See also:* [Vector table](#vector-table), [Load and run addresses](#load-and-run-addresses).
