<a id="time-on-air"></a>**Time on air** — The duration of one radio transmission, preamble plus payload; for low-power radios it sets the transmit energy, the share of a regulatory duty cycle used and the network's capacity. *First defined in* [27-08](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-08-edge-ai-and-iot.md). *See also:* [Duty cycling](#duty-cycling), [Spreading factor (LoRa)](#spreading-factor-lora).

<a id="time-scaling"></a>**Time scaling** — Replacing x(t) by x(at); a > 1 compresses the signal and divides its energy by a, 0 < a < 1 stretches it. Combined with a shift, x(at − b) is x(at) delayed by b/a, not by b. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md).

<a id="time-bandwidth-product"></a>**Time-bandwidth product** — The product of a signal's duration and bandwidth, independent of time scaling and fixed by its shape; for RMS widths σ_t σ_ω ≥ 1/2, with equality only for the Gaussian (the uncertainty principle). *First defined in* [11-06](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-06-continuous-time-fourier-transform.md).

<a id="time-dependent-dielectric-breakdown"></a>**Time-dependent dielectric breakdown** — The wear-out of a gate dielectric under prolonged field stress, which makes the breakdown field depend on stress time (about 15 MV/cm for 1 s on 10 nm SiO₂, lower for years); lifetimes are extrapolated from accelerated tests. *First defined in* [09-08](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-08-mos-capacitor.md).

<a id="time-domain-reflectometry"></a>**Time-domain reflectometry** — (TDR.) Measuring a line's impedance profile by launching a fast step and recording the reflections at the input; the round-trip time locates each discontinuity, the reflection's height gives its impedance, and a dip's or bump's area gives a shunt capacitance or series inductance. *First defined in* [13-07](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-07-transmission-lines-time-domain.md). *See also:* [Reflection coefficient](#reflection-coefficient).

<a id="time-interleaved-adc"></a>**Time-interleaved ADC** — M identical ADCs that sample in rotation, each at f_s/M, to form one converter at f_s; offset, gain, timing and bandwidth differences between channels produce spurs at multiples of f_s/M and around them. *First defined in* [20-07](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-07-nyquist-adcs.md). *See also:* [Timing skew](#timing-skew).

<a id="time-invariant-system"></a>**Time-invariant system** — A system for which delaying the input by any t₀ only delays the output by t₀; tested by comparing "delay, then system" with "system, then delay" for every input. *First defined in* [11-02](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-02-system-properties.md). *See also:* [LTI system](#lti-system).

<a id="time-related-output-capacitance"></a>**Time-related output capacitance** — C_o(tr) = Q_oss/V, the linear capacitance with the same charge as a switch's output capacitance; it sets how long a current takes to swing the switch node. The energy-related C_o(er) = 2E_oss/V² is far smaller for superjunction parts. *First defined in* [22-06](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-06-converter-losses-and-wide-bandgap.md). *See also:* [Output charge](#output-charge).

<a id="time-to-digital-converter-tdc"></a>**Time-to-digital converter (TDC)** — A circuit that measures a time interval, such as the phase error of an all-digital PLL, as a digital word; its resolution sets an in-band phase-noise floor. *First defined in* [20-10](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-10-plls-and-jitter.md). *See also:* [All-digital PLL (ADPLL)](#all-digital-pll-adpll).

<a id="timing-arc"></a>**Timing arc** — A cause-and-effect timing relation from one pin of a cell to another (input to output, or clock to output), with its own delay tables and a unateness: negative (inverting), positive or non-unate. *First defined in* [19-10](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-10-synthesis-and-sta.md). *See also:* [Nonlinear delay model (NLDM)](#nonlinear-delay-model-nldm).

<a id="timing-closure"></a>**Timing closure** — The iterative process of changing RTL, constraints, tool options or placement until every timing path in a design meets its constraints with non-negative slack. *First defined in* [08-12](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-12-fpga-implementation-flow.md). *See also:* [Timing constraint](#timing-constraint), [Slack](#slack).

<a id="timing-constraint"></a>**Timing constraint** — A statement to the implementation tools of a design's timing requirements, such as clock periods, I/O delays, and false or multicycle paths; the tools check only what the constraints describe. *First defined in* [08-12](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-12-fpga-implementation-flow.md). *See also:* [Timing closure](#timing-closure).

<a id="timing-skew"></a>**Timing skew** — In a time-interleaved ADC, the difference between a channel's actual and ideal sampling instant; for two channels it produces an image at f_s/2 − f_in with relative power (π f_in Δt)². *First defined in* [20-07](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-07-nyquist-adcs.md). *See also:* [Time-interleaved ADC](#time-interleaved-adc).

<a id="tinyml"></a>**TinyML** — Machine-learning inference on microcontroller-class devices at milliwatt and lower power, with models of tens to hundreds of kilobytes; benchmarked by MLPerf Tiny in microjoules per inference. *First defined in* [27-08](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-08-edge-ai-and-iot.md). *See also:* [Quantization (neural networks)](#quantization-neural-networks), [Depthwise-separable convolution](#depthwise-separable-convolution).

<a id="tlb-reach"></a>**TLB reach** — The amount of memory a TLB can map without missing, equal to its number of entries times the page size. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Huge page](#huge-page).

<a id="toeplitz-matrix"></a>**Toeplitz matrix** — A matrix whose entries are constant along every diagonal; writing a convolution as y = Hx gives a Toeplitz H, which lets convolution be computed with matrix-multiplication hardware and libraries. *First defined in* [11-03](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-03-convolution.md).

<a id="tolerance"></a>**Tolerance** — For a component, the maximum allowed deviation of its value from nominal when made, such as ±5% (950 to 1050 Ω for 1 kΩ); temperature drift and ageing come on top. *First defined in* [06-02](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-02-circuit-elements-and-ohms-law.md). *See also:* [Worst-case analysis](#worst-case-analysis).

<a id="tolerance-band-voltage-regulator"></a>**Tolerance band (voltage regulator)** — The allowed spread around a regulator's load line that covers setpoint error, current-sense error and ripple, for example ±22 mV. *First defined in* [22-10](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-10-datacenter-power-delivery.md).

<a id="tops-w"></a>**TOPS/W** — Tera-operations per second per watt, equal to operations per picojoule (a MAC counts as two); meaningful only with its precision, utilization and measurement boundary (macro, chip, card or system). *First defined in* [23-09](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-09-compute-in-memory.md). *See also:* [Utilization (accelerator)](#utilization-accelerator).

<a id="torque"></a>**Torque** — The turning effect of a force, τ = rF⊥ (N·m); for rotation it plays the role of force, and mechanical power is P = τω. *First defined in* [04-01](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-01-mechanics-essentials.md).

<a id="torque-constant"></a>**Torque constant** — The ratio K_t of a DC motor's torque to its current (N·m/A); by energy conservation it equals the back-EMF constant K_e (V·s/rad) in SI units. *First defined in* [15-01](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-01-modeling-dynamic-systems.md). *See also:* [Back-EMF](#back-emf).

<a id="total-addressable-market-tam"></a>**Total addressable market (TAM)** — The total revenue opportunity for a product if it won every possible customer; credible only when rebuilt bottom-up from units, attach rates and prices. *First defined in* [00-01](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-01-map-of-electrical-engineering.md).

<a id="total-cost-of-ownership-tco"></a>**Total cost of ownership (TCO)** — All costs of using equipment over its service life, including purchase, its share of shared infrastructure, energy and operation, usually divided by the useful work delivered. *First defined in* [26-04](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-04-engineering-economics-2.md).

<a id="total-differential"></a>**Total differential** — df = (∂f/∂x)dx + (∂f/∂y)dy + …, the linear approximation of a change in f from small changes in all its inputs; the basis of small-signal models and tolerance analysis. *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="total-harmonic-distortion-thd"></a>**Total harmonic distortion (THD)** — The RMS of all harmonics above the fundamental divided by the fundamental's amplitude; a ±1 square wave has THD of 48 %. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="total-internal-reflection"></a>**Total internal reflection** — Complete reflection of light going from higher to lower index at angles beyond the critical angle sin θ_c = n₂/n₁; it guides light in optical fibers and silicon waveguides. *First defined in* [04-09](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-09-waves-and-optics.md).

<a id="total-probability-theorem"></a>**Total probability theorem** — For events B1, …, Bm that partition the sample space, P(A) = Σ P(Bi) P(A | Bi), a weighted average over the cases. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="total-processing-performance-tpp"></a>**Total processing performance (TPP)** — The US export-control metric for advanced chips, 2 × MacTOPS × bit length of the operation, aggregated over all processing units; performance density is TPP per mm² of die. *First defined in* [26-07](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-07-engineering-ethics.md).

<a id="total-radiated-power-trp"></a>**Total radiated power (TRP)** — The power a device radiates integrated over all directions, measured in an anechoic chamber; 3GPP caps a handheld millimetre-wave phone at 23 dBm TRP while allowing 43 dBm EIRP. *First defined in* [21-10](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-10-antennas-arrays-mmwave.md). *See also:* [EIRP](#eirp), [Spherical coverage](#spherical-coverage).

<a id="total-store-ordering-tso"></a>**Total store ordering (TSO)** — A memory model, like that of x86, in which each core's stores pass through a FIFO store buffer, so a later load may overtake an earlier store to a different address while stores stay in order. *First defined in* [14-12](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-12-multicore-coherence-consistency.md). *See also:* [Store buffer](#store-buffer), [Memory consistency model](#memory-consistency-model).

<a id="total-unadjusted-error-tue"></a>**Total unadjusted error (TUE)** — The worst-case static error of an uncalibrated ADC reading, combining offset, gain error and nonlinearity (and often the reference), in LSB; the honest figure for an absolute measurement. *First defined in* [18-06](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-06-adc-dac-pwm.md). *See also:* [Integral nonlinearity (INL)](#integral-nonlinearity-inl).

<a id="totem-pole-pfc"></a>**Totem-pole PFC** — A bridgeless power-factor-correction boost whose fast leg is a half bridge of switches; in continuous conduction it hard-commutates reverse conduction every cycle, which is practical only with SiC or GaN switches. *First defined in* [22-06](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-06-converter-losses-and-wide-bandgap.md).

<a id="trace"></a>**Trace** — The sum of a square matrix's diagonal entries, equal to the sum of its eigenvalues. *First defined in* [02-08](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-08-eigenvalues-and-eigenvectors.md).

<a id="trace-buffer"></a>**Trace buffer** — An on-chip memory that records selected internal signals every cycle around a programmable trigger; its window is only depth divided by clock frequency, so signal selection and triggering decide what can be seen. *First defined in* [25-12](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-12-post-silicon-validation.md). *See also:* [Scan dump](#scan-dump).

<a id="traceability"></a>**Traceability** — Two-way links from each requirement to the design elements that implement it and the tests that verify it, exposing untested requirements and orphan code or tests; mandatory in safety standards. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="traceability-matrix"></a>**Traceability matrix** — A table linking requirements (rows) to the design elements or tests (columns) that implement or verify them; it yields coverage, childless requirements and orphan tests, and supports impact analysis when a requirement changes. *First defined in* [26-01](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-01-requirements-and-specifications.md). *See also:* [Traceability](#traceability).

<a id="traceback"></a>**Traceback** — The report Python prints when an exception is not handled, listing the chain of calls that led to the error and ending with the failing line and the exception message; read it from the bottom up. *First defined in* [05-01](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-01-python-fundamentals.md).

<a id="trade-secret"></a>**Trade secret** — Information that derives economic value from not being generally known and that its owner takes reasonable measures to keep secret, such as process recipes, test limits or design methods. *First defined in* [26-07](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-07-engineering-ethics.md).

<a id="trans-inductor-voltage-regulator"></a>**Trans-inductor voltage regulator** — The TLVR, a multiphase buck in which each phase's inductor has a secondary winding and all secondaries form one series loop, so a transient on any phase drives every phase's current at once. *First defined in* [22-05](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-05-magnetics-design.md). *See also:* [Coupled inductor](#coupled-inductor).

<a id="transaction-layer-packet-tlp"></a>**Transaction-layer packet (TLP)** — The PCIe unit that carries a memory read or write, a completion, a configuration access or a message, made of a 12- or 16-byte header and an optional payload; framing and link CRC add more bytes, so small payloads use the link inefficiently. *First defined in* [24-05](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-05-pcie-cxl-ethernet.md). *See also:* [PCI Express (PCIe)](#pci-express-pcie), [Flit](#flit).

<a id="transconductance"></a>**Transconductance** — g_m = ∂I_out/∂V_in, the change in a device's output current per unit change of its controlling voltage; for a square-law MOSFET g_m = 2I_D/(V_GS − V_TH). *First defined in* [01-09](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-09-multivariable-calculus-1.md).

<a id="transconductance-amplifier"></a>**Transconductance amplifier** — An amplifier that senses a voltage and delivers a current, characterized by its short-circuit transconductance G_m (S); ideally both R_i and R_o are infinite. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md).

<a id="transconductance-efficiency"></a>**Transconductance efficiency** — The ratio g_m/I_D, the transconductance obtained per unit of bias current; 2/V_ov for a MOSFET in strong inversion, at most 1/(mV_T) in weak inversion, and 1/V_T for a bipolar transistor. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="transfer-function"></a>**Transfer function** — H(s) = Y(s)/X(s), the ratio of output to input transforms of a linear time-invariant system with zero initial conditions; it equals the transform of the impulse response, and H(jω) is the frequency response. *First defined in* [02-05](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-05-laplace-transform-for-odes.md). *See also:* [Poles and zeros](#poles-and-zeros), [Impulse response](#impulse-response).

<a id="transfer-ratio"></a>**Transfer ratio** — C_s/(C_s + C_BL), the fraction of a DRAM cell's voltage difference from the precharge level that appears on the bitline after charge sharing; typically about 1/5 to 1/10. *First defined in* [23-03](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-03-dram-cells-arrays-refresh.md). *See also:* [Charge sharing](#charge-sharing).

<a id="transformer"></a>**Transformer** — Windings sharing a magnetic flux; ideally v₂/v₁ = N₂/N₁, i₂/i₁ = N₁/N₂ and impedances scale by (N₁/N₂)². It needs changing flux and provides galvanic isolation. *First defined in* [04-07](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-07-faraday-lenz-and-inductance.md).

<a id="transient"></a>**Transient** — The part of a circuit's response that dies out after a disturbance (such as a switching event), as the circuit moves from one steady state to another. *First defined in* [07-02](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-02-first-order-rc-rl-transients.md). *See also:* [Time constant](#time-constant).

<a id="transient-analysis"></a>**Transient analysis** — A simulation of a circuit's voltages and currents versus time for arbitrary input waveforms, computed step by step with numerical integration. *First defined in* [00-04](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-04-toolchain-walkthrough.md).

<a id="transimpedance-amplifier"></a>**Transimpedance amplifier** — A current-to-voltage converter, v_out = −R_f i_in, formed by feeding a current into an op-amp's virtual ground; it presents zero input resistance, and large R_f makes bias current a significant error. *First defined in* [06-10](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-10-ideal-op-amp.md). *See also:* [Input bias current](#input-bias-current).

<a id="transistor-stacking"></a>**Transistor stacking** — Placing N switch transistors in series so each sees 1/N of the RF voltage; it multiplies R_on by N and divides C_off by N, and widening each transistor N times restores R_on at N² times the area. *First defined in* [21-09](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-09-rf-front-end.md). *See also:* [Switch figure of merit (Ron·Coff)](#switch-figure-of-merit-ron-coff).

<a id="transit-frequency"></a>**Transit frequency** — f_T = g_m/(2πC_gg), the frequency at which a transistor's small-signal current gain falls to one; it rises with inversion level and falls with channel length, as 1/L² for long channels and 1/L when the carriers are velocity-saturated. *First defined in* [20-01](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-01-analog-design-fundamentals-gm-id.md). *See also:* [Cutoff frequency](#cutoff-frequency), [Velocity saturation](#velocity-saturation).

<a id="transition-band"></a>**Transition band** — The frequency range between a filter's passband and stopband; in a windowed FIR design its width shrinks in proportion to 1/N, while the ripple is set by the window's shape. *First defined in* [11-07](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-07-discrete-time-fourier-transform.md).

<a id="transition-fault"></a>**Transition fault** — A delay-fault model in which a node is slow to rise or slow to fall; detecting it needs two patterns, one to set the initial value and one to launch the transition, captured at functional speed. *First defined in* [19-12](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-12-design-for-test.md). *See also:* [Stuck-at fault](#stuck-at-fault), [Scan chain](#scan-chain).

<a id="translation-lookaside-buffer-tlb"></a>**Translation lookaside buffer (TLB)** — A small cache of recent virtual-to-physical page translations and their permissions, consulted on every memory access; a miss triggers a page-table walk. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [TLB reach](#tlb-reach), [Page table](#page-table).

<a id="translation-unit"></a>**Translation unit** — One C source file after preprocessing (with its included headers pasted in), compiled on its own into an object file. *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md).

<a id="transmission-coefficient"></a>**Transmission coefficient** — The ratio τ of the transmitted to the incident electric field at an interface; 1 + Γ = 2η₂/(η₁ + η₂) at normal incidence. The transmitted power fraction is (η₁/η₂)|τ|², not |τ|². *First defined in* [13-06](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-06-reflection-and-transmission.md). *See also:* [Reflection coefficient](#reflection-coefficient).

<a id="transmission-gate"></a>**Transmission gate** — An nMOS and a pMOS transistor in parallel, driven by complementary control signals, that pass a signal in either direction without a threshold drop when on; the basic switch of CMOS latches and multiplexers. *First defined in* [08-06](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-06-latches-and-flip-flops.md).

<a id="transmission-line"></a>**Transmission line** — A pair of conductors along which signals travel as waves with finite speed, so that voltage and current vary with position and reflections occur at impedance changes. *First defined in* [00-02](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-02-the-abstraction-stack.md). *See also:* [Characteristic impedance](#characteristic-impedance), [Reflection coefficient](#reflection-coefficient).

<a id="transpose"></a>**Transpose** — Aᵀ, the matrix with rows and columns exchanged, (Aᵀ)ᵢⱼ = aⱼᵢ. The transpose of a product reverses the order, (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ; a matrix equal to its transpose is symmetric. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md).

<a id="transposed-form"></a>**Transposed form** — The structure obtained from a signal-flow graph by reversing every branch, swapping input and output and exchanging adders with branch points; it has the same transfer function, and for an FIR filter it shortens the critical path to one multiplier and one adder. *First defined in* [16-08](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-08-filter-structures.md). *See also:* [Signal-flow graph](#signal-flow-graph), [Critical path](#critical-path).

<a id="transresistance-amplifier"></a>**Transresistance amplifier** — An amplifier that senses a current and delivers a voltage, characterized by its open-circuit transresistance R_m (Ω); ideally both R_i and R_o are zero. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Transimpedance amplifier](#transimpedance-amplifier).

<a id="trap"></a>**Trap** — A localized electron state in the band gap, from an impurity or crystal defect, that captures and emits carriers; deep (near mid-gap) traps act as recombination and generation centers. *First defined in* [09-04](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-04-generation-recombination-continuity.md).

<a id="trap-processor"></a>**Trap (processor)** — A transfer of control to a more privileged handler caused by an exception, a system call (ecall) or an interrupt; the hardware saves the PC and cause, and an xRET instruction returns. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Precise exception](#precise-exception), [Privilege mode](#privilege-mode), [Page fault](#page-fault).

<a id="trapezoidal-ringing"></a>**Trapezoidal ringing** — A numerical artifact of the trapezoidal rule, whose amplification factor tends to −1 for very fast modes, so stiff components flip sign every step instead of decaying; it is damped by Gear methods or by mixing in backward Euler. *First defined in* [02-10](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-10-numerical-methods.md).

<a id="trapezoidal-rule"></a>**Trapezoidal rule** — Numerical integration joining samples with straight lines; its error falls as the square of the step. SPICE's default transient integration method. *First defined in* [01-05](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-05-integrals.md).

<a id="tree-covering"></a>**Tree covering** — A technology-mapping method: write the logic and every library cell as trees of two-input NANDs and inverters, then choose, by dynamic programming from the leaves up, the set of cell patterns that covers the tree at least total area or delay. Optimal for trees; logic with fanout is split into trees first. *First defined in* [19-10](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-10-synthesis-and-sta.md). *See also:* [Technology mapping](#technology-mapping).

<a id="trellis"></a>**Trellis** — The state diagram of a convolutional encoder unrolled in time; every coded sequence is a path through it, and the Viterbi algorithm searches it for the best path. *First defined in* [17-08](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-08-channel-coding.md). *See also:* [Viterbi algorithm](#viterbi-algorithm), [Convolutional code](#convolutional-code).

<a id="triangular-distribution"></a>**Triangular distribution** — A probability distribution defined by a minimum, most-likely and maximum value, with mean (a + m + b)/3; a simple model of skewed task-duration risk. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).

<a id="trigonometric-substitution"></a>**Trigonometric substitution** — Replacing x by a sin θ, a tan θ or a sec θ so that a Pythagorean identity collapses √(a² − x²), a² + x² or √(x² − a²); the reference triangle converts the answer back to x. *First defined in* [01-06](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-06-techniques-of-integration.md).

<a id="trim"></a>**TRIM** — A host command telling an SSD which logical blocks no longer hold useful data, so garbage collection need not copy them; it raises the effective over-provisioning. *First defined in* [23-07](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-07-ssd-controllers.md). *See also:* [Garbage collection (SSD)](#garbage-collection-ssd).

<a id="trimming"></a>**Trimming** — Adjusting a circuit once at production test (with fuses, one-time-programmable memory or laser-cut resistors) to remove an offset or gain error measured at one condition. *First defined in* [20-11](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-11-layout-matching-pvt.md).

<a id="triple-modular-redundancy-tmr"></a>**Triple modular redundancy (TMR)** — Running three copies of a module with a majority voter, giving reliability 3R² − 2R³, better than one module only when R > 0.5. *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md).

<a id="triplen-harmonics"></a>**Triplen harmonics** — Harmonics of order 3, 6, 9, …; in a three-phase system they are in phase in all three lines, so they add in the neutral (three times the per-phase value) instead of cancelling. *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md). *See also:* [Neutral current](#neutral-current), [Total harmonic distortion (THD)](#total-harmonic-distortion-thd).

<a id="tristate-buffer"></a>**Tristate buffer** — A buffer whose output is either driven to the input value or disconnected (high impedance, Z), so that several drivers can share one wire as long as exactly one is enabled. *First defined in* [08-04](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-04-combinational-building-blocks.md).

<a id="true-dependence"></a>**True dependence** — A read-after-write (RAW) dependence, in which a later instruction needs the value an earlier one produces; it carries data and cannot be removed, only waited for. *First defined in* [14-08](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-08-out-of-order-and-superscalar.md). *See also:* [Name dependence](#name-dependence), [Data hazard](#data-hazard).

<a id="true-rms-meter"></a>**True-RMS meter** — A meter that computes the square root of the mean square of the signal, reading correctly for any waveform within its bandwidth and crest-factor limits, unlike average-responding meters calibrated for sines. *First defined in* [01-07](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-07-applications-of-integration.md). *See also:* [RMS value](#rms-value), [Form factor](#form-factor).

<a id="true-time-delay"></a>**True-time delay** — Steering an array with real delays rather than phase shifts, so the beam points the same way at every frequency; it needs delay spans of many carrier periods, costly in analog hardware and natural in digital beamforming. *First defined in* [21-10](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-10-antennas-arrays-mmwave.md). *See also:* [Beam squint](#beam-squint).

<a id="trustzone-m"></a>**TrustZone-M** — Arm's security extension for Armv8-M cores: every address and execution state is Secure or Non-secure (set by the SAU and IDAU), and Non-secure code may enter Secure code only through secure-gateway (SG) instructions in Non-Secure Callable memory. *First defined in* [18-11](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-11-hardware-security.md). *See also:* [Root of trust](#root-of-trust).

<a id="truth-table"></a>**Truth table** — A list of a function's output for every combination of its n inputs, 2^n rows; read as a binary number (row i's output as bit i) it is the integer that programs an FPGA lookup table. *First defined in* [08-02](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-02-boolean-algebra-and-gates.md).

<a id="tsv-keep-out-zone"></a>**TSV keep-out zone** — The area around a TSV where no transistors may sit, because the copper's thermal-expansion mismatch strains the silicon and shifts device characteristics; with tens of thousands of TSVs it costs several percent of a die. *First defined in* [23-05](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-05-hbm-in-depth.md). *See also:* [Through-silicon via (TSV)](#through-silicon-via-tsv).

<a id="tunnel-magnetoresistance-tmr"></a>**Tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR)** — The resistance contrast of a magnetic tunnel junction, (R_AP − R_P)/R_P; MRAM reads it as a current difference, diluted by the access transistor's series resistance. *First defined in* [23-08](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-08-emerging-memories.md). *See also:* [Magnetic tunnel junction](#magnetic-tunnel-junction).

<a id="tunneling-breakdown"></a>**Tunneling breakdown** — Reverse breakdown of a junction heavily doped on both sides, in which electrons tunnel from the valence band to the conduction band across a gap of E_g/qE; it occurs at fields near 10⁶ V/cm in silicon, at low voltages, and its voltage falls with temperature. *First defined in* [09-06](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-06-pn-junction-iv-and-capacitance.md).

<a id="turbo-power-limit"></a>**Turbo power limit** — A short-term power limit above the sustained limit that a processor may draw until an exponentially weighted average of its power reaches the sustained limit; the burst lasts tau times ln((P2 - P0)/(P2 - P1)). *First defined in* [27-05](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-05-pc-soc.md). *See also:* [Sustained power](#sustained-power).

<a id="turns-ratio"></a>**Turns ratio** — N1:N2, the ratio of primary to secondary turns of a transformer; it sets the voltage ratio (directly), the current ratio (inversely) and the impedance ratio (squared). *First defined in* [07-09](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-09-mutual-inductance-and-transformers.md).

<a id="tustin-transformation"></a>**Tustin transformation** — The control engineer's name for the bilinear transform used to discretize a controller, s ← (2/T)(z − 1)/(z + 1); it keeps stable controllers stable and preserves gain and phase values but warps the frequencies at which they occur. *First defined in* [15-11](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-11-digital-control.md). *See also:* [Bilinear transform](#bilinear-transform), [Frequency prewarping](#frequency-prewarping).

<a id="twiddle-factor"></a>**Twiddle factor** — A root of unity W_N^k = e^{−j2πk/N} by which an FFT butterfly multiplies one of its inputs; W = 1 and W = −j need no multiplier, and the radix-2 FFT has (N/2)log₂N − 3N/2 + 2 non-trivial twiddle products. *First defined in* [16-04](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-04-the-fft.md). *See also:* [Butterfly](#butterfly).

<a id="twos-complement"></a>**Two's complement** — The standard binary representation of signed integers, in which an n-bit pattern with top bit set represents its unsigned value minus 2^n; range −2^(n−1) to 2^(n−1) − 1. Mandatory in C23. *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md).

<a id="two-bit-saturating-counter"></a>**Two-bit saturating counter** — A predictor entry with four states, predicting taken in the upper two; it needs two consecutive wrong outcomes to change its prediction, so a loop branch is mispredicted only at the exit. *First defined in* [14-07](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-07-branch-prediction-and-speculation.md).

<a id="two-dimensional-channel-material"></a>**Two-dimensional channel material** — An atomically thin semiconductor, such as a transition-metal dichalcogenide, proposed as a transistor channel for its ultimate thinness; the IRDS judges it not yet mature for manufacturing. *First defined in* [09-12](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-12-finfet-gaa-cfet-backside-power.md).

<a id="two-dimensional-electron-gas"></a>**Two-dimensional electron gas** — A sheet of electrons confined in a thin quantum well at a heterojunction (2DEG), free to move along the interface; the channel of a HEMT, with densities of order 10¹³ cm⁻² in AlGaN/GaN. *First defined in* [09-13](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-13-compound-and-wide-bandgap-semiconductors.md).

<a id="two-load-method"></a>**Two-load method** — Finding a source's Thévenin equivalent from its terminal voltage with two known loads, using 1/v = 1/V_th + (R_th/V_th)(1/R_L); a meter's input resistance is part of each load. *First defined in* [06-08](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-08-thevenin-and-norton.md). *See also:* [Thevenin equivalent](#thevenin-equivalent).

<a id="two-port-loading-method"></a>**Two-port loading method** — The classical way to analyse a feedback amplifier by absorbing the feedback network's loading into the amplifier (its input-port resistance with the other port shorted for shunt or opened for series connections) and then applying A/(1 + Aβ); it neglects forward transmission through the network and reverse transmission through the amplifier. *First defined in* [12-05](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-05-feedback-topologies.md). *See also:* [Return ratio](#return-ratio), [Feedback topology](#feedback-topology).

<a id="two-port-network"></a>**Two-port network** — A linear network with two terminal pairs (ports), each carrying equal and opposite currents, described by a 2 × 2 matrix relating its port voltages and currents at each frequency (z, y, h, ABCD or S parameters). *First defined in* [07-10](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-10-two-port-networks.md).

<a id="two-stage-op-amp"></a>**Two-stage op-amp** — The standard CMOS operational amplifier, a differential pair with a current-mirror load followed by a common-source second stage, Miller-compensated by a capacitor across the second stage; gain g_m1R_1·g_m6R_2 and gain-bandwidth product g_m1/(2πC_c). *First defined in* [12-08](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-08-op-amp-internals.md). *See also:* [Miller compensation](#miller-compensation), [Slew rate](#slew-rate), [Folded cascode](#folded-cascode).

<a id="two-wattmeter-method"></a>**Two-wattmeter method** — Measuring the total power of any three-wire system with two wattmeters whose current coils are in two lines and whose voltage coils return to the third; for a balanced load the readings also give Q = √3 (W2 − W1). *First defined in* [07-11](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-11-three-phase-circuits.md).

<a id="two-way-ranging"></a>**Two-way ranging** — Measuring distance by a timed message exchange between two devices with independent clocks; single-sided ranging suffers an error of half the reply time times the clock difference, which double-sided ranging cancels, leaving about the distance times the mean clock offset. *First defined in* [21-12](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-12-modem-baseband-and-standards.md). *See also:* [Phase-based ranging](#phase-based-ranging).

<a id="type-i-and-type-ii-errors"></a>**Type I and type II errors** — Rejecting a true null hypothesis (false alarm, probability α) and failing to reject a false one (missed detection, probability β). *First defined in* [03-05](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-05-estimation-and-hypothesis-testing.md).

<a id="type-iii-compensator"></a>**Type III compensator** — A switching-regulator compensator with an integrator, two zeros and two poles, ω_I(1 + s/ω_z)²/[s(1 + s/ω_p)²]; the zeros near the output LC resonance supply up to 180° of phase lead and the poles above crossover filter switching noise. *First defined in* [15-09](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-09-lead-lag-compensation.md). *See also:* [Lead compensator](#lead-compensator).

<a id="type-ii-compensator"></a>**Type-II compensator** — An integrator with one zero and one pole, giving up to 90° of phase boost; used when the plant is first-order near crossover, as in current-mode control. *First defined in* [22-07](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-07-converter-dynamics-and-control.md). *See also:* [Type III compensator](#type-iii-compensator).

<a id="letter-u"></a>

## U

<a id="ualink"></a>**UALink** — Ultra Accelerator Link, an open accelerator-to-accelerator scale-up interconnect; its 200G 1.0 specification (April 2025) runs 200 Gb/s per connection on 212.5 Gb/s electrical lanes for pods of up to 1,024 accelerators. *First defined in* [24-05](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-05-pcie-cxl-ethernet.md). *See also:* [Ultra Ethernet](#ultra-ethernet).

<a id="uart"></a>**UART** — Universal asynchronous receiver-transmitter: a serial port that sends characters framed by a start bit and stop bits at an agreed baud rate with no shared clock, so the receiver must tolerate the mismatch between the two ends' clocks. *First defined in* [18-05](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-05-gpio-uart-spi-i2c.md). *See also:* [Baud rate](#baud-rate).

<a id="ucie"></a>**UCIe** — Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express, the die-to-die standard (1.0 in 2022; 3.0 in August 2025 at up to 64 GT/s) with standard-package (UCIe-S), advanced-package (UCIe-A) and hybrid-bonded (UCIe-3D) classes and energy targets of 0.5, 0.25 and under 0.05 pJ/b. *First defined in* [24-06](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-06-d2d-memory-phys-scale-up.md). *See also:* [Die-to-die interface](#die-to-die-interface), [Chiplet](#chiplet).

<a id="udp"></a>**UDP** — A minimal transport protocol (8-byte header: ports, length, checksum) with no reliability or congestion control, used for real-time media and simple queries. *First defined in* [17-13](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-13-computer-networks-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [TCP](#tcp).

<a id="ultimate-gain"></a>**Ultimate gain** — The proportional gain K_u at which a loop sits on its stability boundary and oscillates steadily, with the ultimate period P_u; found by Routh, by experiment, or by relay feedback, and used by tuning rules. *First defined in* [15-08](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-08-pid-control.md). *See also:* [Ziegler–Nichols tuning](#ziegler-nichols-tuning), [Routh–Hurwitz criterion](#routh-hurwitz-criterion).

<a id="ultra-ethernet"></a>**Ultra Ethernet** — The Ultra Ethernet Consortium's Ethernet-based stack for AI and HPC (specification 1.0, June 2025; 1.1, October 2026): standard Ethernet PHYs with new RDMA transport, congestion control and optional credit-based flow control and link-level retry. *First defined in* [24-05](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-05-pcie-cxl-ethernet.md). *See also:* [UALink](#ualink), [Link-level retry](#link-level-retry).

<a id="ultra-thin-body-transistor"></a>**Ultra-thin-body transistor** — A MOSFET built in a silicon film only a few nanometers thick on an insulator (UTB SOI); the thin body replaces the depletion and junction depths in the characteristic length, so short channels need no heavy doping. *First defined in* [09-12](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-12-finfet-gaa-cfet-backside-power.md).

<a id="uncertainty-principle"></a>**Uncertainty principle** — Heisenberg's limit Δx·Δp ≥ ħ/2 on how sharply position and momentum can both be defined; confinement to a small region forces a momentum spread and hence a minimum kinetic energy. *First defined in* [04-10](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-10-intro-quantum-mechanics.md).

<a id="uncorrectable-bit-error-rate-uber"></a>**Uncorrectable bit error rate (UBER)** — Wrong bits delivered to the host per bit read after error correction; for a k-bit codeword correcting t errors it is about (t + 1)P_fail/k, with JEDEC targets of 1e-15 (client) and 1e-16 (enterprise). *First defined in* [23-07](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-07-ssd-controllers.md). *See also:* [Write amplification factor (WAF)](#write-amplification-factor-waf).

<a id="uncorrectable-codeword-ratio"></a>**Uncorrectable codeword ratio** — The fraction of codewords with more wrong symbols than the code can correct; for independent errors, the binomial tail P(N > t). *First defined in* [03-04](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-04-joint-distributions-and-clt.md).

<a id="undefined-behavior"></a>**Undefined behavior** — In C, an operation (signed overflow, reading an uninitialized variable, out-of-bounds access, oversized shift) on which the standard imposes no requirements; compilers may assume it never happens, so results can be silently wrong. *First defined in* [05-05](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-05-c-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Sanitizer](#sanitizer).

<a id="underdamped"></a>**Underdamped** — A second-order system with ζ < 1, whose complex characteristic roots −α ± jω_d give a sinusoidal response inside a decaying envelope. *First defined in* [02-03](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-03-second-order-linear-odes.md).

<a id="underfill"></a>**Underfill** — An epoxy filled between a flip-chip die and its substrate after reflow; it bonds die to substrate so thermal-mismatch strain is shared by the whole interface rather than concentrated in the solder joints. *First defined in* [25-06](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-06-packaging-fundamentals.md).

<a id="unified-memory"></a>**Unified memory** — A single DRAM pool shared by a SoC's CPU, GPU and NPU behind one memory controller, so data need not be copied between separate memories and large models can use most of the system's capacity. *First defined in* [27-05](../courses/27-system-architectures/chapters/27-05-pc-soc.md). *See also:* [Memory on package](#memory-on-package).

<a id="uniform-plane-wave"></a>**Uniform plane wave** — An electromagnetic wave whose fields are uniform over planes perpendicular to its direction of travel, with E, H and the direction mutually perpendicular and E/H equal to the medium's intrinsic impedance; the far-field model of every radiated wave. *First defined in* [13-05](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-05-plane-waves.md). *See also:* [Intrinsic impedance](#intrinsic-impedance), [Helmholtz equation](#helmholtz-equation).

<a id="unilateral-amplifier"></a>**Unilateral amplifier** — An amplifier with no reverse transmission (y_12 = 0), so its input resistance does not depend on its load; a single stage without a feedback element is approximately unilateral. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Two-port network](#two-port-network).

<a id="uninterruptible-power-supply-ups"></a>**Uninterruptible power supply (UPS)** — Equipment that keeps critical loads powered through utility disturbances, typically by rectifying the grid to charge batteries and inverting back to AC (double conversion), at a few percent of loss. *First defined in* [22-10](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-10-datacenter-power-delivery.md).

<a id="union-bound"></a>**Union bound** — The inequality P(A1 ∪ … ∪ An) ≤ P(A1) + … + P(An), valid for any events: the probability that anything goes wrong is at most the sum of the individual probabilities; tight for rare, nearly disjoint events. In detection, a symbol's error probability is at most the sum of Q(d/√(2N0)) over the other points (17-05). *First defined in* [03-01](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-01-probability-in-ee-language.md). *See also:* [Inclusion–exclusion principle](#inclusion-exclusion-principle), [Q-function](#q-function).

<a id="uniqueness-theorem"></a>**Uniqueness theorem** — Poisson's equation with the potential (or the normal field) given on every boundary has only one solution, so any function satisfying the equation and the boundary conditions, however found, is the solution. *First defined in* [13-02](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-02-electrostatics-boundary-value-problems.md). *See also:* [Laplace's equation](#laplaces-equation), [Method of images](#method-of-images).

<a id="unit-circle"></a>**Unit circle** — |z| = 1 in the z-plane, where z = e^{jω} and the system function becomes the frequency response; DC is z = 1, f_s/4 is z = j and half the sample rate is z = −1. A causal system is stable exactly when all its poles lie inside it. *First defined in* [11-09](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-09-z-transform.md).

<a id="unit-impulse"></a>**Unit impulse** — δ(t), the idealized pulse of zero width and unit area (a generalized function); ∫ δ(t) f(t) dt = f(0), its transform is 1, and it models a sudden kick such as a charge dumped onto a capacitor. *First defined in* [02-05](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-05-laplace-transform-for-odes.md). *See also:* [Unit step function](#unit-step-function), [Impulse response](#impulse-response).

<a id="unit-in-the-last-place-ulp"></a>**Unit in the last place (ulp)** — The gap between a floating-point number and the next representable number of the same binade; for FP32 values in [1, 2) it is 2⁻²³. *First defined in* [14-04](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-04-computer-arithmetic-and-number-formats.md). *See also:* [Unit roundoff](#unit-roundoff).

<a id="unit-roundoff"></a>**Unit roundoff** — u = ε/2, the largest relative error of rounding one real number to the nearest floating-point number; 2⁻⁵³ ≈ 1.1×10⁻¹⁶ in double precision, so each basic operation satisfies fl(x∘y) = (x∘y)(1 + δ) with |δ| ≤ u. *First defined in* [02-10](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-10-numerical-methods.md). *See also:* [Machine epsilon](#machine-epsilon).

<a id="unit-sample"></a>**Unit sample** — δ[n], equal to 1 at n = 0 and 0 elsewhere; the discrete-time impulse, an ordinary sequence with δ[n] = u[n] − u[n − 1], from which every sequence is built as x[n] = Σ x[k] δ[n − k]. *First defined in* [11-01](../courses/11-signals-and-systems/chapters/11-01-signals-classification-and-operations.md). *See also:* [Unit impulse](#unit-impulse).

<a id="unit-step-function"></a>**Unit step function** — u(t), equal to 0 for t < 0 and 1 for t ≥ 0; it models a switch closing at t = 0 and has a jump discontinuity there. *First defined in* [01-02](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-02-limits-and-continuity.md).

<a id="unit-test"></a>**Unit test** — A small automated check that runs one function or module on chosen inputs and asserts the result (a hand-worked case, a symmetry, a bound or an expected error); pytest is the standard Python runner. *First defined in* [05-04](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-04-reproducible-workflows.md). *See also:* [Regression test](#regression-test), [Self-checking testbench](#self-checking-testbench).

<a id="unit-output-method"></a>**Unit-output method** — For a single-source circuit, assume an output of 1 (volt or ampere), work backwards to the source value this requires, then scale by homogeneity; well suited to ladders. *First defined in* [06-07](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-07-linearity-and-superposition.md). *See also:* [Homogeneity](#homogeneity).

<a id="unity-gain-point"></a>**Unity-gain point** — An input voltage at which an inverter's transfer curve has slope −1; V_IL (below the switching threshold) and V_IH (above it) bound the inputs a gate reads reliably and define its noise margins. *First defined in* [19-01](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-01-cmos-inverter-static.md). *See also:* [Noise margin](#noise-margin), [Switching threshold](#switching-threshold).

<a id="unity-gain-stable"></a>**Unity-gain stable** — Said of an op-amp whose compensation keeps it stable with 100% feedback (a buffer), the case of largest loop gain; a decompensated op-amp trades this for a higher gain-bandwidth product and a minimum stable closed-loop gain. *First defined in* [12-06](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-06-stability-and-compensation.md). *See also:* [Dominant-pole compensation](#dominant-pole-compensation), [Phase margin](#phase-margin).

<a id="universal-mobility"></a>**Universal mobility** — The observation that silicon MOSFET surface mobilities fall on one curve against the effective vertical field; Hu fits electrons with 540/[1 + (E_eff/0.9 MV/cm)^1.85] cm²/V·s. *First defined in* [09-09](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-09-long-channel-mosfet.md).

<a id="universal-verification-methodology-uvm"></a>**Universal Verification Methodology (UVM)** — IEEE 1800.2: a SystemVerilog class library and methodology for building reusable testbenches from sequences, sequencers, drivers, monitors, agents, scoreboards and environments, configured by a factory and a configuration database. *First defined in* [19-13](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-13-verification-methods.md). *See also:* [Testbench](#testbench), [Scoreboard](#scoreboard).

<a id="upfront-licence-fee"></a>**Upfront licence fee** — The fixed amount an IP licensee pays when a licence is signed, separate from the royalties paid as units ship. *First defined in* [26-04](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-04-engineering-economics-2.md). *See also:* [Royalty](#royalty).

<a id="uplink-limited-coverage"></a>**Uplink-limited coverage** — The usual state of cellular networks, in which the phone's far lower transmit power makes the uplink close at a shorter range than the downlink, so the cell edge is where the phone can no longer be heard; balanced with receive diversity, narrow uplink allocations and higher power classes. *First defined in* [21-11](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-11-link-budgets.md). *See also:* [Link budget](#link-budget), [Noise rise](#noise-rise).

<a id="usable-capacity"></a>**Usable capacity** — The charge a cell actually delivers before its terminal voltage reaches the cutoff at a given current and temperature; less than rated capacity whenever IR drop moves the cutoff to a higher SOC. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md). *See also:* [Cutoff voltage](#cutoff-voltage).

<a id="usage-profile"></a>**Usage profile** — The list of states a device spends its day in, each with an output power, a converter efficiency at that load and a duration; the sum of power × time / efficiency over the states, plus the standing quiescent draw, gives the daily energy and the battery life. *First defined in* [22-08](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-08-pmics.md). *See also:* [Quiescent current](#quiescent-current).

<a id="use-after-free"></a>**Use after free** — Accessing heap memory after it has been freed (or moved by realloc), through a dangling pointer; the memory may already belong to something else, so results are silently wrong or exploitable. *First defined in* [05-06](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-06-c-pointers-and-memory.md).

<a id="utf-8"></a>**UTF-8** — The variable-length encoding of Unicode code points in 1 to 4 bytes, identical to ASCII for U+0000 to U+007F; continuation bytes start with 10, so a receiver can find character boundaries from any point in a stream. *First defined in* [08-01](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-01-number-systems-and-codes.md).

<a id="utilization"></a>**Utilization** — The fraction of a device's resources (logic cells, block RAMs, DSP blocks, I/O) that a design uses, as reported after synthesis or placement; in ASIC physical design, total standard-cell area divided by core area. High utilization makes routing harder. *First defined in* [08-12](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-12-fpga-implementation-flow.md).

<a id="utilization-accelerator"></a>**Utilization (accelerator)** — The fraction of an accelerator's processing elements doing useful work on a given model; delivered throughput is peak operations per element × elements × utilization, so peak TOPS overstates real performance. *First defined in* [23-09](../courses/23-memory-and-storage-technology/chapters/23-09-compute-in-memory.md). *See also:* [TOPS/W](#tops-w).

<a id="letter-v"></a>

## V

<a id="v-model"></a>**V-model** — A development process in which each level of specification (requirements, architecture, module design) is paired with a matching level of verification (system, integration, unit tests); the backbone of automotive and avionics processes. *First defined in* [05-09](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-09-software-engineering-practices.md).

<a id="v-number"></a>**V-number** — The normalized frequency of a step-index fibre, V = (2πa/λ)·NA; the fibre is single-mode when V < 2.405, the first zero of the Bessel function J₀. *First defined in* [13-10](../courses/13-electromagnetics/chapters/13-10-waveguides-and-resonators.md). *See also:* [Numerical aperture](#numerical-aperture), [Mode field diameter](#mode-field-diameter).

<a id="vacuum-level"></a>**Vacuum level** — The energy of an electron at rest just outside a material, the reference from which electron affinity and work function are measured on a band diagram. *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md).

<a id="vacuum-permeability"></a>**Vacuum permeability** — The constant µ₀ = 1.25663706127 × 10⁻⁶ N/A² (CODATA 2022), measured since the 2019 SI redefinition and within a part in 10⁹ of 4π × 10⁻⁷. *First defined in* [04-06](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-06-magnetic-fields-and-forces.md).

<a id="vacuum-permittivity"></a>**Vacuum permittivity** — The constant ε₀ = 8.854 × 10⁻¹² F/m that sets the strength of electric forces in vacuum (k_e = 1/(4πε₀) ≈ 8.988 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²); measured, not exact, since the 2019 SI redefinition. *First defined in* [04-02](../courses/04-physics-for-ee/chapters/04-02-charge-coulomb-and-electric-fields.md).

<a id="valid-ready-handshake"></a>**Valid/ready handshake** — The flow-control rule of AXI and similar interfaces: the sender asserts VALID with the data, the receiver asserts READY when it can accept, and a transfer happens on each clock edge where both are high; a sender may not wait for READY before asserting VALID. *First defined in* [14-11](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-11-io-buses-and-interconnect.md). *See also:* [AXI](#axi).

<a id="validation-of-a-product"></a>**Validation (of a product)** — Showing that a product accomplishes its intended purpose for its users and stakeholders; it answers "did we build the right product?", which a product can fail even when it passes verification. *First defined in* [26-01](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-01-requirements-and-specifications.md). *See also:* [Verification (of a product)](#verification-of-a-product).

<a id="value-of-flexibility"></a>**Value of flexibility** — How much less a plan that waits to choose until uncertainty resolves is expected to cost than the same first-stage choice committed for both generations; never negative when keeping the choice is free. *First defined in* [26-04](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-04-engineering-economics-2.md). *See also:* [Real option](#real-option).

<a id="vapor-chamber"></a>**Vapor chamber** — A flat sealed chamber with a wick and a small charge of working fluid that spreads heat by evaporation at the hot area and condensation elsewhere, with an effective conductivity far above solid copper's. *First defined in* [25-08](../courses/25-fabrication-packaging-test-and-reliability/chapters/25-08-thermal-engineering.md). *See also:* [Spreading resistance](#spreading-resistance).

<a id="varactor"></a>**Varactor** — A capacitor whose value varies with its DC bias (a reverse-biased junction or a MOS capacitor), used for continuous fine tuning of a VCO; its Q falls as its tuning ratio rises. *First defined in* [21-06](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-06-oscillators-and-vcos.md). *See also:* [Switched-capacitor bank](#switched-capacitor-bank), [VCO gain (KVCO)](#vco-gain-kvco).

<a id="variable-frequency-drive-vfd"></a>**Variable-frequency drive (VFD)** — A rectifier, DC link and PWM inverter that supply an AC motor at adjustable frequency and voltage, giving speed control, soft starting and energy savings on fans and pumps. *First defined in* [22-11](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-11-electric-machines.md). *See also:* [Volts-per-hertz control](#volts-per-hertz-control), [Affinity laws](#affinity-laws).

<a id="variance"></a>**Variance** — The expected squared deviation from the mean, Var(X) = E[(X − μ)²] = E[X²] − μ²; for a zero-mean voltage in 1 Ω it is the AC power. *First defined in* [03-03](../courses/03-probability-statistics-and-random-variables/chapters/03-03-expectation-and-functions-of-rvs.md). *See also:* [Standard deviation](#standard-deviation).

<a id="variation-of-parameters"></a>**Variation of parameters** — A general method for particular solutions of linear ODEs, y_p = u₁y₁ + u₂y₂ with u₁′ = −y₂g/W and u₂′ = y₁g/W (W the Wronskian); it works for any continuous input. *First defined in* [02-04](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-04-forced-response-and-resonance.md). *See also:* [Wronskian](#wronskian).

<a id="vbe-multiplier"></a>**VBE multiplier** — A transistor with a resistor divider across its collector–base and base–emitter junctions that produces V_BE(1 + R1/R2); used to bias class AB output stages, and mounted on their heat sink so the bias falls as they heat. *First defined in* [12-07](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-07-output-stages.md). *See also:* [Class-AB amplifier](#class-ab-amplifier), [Thermal runaway](#thermal-runaway).

<a id="vccs"></a>**VCCS** — Voltage-controlled current source, i = g v_x, with transconductance g in siemens; SPICE element G. The core of a MOSFET's small-signal model. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [Dependent source](#dependent-source), [Transconductance](#transconductance).

<a id="vco-gain-kvco"></a>**VCO gain (KVCO)** — The slope of a VCO's frequency against its control voltage, in Hz/V or rad/s per volt; for the same varactor it scales as C_tot^(−3/2), and noise on the control line causes phase noise K²S_v/(2Δf²). *First defined in* [21-06](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-06-oscillators-and-vcos.md). *See also:* [Voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO)](#voltage-controlled-oscillator-vco), [Varactor](#varactor).

<a id="vcsel"></a>**VCSEL** — A vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser, whose cavity is formed by distributed Bragg reflector stacks above and below the active layer so that it emits from the wafer surface. *First defined in* [09-14](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-14-optoelectronic-devices.md).

<a id="vcvs"></a>**VCVS** — Voltage-controlled voltage source, v = μ v_x, with dimensionless voltage gain μ; SPICE element E. The first-order model of an op-amp. *First defined in* [06-06](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-06-dependent-sources.md). *See also:* [Dependent source](#dependent-source).

<a id="vector"></a>**Vector** — An ordered list of n numbers, written as a column; pictured as an arrow in space, a set of related quantities (such as node voltages), or a sampled signal. *First defined in* [02-06](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-06-vectors-matrices-and-linear-systems.md). *See also:* [Linear combination](#linear-combination), [Dot product](#dot-product).

<a id="vector-field"></a>**Vector field** — A rule that assigns a vector to every point in space, such as an electric field E(x, y, z) or a current density J. *First defined in* [01-10](../courses/01-calculus-for-engineers/chapters/01-10-multivariable-calculus-2.md).

<a id="vector-network-analyzer"></a>**Vector network analyzer** — An instrument that measures S-parameters in magnitude and phase by separating incident and reflected waves at each port with directional couplers and detecting them coherently; its systematic errors are removed by calibration. *First defined in* [21-01](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-01-s-parameters.md). *See also:* [S-parameters](#s-parameters), [De-embedding](#de-embedding).

<a id="vector-space"></a>**Vector space** — A set closed under addition and scalar multiplication obeying the usual algebra rules, such as Rⁿ, polynomials, or the solutions of a homogeneous linear ODE. *First defined in* [02-07](../courses/02-complex-numbers-des-and-linear-algebra/chapters/02-07-determinants-inverses-and-vector-spaces.md). *See also:* [Subspace](#subspace), [Basis](#basis).

<a id="vector-table"></a>**Vector table** — The table of addresses a processor reads on reset and on exceptions; on Cortex-M its first word is the initial main stack pointer, its second the reset handler, then one entry per exception and interrupt. *First defined in* [18-01](../courses/18-embedded-systems-and-microcontrollers/chapters/18-01-microcontroller-architecture.md). *See also:* [Memory map](#memory-map).

<a id="vectorization"></a>**Vectorization** — Writing a computation as operations on whole arrays so compiled library code does the looping, typically 10 to 100 times faster than an element-by-element Python loop. *First defined in* [05-02](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-02-numpy-and-vectorization.md).

<a id="vegards-law"></a>**Vegard's law** — The rule that an alloy's lattice constant varies linearly with composition between those of its end members, a(x) = (1 − x)a_A + x a_B; band gaps usually deviate from linearity (bowing). *First defined in* [09-01](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-01-crystals-and-energy-bands.md).

<a id="velocity-overshoot"></a>**Velocity overshoot** — Carrier velocities above the saturation velocity in channels so short that carriers cross before they can lose their energy to optical phonons; it relaxes the velocity-saturation limit in very short transistors. *First defined in* [09-10](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-10-short-channel-effects-and-leakage.md).

<a id="velocity-saturation"></a>**Velocity saturation** — The levelling-off of carrier drift velocity at high fields (above about 10⁴ V/cm in silicon) near 10⁷ cm/s, because hot carriers lose energy by emitting optical phonons; it limits the current of short transistors. *First defined in* [09-03](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-03-drift-and-diffusion.md). *See also:* [Optical phonon](#optical-phonon), [Ballistic transport](#ballistic-transport).

<a id="velocity-form-pi"></a>**Velocity-form PI** — A discrete PI controller written as an update of its output, u_k = u_{k−1} + b₀e_k + b₁e_{k−1}; clamping u_k at the actuator limit stops integral accumulation without a separate integrator state, and it switches bumplessly from manual to automatic. *First defined in* [15-11](../courses/15-control-systems/chapters/15-11-digital-control.md). *See also:* [Integrator windup](#integrator-windup).

<a id="verification-of-a-product"></a>**Verification (of a product)** — Proof that a product complies with its specification, by test, analysis, inspection or demonstration; it answers "did we build the product right?" *First defined in* [26-01](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-01-requirements-and-specifications.md). *See also:* [Validation (of a product)](#validation-of-a-product), [Verification methods (TAID)](#verification-methods-taid).

<a id="verification-methods-taid"></a>**Verification methods (TAID)** — Test (measured data from the product), analysis (modelling and simulation), inspection (visual examination of the product or its records) and demonstration (showing the capability in use without detailed data), as defined in the NASA Systems Engineering Handbook. *First defined in* [26-01](../courses/26-engineering-design-and-professional-practice/chapters/26-01-requirements-and-specifications.md). *See also:* [Verification (of a product)](#verification-of-a-product).

<a id="verification-plan"></a>**Verification plan** — The list of every feature in a chip's specification together with how each will be checked (scoreboard, assertion, formal proof, software test) and how its exercise will be measured (coverage items); the yardstick for verification signoff. *First defined in* [19-13](../courses/19-digital-vlsi-design/chapters/19-13-verification-methods.md). *See also:* [Design verification](#design-verification), [Coverage closure](#coverage-closure).

<a id="verilog"></a>**Verilog** — A hardware description language created in 1984 and standardized as IEEE 1364 (1995, 2001, 2005); since 2009 it is formally part of SystemVerilog (IEEE 1800). *First defined in* [08-05](../courses/08-digital-logic-design/chapters/08-05-verilog-and-testbenches.md). *See also:* [SystemVerilog](#systemverilog), [Hardware description language (HDL)](#hardware-description-language-hdl).

<a id="version-control"></a>**Version control** — Recording every saved state of a project's files with author, date and reason, so changes can be compared, attributed and undone; git is the standard tool. *First defined in* [05-04](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-04-reproducible-workflows.md). *See also:* [Commit](#commit).

<a id="vertical-power-delivery"></a>**Vertical power delivery** — Placing voltage-regulator power stages and inductors directly beneath a processor, on the other side of the board, so the high current flows a few millimetres vertically instead of centimetres laterally. *First defined in* [22-10](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-10-datacenter-power-delivery.md).

<a id="vestigial-sideband"></a>**Vestigial sideband** — Modulation that keeps one sideband and a shaped remnant of the other, so that messages with energy down to DC can be filtered without an infinitely sharp edge at the carrier; the analog-television standard. *First defined in* [17-03](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-03-analog-modulation.md). *See also:* [Single-sideband modulation](#single-sideband-modulation).

<a id="via-stub"></a>**Via stub** — The unused part of a via barrel beyond the layer where the signal leaves it: an open-ended transmission line that notches the channel at the quarter-wave frequency c/(4ℓ√εr). *First defined in* [24-01](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-01-signal-integrity-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Back-drilling](#back-drilling).

<a id="view-numpy"></a>**View (NumPy)** — An array that shares memory with another, as produced by basic slicing, reshaping and transposing; writing through a view changes the original, unlike a copy. *First defined in* [05-02](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-02-numpy-and-vectorization.md).

<a id="virtual-array"></a>**Virtual array** — The set of positions formed by every transmitter–receiver pair of a MIMO radar, at the sums of their positions; N_TX transmitters and N_RX receivers can emulate a filled array of N_TX N_RX elements. *First defined in* [21-10](../courses/21-rf-and-microwave-engineering/chapters/21-10-antennas-arrays-mmwave.md). *See also:* [Grating lobe](#grating-lobe).

<a id="virtual-environment"></a>**Virtual environment** — A per-project folder holding a Python interpreter and its own installed packages, so library versions can be pinned per project (created with python -m venv and filled from requirements.txt). *First defined in* [05-01](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-01-python-fundamentals.md).

<a id="virtual-memory"></a>**Virtual memory** — The mechanism, shared by hardware and operating system, that gives each process its own address space by translating virtual addresses to physical ones page by page, providing isolation, protection, relocation and demand paging. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Page table](#page-table), [Translation lookaside buffer (TLB)](#translation-lookaside-buffer-tlb).

<a id="virtual-short"></a>**Virtual short** — The ideal op-amp rule v+ = v− (with no input current), valid only while negative feedback is active and the output is inside its range; with the + input grounded it makes the − input a virtual ground. *First defined in* [06-10](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-10-ideal-op-amp.md). *See also:* [Operational amplifier](#operational-amplifier), [Negative feedback](#negative-feedback).

<a id="virtually-indexed-physically-tagged-vipt-cache"></a>**Virtually indexed, physically tagged (VIPT) cache** — A cache whose set index comes from untranslated page-offset bits, so it can be read in parallel with the TLB lookup and then compared against the physical tag; it requires size divided by associativity to be at most the page size. *First defined in* [14-10](../courses/14-computer-organization-and-architecture/chapters/14-10-virtual-memory.md). *See also:* [Translation lookaside buffer (TLB)](#translation-lookaside-buffer-tlb), [Set-associative cache](#set-associative-cache).

<a id="viterbi-algorithm"></a>**Viterbi algorithm** — Maximum-likelihood sequence decoding by dynamic programming over a trellis, keeping one survivor path per state with add-compare-select steps; cost 2^(K−1) operations per bit instead of exponential in message length. *First defined in* [17-08](../courses/17-communication-systems/chapters/17-08-channel-coding.md). *See also:* [Trellis](#trellis), [Free distance](#free-distance).

<a id="vliw"></a>**VLIW** — Very long instruction word; an architecture that issues several independent operations per cycle in one wide instruction scheduled by the compiler, the classic organization of DSP cores. *First defined in* [16-11](../courses/16-digital-signal-processing/chapters/16-11-dsp-hardware-architectures.md). *See also:* [SIMD](#simd).

<a id="volatile"></a>**Volatile** — A C type qualifier telling the compiler that every read and write of an object has effects it cannot see (hardware registers, variables shared with interrupts), so none may be removed, merged or reordered; it does not make operations atomic. *First defined in* [05-07](../courses/05-programming-for-engineers/chapters/05-07-bit-manipulation.md).

<a id="volt-second-balance"></a>**Volt-second balance** — In a periodic steady state the average voltage across an inductor is zero (and the average current into a capacitor, charge balance), because its current (voltage) returns to the same value each period; the starting point for analyzing switching converters. *First defined in* [07-01](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-01-capacitors-and-inductors.md). *See also:* [Inductance](#inductance).

<a id="voltage"></a>**Voltage** — The energy per unit charge gained in moving from one point to another (1 V = 1 J/C); it is always defined between two points, written v_AB = v_A − v_B. *First defined in* [06-01](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-01-charge-current-voltage-power.md). *See also:* [Reference node (ground)](#reference-node-ground), [Passive sign convention](#passive-sign-convention).

<a id="voltage-amplifier"></a>**Voltage amplifier** — An amplifier that senses an input voltage and delivers an output voltage, modeled by its open-circuit voltage gain A_vo, input resistance R_i and output resistance R_o; ideally R_i → ∞ and R_o → 0. *First defined in* [10-05](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-05-amplifier-fundamentals.md). *See also:* [Unilateral amplifier](#unilateral-amplifier).

<a id="voltage-divider"></a>**Voltage divider** — Series resistors sharing a voltage in proportion to their resistances, v_k = v R_k/ΣR; for two, v_out = v_in R2/(R1 + R2). *First defined in* [06-03](../courses/06-circuit-analysis-1-dc/chapters/06-03-kirchhoffs-laws.md). *See also:* [Loading effect](#loading-effect).

<a id="voltage-doubler"></a>**Voltage doubler** — A clamp followed by a peak rectifier, giving a DC output near twice the input's peak minus two diode drops; cascading stages multiplies further. *First defined in* [10-01](../courses/10-electronics-1/chapters/10-01-diodes-and-diode-circuits.md).

<a id="voltage-identification-vid"></a>**Voltage identification (VID)** — A digital code a processor sends to its voltage regulator to set the regulator's target voltage, changed in small steps at a specified slew rate during DVFS. *First defined in* [22-10](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-10-datacenter-power-delivery.md). *See also:* [Load line (voltage regulator)](#load-line-voltage-regulator).

<a id="voltage-regulation"></a>**Voltage regulation** — The fractional change in a transformer's (or supply's) output voltage from no load to full load, about I(R_eq cos θ + X_eq sin θ)/V_rated for a lagging load. *First defined in* [07-09](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-09-mutual-inductance-and-transformers.md).

<a id="voltage-relaxation-battery"></a>**Voltage relaxation (battery)** — The slow recovery of a cell's terminal voltage toward its open-circuit voltage after the current stops, as the RC (diffusion) polarization decays; gauges must wait for it before reading OCV. *First defined in* [22-09](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-09-batteries-charging-fuel-gauging.md).

<a id="voltage-standing-wave-ratio-vswr"></a>**Voltage standing-wave ratio (VSWR)** — (1 + |Γ|)/(1 − |Γ|), the ratio of the largest to the smallest voltage amplitude along a line feeding a mismatched load; for a resistive load it equals the ratio of the larger to the smaller resistance. *First defined in* [07-10](../courses/07-circuit-analysis-2-transient-and-ac/chapters/07-10-two-port-networks.md). *See also:* [Return loss](#return-loss), [Mismatch loss](#mismatch-loss).

<a id="voltage-transfer-characteristic"></a>**Voltage transfer characteristic** — The plot of a logic gate's static output voltage against its input voltage (VTC); its steep middle region and flat rails give noise margins and regeneration. *First defined in* [09-11](../courses/09-semiconductor-devices/chapters/09-11-cmos-and-scaling.md).

<a id="voltage-controlled-oscillator"></a>**Voltage-controlled oscillator** — An oscillator whose frequency is tuned by a control voltage, typically through a varactor in an LC tank or the bias of a ring oscillator's stages; the controlled element of a phase-locked loop. *First defined in* [12-09](../courses/12-electronics-2/chapters/12-09-oscillators.md). *See also:* [Ring oscillator](#ring-oscillator), [Negative resistance](#negative-resistance).

<a id="voltage-controlled-oscillator-vco"></a>**Voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO)** — An oscillator whose frequency varies with a control voltage, ω = ω_free + K_VCO·V (K_VCO in rad/s per volt); in a PLL's phase-domain model it is an integrator, because phase is the integral of frequency. *First defined in* [20-10](../courses/20-analog-and-mixed-signal-ic-design/chapters/20-10-plls-and-jitter.md). *See also:* [Phase-locked loop (PLL)](#phase-locked-loop-pll), [Phase noise](#phase-noise).

<a id="voltage-mode-control"></a>**Voltage-mode control** — Regulation in which an error amplifier's output is compared with a fixed sawtooth to set the duty cycle, so the loop includes the power stage's LC resonance. *First defined in* [22-07](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-07-converter-dynamics-and-control.md). *See also:* [Peak current-mode control](#peak-current-mode-control).

<a id="voltage-mode-driver"></a>**Voltage-mode driver** — A transmitter (also source-series-terminated, SST) that switches each output to a supply or ground through a 50 Ω on-resistance; it delivers the same swing as a CML driver for a quarter of the supply power. *First defined in* [24-03](../courses/24-high-speed-io-signal-integrity-and-photonics/chapters/24-03-serdes-architecture.md). *See also:* [Current-mode logic (CML)](#current-mode-logic-cml).

<a id="volts-per-hertz-control"></a>**Volts-per-hertz control** — Scalar drive control that keeps V/f constant to hold the motor's flux, with a voltage boost at low speed to offset the stator resistance drop. *First defined in* [22-11](../courses/22-power-electronics-and-energy-conversion/chapters/22-11-electric-machines.md).

<a id="letter-w"></a>

## W

<a id="wafer-cycle-time"></a>**Wafer cycle time** — The time a wafer spends in the fab from start to finish, roughly 1–1.5 days per mask layer and 14–20 weeks for advanced processes. *First defined in* [00-05](../courses/00-orientation/chapters/00-05-how-chip-companies-are-organized.md).
